items.title: hdUE user guide
items.text:
hdUE (HdUnrealEngine) is a Hydra render delegate that renders OpenUSD with Unreal Engine 5.8 inside the host process: the Houdini Solaris viewport, husk and the USD Render ROP, Live Render, usdview, or a standalone host. It renders with Lumen (Realtime) or UE's Path Tracer, from the same USD and render settings as Karma.

Amazon Lumberyard Bistro (NVIDIA ORCA, CC BY 4.0) rendered by hdUE with MaterialX surfaces: inside at night, and the street outside in the rain. Drag to compare Realtime (Lumen) with UE's Path Tracer.

hdUE follows Unreal Engine and Movie Render Queue: a setting means what it means in UE, with UE's name, range and default, and a scene renders as it would in UE's editor. Where hdUE departs from a UE default, the page says so.

items.title: Architecture and runtime anatomy
items.text:
This page describes what hdUE adds to a process, on which threads it runs and how one frame travels from Hydra to UE and back, so that each part can be checked in Process Explorer or a debugger. Statements come from the code (file names are given) or from live observation of husk and Houdini 22.0.368 on Windows 11 with an RTX 4090 and a 16-core Ryzen 9 5950X (October 2026, Cornell box). Anything that was not observed or read in the code is marked inferred.

items.title: Processes
items.text:
hdUE runs entirely inside the host process. UE is linked into a DLL (UELibrary, unreal/HdUEBackend/Source/HdUEBackend.Target.cs: LinkType = Monolithic, bShouldCompileAsDLL = true, UE_LIBRARY_ENABLED=1), so there is no UE executable, editor or window.

Host Executable Who starts UE Solaris viewport houdini.exe (and the other GUI names in houdiniUi(), src/hydra/delegate.cpp: houdinifx.exe, houdinicore.exe, hindie.exe, ...) The first hdUE delegate, once the Python host (hdue_houdini.py) has started because a Scene Viewer selected hdUE husk, USD Render ROP husk.exe (the ROP launches it as a child of Houdini) The first hdUE delegate hython hython.exe The first hdUE delegate (hython is not in the GUI list, so it gets the husk behaviour) usdview python.exe running scripts/usdview_hdue.py The Python host itself (scripts/hdue_runtime.py, Runtime(start=True))

Child processes. During rendering hdUE starts none. A 10-frame Path Tracer and a 60-frame realtime husk render were polled every 500 ms for children: there were none. A Houdini session with hdUE in the viewport had one child, conhost.exe (Houdini's console). No ShaderCompileWorker runs: the runtime is a cooked game whose shaders come from ShaderArchive-*.ushaderbytecode in the staged Content folder, and the staged Engine\Binaries holds only ThirdParty (no ShaderCompileWorker.exe, CrashReportClient.exe or UnrealTraceServer.exe; UE logs "The Unreal Trace Server binary is not available").

The only child process hdUE can start is the background material preparation (Substrate Builder graphs, and MaterialX graphs the render-time translation cannot express; docs/substrate-builder.md, docs/materials.md), in Houdini's UI and in husk: when a material needs a prepared asset, scripts/live_materials.py starts pwsh (or powershell) with scripts/Prepare-LiveMaterials.ps1 (CREATE_NO_WINDOW, environment stripped of HOUDINI_*, PXR_*, QT_*, HDUE_RUNTIME_CONFIG, ...). That script runs standalone USD Python (Run-UsdPython.ps1) to write the job's graphs, one UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe for the HdUESubstrate commandlet (UE's MaterialX import, the Builder compile, then UE's cook), and the publish step. Its PID is written to runtime-state.json (material_preparation.worker_pid).

items.title: Modules
items.text:
Lists from (Get-Process -Id <pid>).Modules on a running husk render and on a Houdini session with hdUE in the viewport, filtered to what is not part of Houdini or Windows, plus the shared libraries whose origin matters.

Module Path in the observed process Loaded by hdUE_Houdini22.dll <build>\Release\ (installed: the package's folder) USD's PlugRegistry. The package appends the folder holding plugInfo.json to PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME; its LibraryPath is the DLL, its types are HdUnrealEngine and two scene index plugins. Hydra loads it when hdUE is selected or named by --renderer. In Houdini's UI the Python host also opens it with ctypes from Plug.Registry().GetPluginForType(...).path (hdue_houdini.py, hdue_viewport.py) for its hdue_* exports: the same file, so the same module. HdUEBackend-h22-<hash>.dll <runtime>\HdUEBackend\Binaries\Win64\ hdue::Backend (src/client/backend.cpp): LoadLibraryExW(absolute path, LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR \| LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_DIRS), never FreeLibrary. The path is backend_dll from the JSON file named by HDUE_RUNTIME_CONFIG (relative paths resolve against that file), unless the backendLibrary render setting or HDUE_BACKEND_DLL names one. In Houdini's UI the Python host also loads it with ctypes.CDLL(..., winmode=0x1100) (the same flags) to read status. embree4.dll the backend's folder Preloaded by the backend's Initialize (Bridge.cpp) before UELibrary_InitW, from the backend DLL's own folder: NaniteBuilder and the Lumen card builder delay-load it by name, and the executable's folder is the host's. tbb12.dll, tbbmalloc.dll Houdini's bin (the copies beside the backend are not loaded) Windows loads a DLL name once per process. tbbmalloc.dll is a static import of the backend and tbb12.dll an import of hdUE_Houdini22.dll; Houdini has both loaded already. Initialize skips its tbb12 preload when one is loaded and logs the one in use (observed: hdUE: tbb12 interface version 12150 from <Houdini>\bin\tbb12.dll, at Log verbosity, in the UE log file only). Embree therefore runs on Houdini's TBB; scripts/check_shared_dlls.py fails the package when a staged DLL imports a symbol Houdini's copy of the same name does not export. D3D12Core.dll %SystemRoot%\System32 The OS D3D12 runtime. The backend exports D3D12SDKVersion and D3D12SDKPath (UE's UnrealAgilitySDKLink.inl, compiled in by the engine's AgilitySDK module, with no target setting to turn it off), but neither husk.exe nor houdini.exe/houdinifx.exe exports them (checked with dumpbin /exports), and D3D12 reads them from the executable only (inferred from Microsoft's Agility SDK rules). UE's "DirectX Agility SDK runtime found." only checks that some D3D12Core.dll is loaded (WindowsD3D12Device.cpp). The Agility SDK copy UE stages (Binaries\Win64\D3D12\x64) is therefore dead weight: Stage-Runtime.ps1 deletes it and Package-Houdini.ps1 leaves it out. WinPixEventRuntime.dll, GFSDK_Aftermath_Lib.x64.dll, dbghelp.dll <runtime>\Engine\Binaries\ThirdParty\... Delay-load imports of the backend, resolved by UE (the log names the PIX one: "Loading WinPixEventRuntime.dll for PIX profiling"). ispc_texcomp.dll <runtime>\Engine\Binaries\ThirdParty\Intel\ISPCTexComp\Win64-Release\ Delay-loaded by Scene.cpp the first time a runtime texture is block-compressed. Not loaded for the untextured Cornell box. OpenColorIO_sidefx.dll, OpenImageIO_sidefx.dll, openvdb_sesi.dll Houdini's bin Imports of hdUE_Houdini22.dll (dumpbin /dependents): colour management, texture reads and VDB fields use Houdini's libraries. d3d12.dll, dxgi.dll, nvwgf2umx.dll, nvapi64.dll, ... Windows and the NVIDIA driver UE's D3D12 RHI. nvoglv64.dll (GL) is Houdini's viewport.

Why the hashed backend name. Update-HoudiniRuntime.ps1 copies the built HdUEBackend.dll to HdUEBackend-h22-<first 16 hex digits of its SHA-256>.dll beside it and writes that path into runtime-houdini.json. A running Houdini keeps its backend loaded until it exits (it is never freed), so a fixed name could not be replaced while Houdini runs, and a profile always names the exact binary it was made for (inferred from the script; the script itself states no reason). Several hashed copies accumulate in the folder; only the one in the profile is loaded.

Paths UE sees. Initialize starts UE with "<runtime_project>" /Game/HdUETest -game -windowed -d3d12 -unattended -nosplash -nosound -NoLoadingScreen -NoSplash -ResX=640 -ResY=360 plus Backend::boot's -RenderOffscreen, HDUE_UE_ARGS and -userdir="<HDUE_USER_DIR>" when set (HDUE_SHOW_WINDOW=1 drops -RenderOffscreen). UE's base directory is the backend's folder (LogInit: Base Directory: ...\HdUEBackend\Binaries\Win64/), and UE changes the process's working directory to it; the delegate restores the host's working directory after every tick (HdUESelfHost::tick), which husk needs for relative output paths.

items.title: Threads
items.text: Observed with a script that lists each thread's GetThreadDescription (UE names its threads with SetThreadDescription, WindowsPlatformProcess.cpp), its start address (NtQueryInformationThread(ThreadQuerySetWin32StartAddress)) mapped to a module, and its CPU time: the same columns as Process Explorer's Threads tab. hdUE itself names no thread.

items.title: Who owns UE
items.text:
The backend accepts calls only from the thread that called initialize (Bridge.cpp, CheckOwner: HDUE_WRONG_THREAD otherwise; get_status, poll_frame, copy_frame, copy_depth, acquire_gpu_frame and AOV copies are readable from any thread). That thread is UE's game thread. Because it is not the thread that ran the DLL's static initialization, the target defines IS_RUNNING_GAMETHREAD_ON_EXTERNAL_THREAD=1.

In husk, hython and Houdini's UI, the owner is an std::thread that the first delegate creates (startSelfHost, HdUESelfHost::worker in delegate.cpp). It creates a hidden HdUESelfHost window (passed to UE as its window), loads the backend, calls Backend::boot and then serves a queue:

  • run(f) queues f and waits for its result; post(f) queues it without waiting. On the worker itself both run inline.
  • When the queue is empty, it ticks (PeekMessageW dispatch, api().tick(), restore the working directory). In Houdini's UI it ticks continuously, waiting at most 2 ms for work while any viewport delegate is not paused, and after each tick runs the render passes' "pumps", which publish finished frames without waiting for Houdini to call Execute. Under husk it only runs queued work; ticks happen inside Execute.

In Process Explorer this thread is GameThread with a start address in ucrtbase.dll (the CRT thread entry of std::thread), not in the backend. In the Houdini session it was thread 7436 while Houdini's UI thread (start address houdini.exe, unnamed) was 48420, the owner the Python host recorded in runtime-state.json; GameThread CPU time grew while the viewport rendered. The Python host (hdue_houdini.py) never ticks UE: its 16 ms QTimer (250 ms while no Scene Viewer renders with hdUE and no walk is pending) does housekeeping (materials, op: textures, asset overrides, status) and it attaches with Runtime(start=False). Its stage walks are cooperative jobs (scripts/cooperative.py): generators that yield between prims, which the timer advances for at most 8 ms (material preparation) and 4 ms (asset overrides and op: textures) per tick, never while Houdini cooks the viewed stage, so Houdini's UI thread is never held by one; a long walk shows its progress in Houdini's status bar. A walk starts only for a change it reads (_changes: shading prims, bindings, wet and Substrate opinions for materials; shader and light images for op: textures; asset prims, unreal:surface:* and instancing for overrides), never for a light, camera or transform edit, and a change during a walk starts the next one once it has applied its result. A walk that meets a prim an edit removed starts over on the new stage. husk and usdview run the same walks to completion (cooperative.run). On NVIDIA's Da Vinci Workshop (3,000 MaterialX materials, 6,700 meshes) the walks held Houdini's UI for about 2.5 of the 4.5 minutes it froze on selecting hdUE, and for 45 s on every light edit.

Work from other threads reaches the owner through ueRun (delegate.cpp): with the worker, run(f); without one, inline. hdue_run_on_ue_thread runs a task through the same path and returns when it has run; the attached Python host sends every backend call it makes through it (Runtime.on_ue_thread, scripts/hdue_runtime.py). Live Render creates the delegate on one thread and executes it on others, which this indirection covers. In usdview, hdue_runtime.Runtime(start=True) initializes and ticks UE on usdview's Python thread; the delegate finds UE READY and starts no thread.

items.title: Thread inventory
items.text:
husk, realtime and Path Tracer (177-178 threads once UE is up; 60 two seconds after launch):

Name in Process Explorer Count Start module What it is GameThread 1 ucrtbase.dll hdUE's worker thread, renamed by UE (above) RenderThread 0 1 backend UE's rendering thread: ENQUEUE_RENDER_COMMAND work, RDG, readback polling and the half-float to float conversion RHIThread, RHISubmissionThread, RHIInterruptThread 1 each backend D3D12 command translation, submission, GPU completion Foreground Worker #0-1, Background Worker #0-27 2 + 28 backend UE's task scheduler (ParallelFor, UE::Tasks) Foreground Worker (Standby #0-1), Background Worker (Standby #0-15) 2 + 16 backend its standby workers PSOPrecompilePool #0-23 24 backend PSO compilation (UE's runtime PSO precache requests) IOThreadPool #0-3, BackgroundThreadPool #0-1, IoDispatcher, FAsyncLoadingThread 4 + 2 + 1 + 1 backend UE's I/O and package loading OutputDeviceRedirector, FAsyncWriter_HdUEBackend 1 each backend log fan-out and the log file writer CrashReportingThread, FHeartBeatThread, RTHeartBeat 0, FMediaTicker, FMessageBus.DefaultBus.Router, ScreenSaverInhibitor 1 each backend UE's crash handler, hang detectors and engine services D3D Background Thread 0-3 4 ucrtbase.dll the D3D12 runtime (inferred from the name) unnamed 64 ucrtbase.dll host thread pools; inferred: TBB workers (Hydra's WorkParallelForN, used by hdUE's mesh conversion, OCIO and render buffer copies) and Houdini's own pools; the start address alone cannot tell them apart unnamed 7-8 nvwgf2umx.dll NVIDIA's D3D12 driver unnamed 1 husk.exe husk's main thread: Hydra sync and Execute

Houdini's UI adds the same UE set (615 threads in all) next to Houdini's own: its UI thread, Qt's QQmlThread, QSGRenderThread and Thread (pooled), 82 unnamed ucrtbase.dll threads, 11 in nvoglv64.dll (GL), and 394 unnamed threads starting in nvwgf2umx.dll, against 7-8 under husk (inferred: driver threads of the D3D12 devices in the process).

items.title: hdUE's parallel work
items.text:
• Delegate (host side). Hydra syncs prims on its own TBB workers (HdRenderIndex::SyncAll); prims write into HdUEState under its mutex. prepareMeshes converts points, normals and UV sets with WorkParallelForN; HdUEToSceneLinear (OCIO) and the render buffers' copies (render_buffer.cpp) use it too. Colour textures in another colour space are converted once through OCIO into EXRs under %TEMP%\hdue_ocio.
  • Backend (UE side). ApplyScene builds static meshes with ParallelFor over the batch (Scene.cpp); texture block compression and readback conversion use ParallelFor. Interactive hosts launch Lumen card and Nanite builds as UE::Tasks at BackgroundLow priority (HdueConversion), one per set of identical meshes, which TickConversions swaps in on the game thread; a scene being destroyed waits for its running builds. Offline hosts build them inline before the frame.

items.title: One frame
items.text:
1. Sync (host thread, Hydra workers). Rprims (Mesh, Points, Curves, Volume in prims.cpp), sprims (materials, lights, cameras) and bprims (render buffers, fields) copy what UE needs into HdUEState: geometry, transforms, materials, and dirty sets (dirtyMeshes, movedMeshes, ...). Each change bumps revision. No UE call happens during Sync.
  2. Execute (Pass::_Execute, host thread). Copies the pass state (AOV bindings, buffers, view, projection, camera values) into a PassSnapshot, since Houdini reuses those objects once Execute returns. Then:
  3. husk / hython: host.run(...) blocks the host thread while the UE thread calls executeOnce repeatedly for up to 250 ms or until converged, so a realtime frame costs GPU time rather than husk's polling interval.
  4. Houdini's UI: host.post(...) and return at once; calls arriving while one is queued are coalesced to the newest camera, and the pump keeps publishing until IsConverged.
  5. executeOnce (UE thread). Ticks UE (unless the loop just did), creates or resizes the session (create_session, resize_session), and when revision changed: prepareScene takes the dirty sets under the state lock into a ScenePacket of ABI descriptors (a mesh that frees its arrays once uploaded moves them into the packet, released in the state, and convertDeferred builds its descriptor after the lock is released: built under it, a 1 GB streaming batch held the lock for 0.7 s while every Hydra Sync thread waited), then sendScene calls apply_scene (meshes, materials, removals; reset_scene on the first batch), then the lighting, volume, asset, surface and motion functions (set_transforms for moved meshes, keeping their geometry). Then it builds an HdueRenderRequest (UE centimetres, +X forward, +Z up; generation, mode, samples, warmup, projection, depth of field) and calls request_render when the request changed, then poll_frame / copy_frame (and copy_depth, poll_aov, copy_aov_buffer for AOVs).
  6. UE tick (Tick, Bridge.cpp). UELibrary_Tick, native assets, lighting and TickConversions; retire finished readbacks and poll the pending ones; when the Path Tracer's virtual texture warm-up is ready, reset the view state; unless the current request's frame is converged, Draw.
  7. Render. Draw builds a scene view family for the session's render target (SCS_FinalToneCurveHDR, so the float target gets UE's tone curve as linear Rec.709) and RenderAndReadBack calls BeginRenderingViewFamily. A frame converges after samples_per_pixel Path Tracer draws, or after warmup_frames full-resolution realtime draws; offline, the next frame of a sequence keeps the history and converges after one.
  8. Readback (CPU path). A FRHIGPUTextureReadback copies the colour (and depth, Path Tracer albedo/normal guides) in one of three slots. On a later tick the render thread locks it, converts half floats to float RGBA with straight alpha (and device depth to linear centimetres), and publishes Pixels and Frame under FrameMutex, with frame_id, generation, converged, completed_samples. poll_frame returns the newest frame; the delegate compares its generation with the request's so a stale frame is not shown as current.
  9. Shared GPU frames (Solaris viewport). With configure_gpu_frames enabled, each beauty draw is also written into a ring of three shared D3D12 textures (RGBA16F colour, R32F depth, bottom row first) and UE's queue signals a shared ready fence (SharedFrames.cpp). On the GL thread, HdUERenderBuffer::GetResource → HdUEGpuFrames::color calls acquire_gpu_frame, imports the NT handles once per ring (GL_EXT_memory_object_win32, GL_EXT_semaphore_win32), waits for the ready fence on the GPU (glWaitSemaphoreEXT), copies into HgiGL textures (glCopyImageSubData) and signals the release fence. The CPU readback then runs only for converged frames, and Houdini composites the CPU buffers once they hold the converged frame, since its selection highlight lines the CPU primId buffer up with a CPU colour buffer. Motion blur, the denoiser, a non-Rec.709 OCIO scene_linear, husk, usdview, Live Render and HDUE_GPU_FRAMES=0 keep the CPU path (docs/houdini/index.md).
  10. Publish (delegate). Pixels are converted to the OCIO scene_linear space when needed, written into the bound HdUERenderBuffers (colour, depth, AOVs, Cryptomatte), and the host maps them: husk writes the image, Houdini draws it.

items.title: Interactive and offline profiles
items.text:
Backend::boot passes HDUE_INIT_INTERACTIVE exactly in Houdini's UI (houdiniUi()); every other host gets the offline profile.

Offline (husk, hython) Interactive (Houdini's UI) Scalability Cinematic, keeping the resolution quality; r.Streaming.FullyLoadUsedTextures=1, r.D3D12.GPUTimeout=0, faster Lumen surface cache updates (Initialize) project defaults PSOs a draw does not count towards convergence while PSOs compile (observed: "hdUE request 1 waits for 2996 PSO compilations") not waited for; meshes appear when their PSOs are ready (UE's r.PSOPrecache.ProxyCreationStrategy 1) Texture streaming BlockTillAllRequestsFinished and pending virtual texture tiles before the frame not waited for Lumen cards and Nanite built inline in ApplyScene the mesh shows first, UE::Tasks build cards and Nanite, TickConversions swaps them in Resolution while moving full r.HdUE.InteractiveScreenPercentage (50) until requests stop for 250 ms Readbacks one in flight: the first draw, the converging one, and one per 250 ms for progress up to three in flight, every draw (or only converged ones with shared GPU frames) UE ticks inside Execute continuously on the UE thread

items.title: Startup and shutdown
items.text:
Startup. HdUnrealEngine::CreateRenderDelegate → HdUERenderDelegate constructor → hdue::Backend loads the backend and fills its one table from hdue_get_api (checked for version and size) → if no worker exists, get_status; when COLD, startSelfHost:

  • husk and hython wait for the boot; Houdini's UI returns at once (work posted meanwhile runs once UE is ready, and a boot failure is kept in bootError and reported by every later delegate).
  • On the new thread: hidden window, Backend::boot(instance, window, runtime_project, interactive) → Initialize: owner thread, embree/tbb preload, UELibrary_InitW, checks for GEngine, a non-null RHI and a game world with a scene, offline cvars, READY. Then std::atexit(shutdownSelfHost).

UE starts once per process. Later delegates (the next viewport, husk --restart-delegate) increment host.delegates and reuse it; deleting a delegate destroys its session (destroy_session releases the scene, readbacks and view states) but not UE. The backend has one session at a time ("The initial backend supports one active session."). Under husk, UE starts before husk prints >>> Render ... frame 1 (observed); about 3 s elapse between husk loading the stage and "Engine is initialized".

Shutdown in Houdini's UI. Host.close (Qt aboutToQuit, or atexit) calls hdue_shutdown_ue → shutdownSelfHost: on the UE thread, one tick, Backend::shutdown → Shutdown (DestroySession, UELibrary_Shutdown), destroy the window; then join the thread. Shutdown also constructs a function-local static whose destructor, which runs before UE's own static destructors at process exit, hands the game thread to the exiting thread (FTaskTagScope::SwapTag(ETaskTag::EGameThread), GGameThreadId = current thread), since ~FScheduler checks it runs on the game thread. Viewports that still draw afterwards report converged without rendering.

Shutdown elsewhere (husk). Nobody calls hdue_shutdown_ue. ExitProcess ends every other thread, including UE's, and then runs the DLL's atexit handlers at detach: shutdownSelfHost finds the worker thread already signalled and calls TerminateProcess with the exit code already set, because UE can no longer shut down from there and waiting for it hung the exit (delegate.cpp). So a husk process ends without UELibrary_Shutdown; observed exit code 0 for both renders. hdue_backend_smoke covers the clean path with UE on a worker thread through process exit.

Restart. Not possible: UELibrary cannot initialize again after Shutdown (Initialize returns HDUE_INVALID_STATE unless COLD), so a stopped UE stays stopped until the process exits.

Failures and where to look.

  • UE's log: <runtime project>\Saved\Logs\HdUEBackend.log, previous runs as HdUEBackend-backup-<time>.log, or under HDUE_USER_DIR (-userdir) when the package sets it. It holds every line. The host's stdout (husk's console, Houdini's Log Viewer, which shows the process's output under Standard Output) gets every Warning and Error line of every category (each warning once) and each PSO precache miss (Encountered a new ... PSO (PSOPrecacheState: Missed), which UE logs at Display but which is a PSO compiled on the render thread), as UTF-8. Other Display and Log lines are progress and stay in the file, as a UE game shows its user none of them. UE echoes every Display line by itself (FFeedbackContextAnsi, or -stdout), so Initialize swaps GWarn for UE's base FFeedbackContext when the output devices are created (FCoreDelegates::OnOutputDevicesInit) and adds a filtering device (FHdueConsoleEcho, Bridge.cpp); HDUE_UE_ARGS=-stdout restores UE's full echo.
  • husk shows no Tf warnings of a delegate, so hdUE prints its own to stderr as hdUE warning: ... (once per message) and frame failures as hdUE error: ..., and sets huskErrorStatus so husk exits non-zero.
  • Houdini's host: HDUE_HOUDINI_LOG_DIR, else $HOUDINI_TEMP_DIR/hdUE/<pid>/ (integration.log, runtime-state.json with the UI thread id, UE state, errors and the Substrate worker; ue.log is the name passed to the attached Runtime).
  • HDUE_TRACE_TIMING=1 (to HDUE_TRACE_FILE when set) prints slow ticks, slow tasks and where each Execute spent its time.
  • A UE crash is handled in process by UE's handler (CrashReportingThread); no crash reporter is staged, so none starts (inferred from the staged files). A hang in Houdini's UI shows the UI thread waiting in HdUESelfHost::run (a std::future::get: render stats, delegate and render pass destruction still use run) while GameThread is busy or blocked; Execute itself only posts.

items.title: Memory, GPU and disk
items.text:
• Scene data exists twice. The delegate keeps its own copy in HdUEState (points, normals, UVs, indices, transforms, materials) so that later edits resend only what changed; HDUE_TRACE_SCENE prints its running size during sync. submit sends it in batches of about 1 GB of stored geometry: each batch's ScenePacket holds its converted descriptors for the duration of apply_scene, which copies everything it needs (strings included) before returning (one packet for a whole scene copied it all a second time). Mesh rprims keep nothing of their own: the wet-mask refresh triangulates from the scene delegate when it needs a mask. Change detection compares a hash of each mesh's arrays (HdUEGeometryHash). Nor is the copy kept once UE has the mesh: once UE has a static mesh, finishScene frees its arrays (deforming, wet, masked and displaced meshes keep them). A later material, visibility or sidedness change reaches UE through update_meshes (C ABI 13) without the geometry, and a move through set_transforms; Sync compares the re-read arrays with the stored hash and frees them again. When UE needs the geometry after all (needs_upload: a static mesh made editable, or a Nanite mesh given a translucent material), the render pass calls the rprim's Sync itself with the geometry bits (HdUERepullMeshes), as Hydra would for a dirty prim (Houdini's viewport never syncs an rprim the render pass marks dirty), and frames do not converge until it is back. A mesh made wet after its upload comes back this way, and uploads dynamic. Large scenes are uploaded while Hydra still syncs them (HdUEStreamMeshes, husk, hython and Houdini's viewport): once 1 GB of stored geometry waits, hdUE's UE thread uploads it in batches (creating the session at the render settings' resolution if the first Execute has not come yet), and Sync threads wait while more than 4 GB waits; HDUE_STREAM_BYTES sets the batch size for tests. usdview keeps its copy, which its CPU ray picks read; Houdini's viewport picks from the ID AOVs UE renders and needs none. UE then owns its meshes (UStaticMesh render data without CPU copies once on the GPU, as UE's runtime builds, Nanite data, Lumen cards, dynamic meshes), materials, lights and textures in its world. Observed working sets: 2.7-2.9 GB for husk on the Cornell box, 5.1 GB for the Houdini session.
  • Heavy scenes. NVIDIA's Da Vinci Workshop shot (6,700 meshes, 617M triangles, render purpose) in Houdini's viewport (Launch-Houdini.ps1 -TestKind heavy, under a job memory limit with a commit timeline): before the changes below, the process ended at a 24 GB limit 67 s in, after 4 of its uploads, with "Out of video memory": the interactive first-pass meshes were full-resolution static meshes, and Windows charges a process's D3D12 allocations to its commit (all of them would have needed about 110 GB, 200 bytes per vertex). Now first passes stop at an estimated 2 GB (r.HdUE.InteractiveFirstPassMemory), the other meshes appear as their Nanite builds swap in, and the copies of a mesh in later uploads reuse its first pass. The shot then converges in 180 to 210 s with a job peak of 30 to 33 GB (one build per distinct mesh, 1,700, from a warm Nanite cache), and through its camera 3 s later. Of 22.5 GB during the upload, UE's LLM tracked 10.5 GB (8.6 GB of heap, most of it the copies of meshes whose builds wait for memory, and 2.4 GB of graphics); Houdini, its USD stage and the delegate held the rest. A Houdini session showing a small stage through hdUE holds about 10 GB. Houdini recreates its renderer once after the first frame of this stage (HUSD_Imaging::setupRenderer calls resetImagingEngine when its restart check, updateRestartCameraSettings or anyRestartRenderSettingsChanged, is true; read from libHUSD.dll's exports). It happens with the proxy purpose, without the scene camera, with viewport lighting off (no work light), with empty or dummy restartrendersettings and restartcamerasettings in UsdRenderers.json, with the stage's frame rate matched, and without hdUE's host steps (material, texture and asset sync). It does not happen on either half of the stage, on Cornell, smoke.usda or selection.usda. Just before it, Houdini's second evaluation of the render settings reaches the delegate (houdini:fps 24 to 60, shutter:open/close 0 to -0.25/0.25), which on small stages arrives without a reset. Nothing hdUE sends was found to trigger it, which syncs the stage again: destroy_session now frees the old scene at once with UE's UEngine::TrimMemory, as UE frees a level before loading the next, where it stayed until UE's next periodic garbage collection and the second sync passed 40 GB. Inside a Windows job with a memory limit, UE's available memory is the job's (memory.WindowsPlatformMemoryUseContainerMemory), which the background builds are scheduled against. Under husk, with streaming and freed copies, it got through the upload until UE's limits: Nanite's root page pool (one GPU buffer of at most 2 GB on NVIDIA, less 512 MB of streaming pool, holds about 100M of its triangles, since every page of a runtime mesh is a root page) and then the GPU memory of the meshes left without Nanite. Runtime meshes now keep one root page each and stream the rest from memory (an engine edit, Apply-ResidencyPatch.ps1; UE streams only cooked files outside the editor), so the root pool no longer bounds it. Three more things held host memory, each found with a job memory limit, a timeline of the process's commit and a map of its committed regions (VirtualQueryEx): the arrays of released meshes, which v = {} cleared without freeing (assign of an empty list keeps the capacity: about 30 GB in Houdini's mimalloc); Windows charges the process a commit for its D3D12 allocations, and each Nanite mesh kept a full-resolution LOD 0 and ray-tracing BLAS (about 200 bytes per triangle, write-combined regions as large as the GPU's dedicated and shared use), now the Nanite fallback as in UE's static mesh build; and 5,000 of its 6,750 meshes are copies of 1,700, which now share one static mesh each, as UE's USD importer shares them. Reading every render-purpose mesh through USD alone holds 1 GB. Under husk the shot now renders with a job memory peak of 22 GB (it ended at 32 to 38 GB limits before): 656 s from an empty Nanite cache, 117 s from it. Its first frame then hit a UE 5.8.4 bug, a Nanite raster pass that left its read-only dummy buffer in the renderer for Lumen's next card-capture pass to write (DXGI_ERROR_INVALID_CALL), fixed by an engine edit (Apply-ResidencyPatch.ps1). The proxy purpose (Houdini's display options) renders it in about 9 GB.
  • GPU. One render target per session, three readback slots (colour, depth, Path Tracer guides), the AOV view state when AOVs are requested, and, in the Solaris viewport, the three-slot shared ring (colour and depth textures, a ready and a release fence) that GL imports. acquire_gpu_frame returns new NT handles when the ring changes (first call, resize, depth toggled), and the caller closes them.
  • CPU frame buffers. The backend keeps the newest beauty frame, depth, guides and AOV pixels as float arrays under FrameMutex, recycled through spare buffers; copy_frame copies into the caller's buffer. The delegate's render buffers hold their own copy for Map().
  • On disk.
  • Shaders: the cooked shader archives in <runtime>\HdUEBackend\Content and GlobalShaderCache-PCD3D_SM6.bin; nothing is compiled at run time.
  • PSOs: none bundled (docs/building.md, "PSOs"). UE's own PSO disk cache is off (r.D3D12.PSO.DiskCache=0 in the log); the NVIDIA driver keeps its own shader cache (inferred).
  • Converted OCIO textures: %TEMP%\hdue_ocio, entries unused for a week removed (color_management.h).
  • Nanite builds: Saved\NaniteCache (BuildNanite, Scene.cpp), keyed by the builder's version and the mesh's content, entries unused for a week removed.
  • Block-compressed textures: %LOCALAPPDATA%\hdUE\TextureCache (CachePath, Scene.cpp), entries unused for a week removed.
  • Virtual textures: %LOCALAPPDATA%\hdUE\VirtualTextureCache (VirtualTextureBuild.cpp), manifests unused for a week removed with the chunks no other manifest names (a day's grace for chunks a running build has not named yet).
  • UE's Saved (Logs, Config, NaniteCache): %LOCALAPPDATA%\hdUE\Saved, where an installed UE game keeps it (UserSettingsDir(), FPaths::ProjectUserDir), or under HDUE_USER_DIR (-userdir, src/client/backend.cpp).
  • Houdini's host: its log directory (above) and exported op: texture images, removed on shutdown (docs/houdini/index.md).

items.title: ABI
items.text:
include/hdue/bridge.h is the whole backend ABI: HDUE_ABI_VERSION 24, engine 5.8.4. The backend exports one function, hdue_get_api(version, capacity, &api), which fills HdueApi (368 bytes: struct_size, abi_version and 45 function pointers) for exactly HDUE_ABI_VERSION, or returns HDUE_ABI_MISMATCH (another version) or HDUE_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL (capacity under sizeof(HdueApi)) without touching the table. src/client/backend.cpp and scripts/hdue_runtime.py load it once and check its version and size. It does not start UE, and the DLL must stay loaded until process exit. Fixed-width POD fields, UTF-8 strings copied during the call, opaque handles and caller-owned buffers cross it; UE, USD and STL types, exceptions and memory ownership do not. The delegate and backend come from the same build, so there are no optional parts: a change to any function or descriptor bumps the one version.

Functions Purpose initialize, get_status, tick, shutdown, window_message UE's lifetime create_session, destroy_session, resize_session render targets; resizing keeps the scene apply_scene, set_transforms meshes, materials, removals; transforms without resending geometry request_render, poll_frame, copy_frame the beauty set_depth_enabled, copy_depth linear depth readback poll_aov, set_aov_buffers, copy_aov_buffer AOV frames; buffer visualizations from one render upsert_lights, get_lighting_status UsdLux lights, HDRI, IES, light linking channels upsert_volume, remove_volume OpenVDB / field volumes upsert_asset, remove_asset, get_asset_status, get_asset_scene_status native UE assets in the scene get_renderer_info, set_material_parameters, get_material_stats renderer info, native material parameters, stats apply_surfaces, get_surface_status wet surface layer set_post_process post-process settings and cvars configure_residency, get_residency_status the Path Tracer's virtual texture warm-up before its samples count configure_gpu_frames, poll_gpu_frame, acquire_gpu_frame shared D3D12 frames for the host's graphics API pick_native, get_pick_material_info ray picks against UE meshes, material info

Recent versions: 24 groom attributes, materials and instances (HdueGroomDesc, HdueGroomAttribute); 23 Niagara effects (HDUE_ASSET_EFFECT, HdueAssetDesc timing); 22 get_load_status; 21 decals (upsert_decal); 20 volume materials (HdueVolumeDesc.material, parameters); 19 post-process volumes (upsert_post_process_volume); 18 removed the legacy HdueSceneBatch.lights (every light goes through upsert_lights); 17 animated Sparse Volume Texture frames; 16 volume emission, light functions, realtime refraction and grooms (upsert_groom); 15 per-light UE properties and lens distortion; 14 Local Fog Volumes (upsert_local_fog_volume); 13 update_meshes; 12 folded the twelve separately versioned extension tables and hdue_resize_session into HdueApi; 11 added the HDUE_AOV_BUFFERS and HDUE_AOV_LIGHTING requests and the Path Tracer's own albedo and normal; 10 added UV sets (uv_set_count, HdueTextureDesc.uv_set); 9 texture wrap modes and per-texture sRGB decoding; 8 indexed meshes and runtime MaterialX; 7 the camera projection and depth of field; 6 per-vertex and per-instance colours.

The delegate DLL exports a host-side API of its own (include/hdue/viewport_api.h, for the Python host): hdue_get_viewport_status, hdue_set_viewport_up_axis, hdue_run_on_ue_thread, hdue_set_viewport_materials, hdue_set_viewport_surfaces, hdue_set_viewport_textures (each descriptor version 1) and hdue_shutdown_ue. Calls validate versions, sizes, capacities, generations and the owning thread. These stay plain exports: the Python host binds each by name with ctypes, and a table would add a getter and a mirror struct for no loader to remove.

items.title: Motion blur
items.text: UE's Path Tracer has no motion blur of its own (Movie Render Queue averages sub-frames). hdUE does the same inside the delegate: rprims record their transform samples one frame either side (SampleTransform, SampleInstancerTransform) and their velocities; the camera sprim records its own. When the render camera has an open shutter and something moves, the render pass renders unreal:motionSamples sub-frames at times spread over [shutter:open, shutter:close], moving meshes through set_transforms (which leaves geometry untouched), and publishes the running average. Instances with time-sampled positions, orientations, scales or matrices (and no velocities) are evaluated at each sub-frame from the instance matrices at every sample time in the window, interpolated as UsdGeomPointInstancer::ComputeInstanceTransformsAtTime interpolates the primvars (positions and scales linearly, orientations by slerp; HdUEInterpolateInstance). Deforming meshes, and the companion mesh into which a generic prototype's sheared instances are baked (a mesh of its own, split off at Sync: HdUEStoreShearCompanion), are re-uploaded per sub-frame; the prototype's other instances only move. Path Tracer samples are divided between sub-frames. AOVs render the unblurred pose at the current time.

items.title: Inspecting a process
items.text:
The thread table above came from this PowerShell, run against a husk or Houdini PID while it renders (THREAD_QUERY_INFORMATION is needed: GetThreadDescription returns access denied with the limited right):

Add-Type @"
using System; using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
public static class Th {
  [DllImport("kernel32")] static extern IntPtr OpenThread(uint a, bool i, uint id);
  [DllImport("kernel32")] static extern bool CloseHandle(IntPtr h);
  [DllImport("kernel32")] static extern int GetThreadDescription(IntPtr h, out IntPtr d);
  [DllImport("ntdll")] static extern int NtQueryInformationThread(IntPtr h, int c, out IntPtr v, int l, IntPtr r);
  public static string Name(uint id, out long start) {
    IntPtr h = OpenThread(0x40, false, id), p, v; start = 0; string s = "";
    if (h == IntPtr.Zero) return "?";
    if (GetThreadDescription(h, out p) >= 0 && p != IntPtr.Zero) s = Marshal.PtrToStringUni(p);
    if (NtQueryInformationThread(h, 9, out v, IntPtr.Size, IntPtr.Zero) == 0) start = v.ToInt64();
    CloseHandle(h); return s;
  }
}
"@
$p = Get-Process -Id <pid>
$p.Modules | Select ModuleName, FileName
$p.Threads | % { $s = 0L; $n = [Th]::Name([uint32]$_.Id, [ref]$s)
  $m = $p.Modules | ? { $s -ge $_.BaseAddress.ToInt64() -and $s -lt $_.BaseAddress.ToInt64() + $_.ModuleMemorySize }
  "{0}`t{1}`t{2}`t{3}" -f $_.Id, $n, $m.ModuleName, $_.TotalProcessorTime }

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Unreal Engine 5.8.4 source: tag 5.8.4-release, commit f45729c0b6f097038e72b52d366a62baeca3275b.
  • Windows x64, Visual Studio 2022 C++ tools, a Windows SDK, DirectX 12, and hardware ray tracing. The CMake scripts use the Visual Studio 17 2022 generator.
  • MSVC 14.44.35211 or newer (a current Visual Studio 2022 17.14 update) or 14.50.35723 or newer. UE 5.8.4 rejects MSVC 14.39-14.43, 14.44 before 35211, and 14.50 before 35723; Engine/Config/Windows/Windows_SDK.json in the engine source holds the authoritative list.
  • .NET Framework 4.8 SDK and 4.6.2 targeting pack (Visual Studio Installer components Microsoft.Net.Component.4.8.SDK and Microsoft.Net.Component.4.6.2.TargetingPack). Without them, UnrealBuildTool stops with Could not find NetFxSDK install dir.
  • PowerShell 7, Git, and CMake 3.24 or newer, with Git and CMake available on PATH.
  • OpenUSD 26.03 C++ SDK with Hydra/usdImaging, usdview, and Python 3.11 bindings for the standalone host and usdview. Build it with a moderate job count (-j 8); 28 parallel MSVC jobs ran out of compiler heap on a 64 GB machine.
  • Houdini 22.0 with its bundled USD 26.05 and Python 3.13, for Solaris; see Supported Houdini builds.
  • uv for all Python execution and dependency management.

The standalone and Houdini delegates use separate builds because their USD ABIs differ. The UE backend disables UE's USD and Python plugins. Dependencies retain their own licensing requirements.

items.title: Local configuration
items.text:
Run commands from the repository root. Store installation locations in the ignored .local/paths.json file, environment variables, or explicit script parameters. Fill in the values locally; do not commit them.

{
  "engine_root": "",
  "editor_root": "",
  "openusd_root": "",
  "houdini_root": ""
}
Local key Environment variable Script parameter engine_root HDUE_ENGINE_ROOT -EngineRoot editor_root HDUE_EDITOR_ROOT -EditorRoot openusd_root HDUE_OPENUSD_ROOT -OpenUsdRoot houdini_root HDUE_HOUDINI_ROOT or HFS -HoudiniRoot houdini_build_root HDUE_HOUDINI_BUILD_ROOT -BuildDirectory (Houdini build/launch scripts) runtime_config HDUE_RUNTIME_CONFIG -RuntimeConfig review_scene HDUE_REVIEW_SCENE -InputUsd

Explicit parameters take priority over environment variables and local configuration. HDUE_LOCAL_CONFIG selects an alternative local configuration file. Relative values stored in that file are resolved against its directory; relative explicit parameters and environment values use the current working directory.

runtime_config is read by Launch-Houdini.ps1 and Update-HoudiniRuntime.ps1. Pass -RuntimeConfig explicitly to Launch-Usdview.ps1; it otherwise uses the repository's staged runtime. review_scene supplies the input for Test-Usdview.ps1 -Check opacity and -Check glass.

Keep private projects, scene-specific helpers, catalogs, runtime profiles, and review evidence in .local/, external/, or out/. These directories are ignored. The source under unreal/HdUEBackend remains version controlled; its generated Content and build products do not.

items.title: Build and validation
items.text:
.\scripts\Setup-Engine.ps1
.\scripts\Verify.ps1 -WithUsdview

Setup-Engine.ps1 obtains the pinned source using your own engine access. Verify.ps1 builds the host, prepares synthetic UE content, builds the backend DLL, stages a runtime, runs rendering checks, and compares native UE and Hydra HDR images. -WithUsdview adds GUI, camera, and buffer checks. -SkipBuild reuses compatible build and cook outputs.

Individual steps:

.\scripts\Build-Host.ps1        # standalone delegate and hosts (OpenUSD)
.\scripts\Prepare-Content.ps1   # synthetic UE content: Preview Surface, ID, volume materials
.\scripts\Build-Backend.ps1     # UE backend DLL
.\scripts\Stage-Runtime.ps1     # cook and stage the runtime
.\scripts\Build-Houdini.ps1     # Houdini delegate (no OpenUSD needed)
.\scripts\Update-HoudiniRuntime.ps1 -RuntimeConfig .local\runtime.json -OutputConfig .local\runtime-houdini.json
.\scripts\Package-Houdini.ps1 -RuntimeConfig .local\runtime-houdini.json -Zip -UnrealLicenseesOnly  # licensees only: see docs/houdini/index.md

Stage-Runtime.ps1 replaces the staged binaries, including the hashed Houdini copy of the backend, so run Update-HoudiniRuntime.ps1 after every stage.

items.title: PSOs
items.text:
UE compiles a pipeline state object (PSO) the first time a draw or dispatch needs one. hdUE ships no recorded PSO cache: material PSOs are precached when meshes are created (UE's runtime PSO precaching; a mesh appears once its PSOs are ready, UE's default r.PSOPrecache.ProxyCreationStrategy), and the GPU driver keeps every compiled PSO in its own disk cache across runs. A bundled cache, recorded by rendering representative scenes, only covered the passes the recording happened to render and needed recording again after every shader change; with a warm driver cache it changed nothing measurable (texture/udim, two runs per mode: realtime 8.2/7.2 s with it, 6.9/6.8 s without; Path Tracer 6.9/7.0 s with, 7.2/7.2 s without).

Global and post-processing passes that UE does not precache (bloom and blur filters, depth of field, lens flares, the tonemapper, virtual texture page table updates) log Encountered a new graphics PSO (PSOPrecacheState: Missed) the first time each process binds them, 20-35 lines per run. They are UE's Display-level notice that a PSO was created on first use; the driver serves it from its cache. Only the first run after a driver update or cache wipe compiles them for real, a one-off hitch in the first frames. r.PSOPrecache.Validation=2 logs the pass and material of each miss in a material pass, which would be an hdUE precaching gap to fix.

At the end of its pre-initialization UE precaches the compute PSOs of the global shaders (PrecacheComputePipelineStatesForGlobalShaders, r.PSOPrecache.GlobalShaders, 5,404 shaders), one task per shader on the worker threads. Their code is already in memory: loading a shader map reads all of its shaders' code (FShaderLibraryInstance::AddResource), and creating a shader releases its map's hold on that code (FShaderMapResource::CreateShaderOrCrash). Shaders with identical code share one library shader, and FShaderLibraryInstance::GetOrCreateShader creates outside its lock, so two tasks could create it at once: the second, having missed the cache, found the code released by the first and read it again on its worker. Each such read logged "Spent N ms in a blocking wait for shader preload" (18-35 per Houdini session or husk run, NumRefs 1, frame 0); the default material's Nanite raster PSO precache hit the same race. Apply-ResidencyPatch.ps1 makes GetOrCreateShader check its cache again under the lock it already takes, and otherwise hold the code until the shader is created. Turning the global precache off (r.PSOPrecache.GlobalShaders=0) also removed the waits, but left 222 PSOs to compile on the render thread.

The monolithic DLL requires a source engine. A matching editor installation can prepare content. Apply-ResidencyPatch.ps1 makes small engine edits, validating the engine version and each insertion point: one friend declaration for virtual-texture residency, an editor-only guard around NaniteBuilder's displacement-texture read (NaniteDisplace.cpp) so the runtime can build Nanite meshes, and the SUBSTRATE_LOAD_FROM_MATERIALCONTAINER define UE 5.8.4's AmbientCubemapComposite.usf lacks (without it the Ambient Cubemap adds nothing with Substrate's adaptive GBuffer), and, in NaniteStreamingManager, the editor's path for streaming Nanite pages from memory in non-editor builds too (runtime-built meshes keep their pages in memory; cooked ones are never loaded there and stream from disk as before), the same memory path for virtual texture chunks in UploadingVirtualTexture.cpp (runtime UDIM sets keep their chunks in memory), the cache check in ShaderLibraryInstance.cpp described above, and alpha in rough refraction's copy of the scene (DistortFiltering.usf wrote alpha 1 into a PF_FloatR11G11B10 mip chain, DistortionRendering.cpp, so with r.PostProcessing.PropagateAlpha everything seen through glass came out uncovered: alpha 0.06 over opaque objects). ReflectionEnvironmentShaders.usf gets one line in the cube filter (FilterPS): a 512-texel sky light filters its top mip with GGX at roughness 2^(-7/1.2), where ImportanceSampleGGX's sqrt(1 - CosTheta^2) is NaN on the GPU for 5 of its 32 samples; each still passed NoL > 0 and read the cube in a NaN direction, so a dome's pole colour leaked 5/32 into every direction. A NaN half vector becomes (0, 0, 1), its exact limit; MonteCarlo.ush itself stays unchanged, since material shaders include it. The Path Tracer's solid glass (PathTracingMaterialHitShader.usf, PathTracingSubstrateSolidGlass.ush) tints the surface of a non-scattering glass slab whose mean free path is under 1 cm, the 0.01 cm layer UE's Standard Surface function makes of transmission depth 0, instead of absorbing inside the object; the tint travels in SpecularEdgeColor, which solid glass does not read, flagged by the payload's free output bit. Those are material shaders: re-cook the content after applying it, then stage the runtime (Stage-Runtime.ps1): Update-HoudiniRuntime.ps1 alone stages the DLL, not the cooked shaders. The shader edits go into both the source engine and the editor installation (editor_root), since the editor's cook compiles the runtime's global shaders; prepare content and stage the runtime after applying it. The global shaders are a pair, Engine/GlobalShaderCache-PCD3D_SM6.bin and ShaderArchive-Global-PCD3D_SM6-PCD3D_SM6.ushaderbytecode: a runtime given one without the other fails at boot ("Could not load section ... of the global shadermap"). UELibrary and Launch are otherwise unchanged.

items.title: NVIDIA DLSS
items.text:
DLSS is optional and comes from NVIDIA's plugin, which is never committed: the NVIDIA RTX SDKs license does not allow its source to be redistributed or put under this repository's license. Download the UE 5.8 package from NVIDIA's DLSS page (an NVIDIA Developer login; tested with DLSS4.5Plugin_v8.9.0) and copy two of its plugins into unreal/HdUEBackend/Plugins/ (ignored by git):

  • Plugins/DLSS: DLSS.uplugin, Source, Shaders, Config, Resources, Content, Binaries/ThirdParty (the NGX DLLs) and Binaries/Win64 (the prebuilt editor modules, which the cook loads; their BuildId must match editor_root's).
  • Plugins/StreamlineNGXCommon: StreamlineNGXCommon.uplugin, Source, Resources and Binaries/Win64.

The Streamline, Frame Generation, NIS and Movie Pipeline plugins are not needed. HdUEBackend.uproject lists both plugins as optional, and HdUEBackend.Build.cs links DLSS only when Plugins/DLSS/DLSS.uplugin exists. After adding them, run Build-Backend.ps1, Prepare-Content.ps1 (the editor's cook compiles the plugin's global shaders) and Stage-Runtime.ps1; staging copies the NGX DLLs. Engine quality describes the setting.

Fresh verification evidence is written under out/. A successful exit code alone is insufficient: tests require new images, metadata, and clean engine shutdown.

C++ follows Google style with 4-space indents and 120 columns (.clang-format); format what you change with git clang-format or your editor's format-on-save. .clang-tidy enables the bug-prone and performance checks; CI runs it on the client library, and locally it needs a compile_commands.json (cmake -G Ninja -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON from a Visual Studio developer prompt). Both tools ship with Visual Studio's C++ Clang tools. Python uses Black and Ruff (pyproject.toml: 80 columns, Python 3.11+, Google docstrings): uvx black scripts tests integrations and uvx ruff check --fix .... PowerShell uses Invoke-Formatter and PSScriptAnalyzer (PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1). .editorconfig sets whitespace for everything else. CI checks all of them, and lints the workflow with actionlint.

items.title: Supported Houdini builds
items.text:
The HDK only guarantees its ABI within one Houdini daily build. Build-Houdini.ps1 compiles against the build in houdini_root and stamps it into the delegate's version resource, runtime.json and the package name. The installed package loads from that build up to the last 22.0 build; in any build other than the one it was compiled against, the delegate prints a warning when it starts.

hdUE Compiled against Tested on v0.2.0 and later Houdini 22.0.368 22.0.368

items.title: Release checklist
items.text:
GitHub runners cannot build Unreal Engine, so releases are built locally:

  1. Set project(hdUE VERSION x.y.z) in CMakeLists.txt, commit, and tag vx.y.z on that commit.
  2. .\scripts\Verify.ps1 -WithUsdview and .\scripts\Test.ps1 -Suite all on a clean tree.
  3. Render the gallery (hython scripts/render_gallery.py --dev). It fails when a scene's brightness against Karma CPU leaves its band (scripts/check_gallery.py, which CI also runs on the committed docs/gallery.md) or a Cornell hdUE render departs from its tile baseline (tests/gallery_baselines.json); after an intended change, check the images and store new baselines with --bless.
  4. .\scripts\Build-Houdini.ps1, .\scripts\Build-Backend.ps1 -Configuration Test and .\scripts\Update-HoudiniRuntime.ps1 -Configuration Test -OutputConfig .local\runtime-release.json, then .\scripts\Package-Houdini.ps1 -RuntimeConfig .local\runtime-release.json -Zip -UnrealLicenseesOnly. It refuses uncommitted changes, a delegate built from another commit, and a backend that is not the current Test build (packages ship Test; see houdini).
  5. Add the build to the table above. Keep the package zip and its -symbols.zip together; distribute the package only as docs/houdini/index.md describes.

items.title: Standalone rendering and usdview
items.text:
.\scripts\Test-Hydra.ps1 -InputUsd samples/smoke.usda -Mode both -Cycles 1
.\scripts\Launch-Usdview.ps1 -InputUsd samples/smoke.usda
.\scripts\Launch-Usdview.ps1 -InputUsd samples/smoke.usda -Mode pathtraced

The launcher owns UE initialization, Tick, and shutdown on the UI thread. Use it rather than an unmanaged usdview process. Asynchronous scene processing is unsupported.

Camera controls include orbit, pan, and dolly. Continuous updates are coalesced. Lumen retains its ViewState during camera motion; scene, material, time, resolution, and Path Tracer request changes reset accumulation.

The launcher supplies its own CPU picking path for generic meshes and supported native geometry, separate from the Hydra ID AOVs. Native CPU picking requires readable, resident LOD0 data and rejects unsupported material deformation or Nanite overrides.

hdue_usd_render renders a USD file to PFM without a GUI (--prim-id also writes the primId AOV).

items.title: Cameras
items.text: hdUE renders through the USD camera (UsdGeomCamera) that Houdini's viewport or husk hands it. Framing, depth of field, exposure and the shutter come from the camera; UE's lens distortion comes from unreal:lensDistortion:* attributes on it.

items.title: Using it in Solaris
items.text:
1. Create a Camera LOP, or edit an existing camera with it.
  2. Look through it in the viewport, or pick it in the render settings' Camera for husk.
  3. Set depth of field and exposure on its Sampling tab.

The Camera LOP takes millimetres and writes USD's units: tenths of a scene unit, by the stage's metres per unit. A 50 mm lens in a metres stage is focalLength 0.5. hdUE reads the authored value in USD's units, as Hydra does.

items.title: Projection
items.text:
Projection USD attribute projection Default perspective

perspective or orthographic. An orthographic camera's Horizontal Aperture is the width of the view in tenths of a scene unit.

items.title: Focal length and aperture
items.text:
Focal Length USD attribute focalLength Default 50 (tenths of a scene unit) Horizontal Aperture USD attribute horizontalAperture Default 20.955 Vertical Aperture USD attribute verticalAperture Default 15.2908

Focal length over aperture sets the field of view. The aperture is conformed to the image's aspect ratio as Karma conforms it. Focal length also sets how much depth of field blurs: a longer lens at the same f-stop blurs more.

items.title: Lens shift
items.text:
Horizontal Aperture Offset USD attribute horizontalApertureOffset Default 0 Vertical Aperture Offset USD attribute verticalApertureOffset Default 0

Shifts the image window without turning the camera, in the aperture's units. Use it to keep verticals straight in architecture shots.

items.title: Clipping
items.text:
Clipping Range USD attribute clippingRange Default (1, 1000000)

hdUE applies the near clip. It does not apply the far clip: everything beyond it still renders. UE's views keep an infinite far plane, and UE's Path Tracer traces past any far plane. To hide distant geometry, deactivate it or set its visibility instead.

items.title: Depth of field
items.text:
F-Stop USD attribute fStop Default 0 Focus Distance USD attribute focusDistance Default 0, scene units

Depth of field is on when both are above 0. Lower f-stops blur more: each halving of the f-stop doubles the blur. Focus Distance is measured from the camera in scene units, not in tenths.

The toys are 1.2 m apart; the camera is focused on the nearest (2.4 m), with a 50 mm lens on a 36 mm sensor.

At f/1.4, the focus distance moves along the row: toy 0 is 2.4 m away, toy 1 is 3.6 m, toy 3 is 6 m, toy 5 is 8.4 m.

The Path Tracer traces a thin lens (UE's reference depth of field). Realtime uses UE's post-process depth of field, which approximates it and clamps very large blur.

To render every camera in focus, turn on Disable Depth of Field (disableDepthOfField) in the render settings. The UE side of depth of field (blade count, the post-process method) is in the Lens settings.

items.title: Exposure
items.text:
Exposure USD attribute exposure Default 0, stops

Exposure F-Stop, Exposure ISO, Exposure Time · exposure:fStop (1), exposure:iso (100), exposure:time (1)

Each stop of Exposure doubles the image's brightness. hdUE combines the four attributes into one scale as USD defines it, so the exposure triplet works as on a real camera. With the Unreal Tonemapper on (the default), the camera's exposure adds to Exposure Compensation. With it off, it scales the beauty and leaves the other AOVs untouched, as Karma does.

Exposure F-Stop changes brightness only. Depth of field reads F-Stop.

items.title: Lens distortion
Shutter
items.text:
Shutter Open USD attribute shutter:open Default 0 Shutter Close USD attribute shutter:close Default 0, frames

Motion blur needs Shutter Close above Shutter Open. See Motion blur.

items.title: Image size, crops and tiles
items.text: The render settings' resolution, pixel aspect ratio, aspect ratio conform policy and data window (crops, overscan) are honoured, as in Karma. Depth and AOVs follow the same window. One image can be at most 16384 pixels on a side, UE's largest texture on D3D12. For larger images, render husk tiles (--tile-count), each within the limit.

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
Shallow focus on a subject 2 m away, full-frame 50 mm look:

  1. In the Camera LOP, set Focal Length to 50 and Horizontal Aperture to 36 (millimetres).
  2. Set Focus Distance to 2.
  3. Set F-Stop to 1.4.
  4. For final frames, set Render Mode to Path Traced for the thin-lens blur.

Brighten a shot by one stop without touching the lights: set the camera's Exposure to 1.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Cause Fix Everything is a blur, even at f/16. The focal length is authored in millimetres in a metres stage: focalLength 50 is a 5 m lens. Author the lens with the Camera LOP, which converts millimetres; or write 0.5 for 50 mm in a metres stage. No depth of field. F-Stop or Focus Distance is 0, or Disable Depth of Field is on. Set both above 0; turn the render setting off. Distant geometry renders past the far clip. hdUE does not apply the far clip. Deactivate or hide the geometry. Tile seams in a tiled realtime render. Lumen screen traces, bloom and temporal anti-aliasing see only the tile. Render tiled images with the Path Tracer. A huge image fails. Over 16384 pixels on a side. Render husk tiles.

items.title: Unreal Engine and Karma
items.text:
• Framing, aperture offsets, crops and orthographic projection match Karma.
  • The far clip is ignored, where Karma clips.
  • Realtime depth of field is UE's post-process depth of field, not a ray-traced lens; the Path Tracer traces a thin lens like Karma.
  • Lens distortion is UE's model, read from unreal:lensDistortion:*. Split diopters are not translated.

items.title: Conformance
items.text: A spec-driven test set: one small USD scene per schema feature in samples/conformance, written from the OpenUSD schemas (usdGeom, usdLux, usdShade, usdSkel, usdRender, usdVol, usdMedia, usdProc schema.usda), the UsdPreviewSurface specification and the Hydra AOV tokens, not from what hdUE does. Each scene's doc string states what the spec says and what the render must show; its customLayerData["conformance"] lists machine-checked expectations. Failures are gaps to fix or to document, not noise to tune away.

items.title: Running
items.text:
hython scripts/run_conformance.py [--only AREA/FEATURE|PATTERN ...] [--mode realtime|pathtraced] [--matrix]
    [--houdini HFS] [--build build/houdini] [--integrations integrations/houdini] [--runtime-config FILE]

It renders every scene with husk (HdUnrealEngine) in each mode, one husk at a time with a timeout, prints a pass/fail table, writes out/conformance/report.json and, with --matrix, rewrites the matrix below. It exits 1 when a check fails or a render does not finish. Each run takes about 5-12 s (UE startup dominates), so the whole set (150 scenes, both modes) takes about 35 minutes; use --only and --mode while iterating. A scene's "husk" list adds husk options (render_settings/render_pass renders --pass Pass).

items.title: How scenes are built
items.text:
• Every scene sublayers common/stage.usda: metres, Y up, a camera at z = 10 whose frame is exactly x, y in [-5, 5] on the z = 0 plane, a normalized distant key light (4 lux), and 128 x 128 render settings with two products: the beauty and the primId/instanceId AOVs.
  • Small textures they read are in textures.
  • Lights author intensity 1 and set brightness with exposure (except the scene that tests intensity).
  • The runner writes a root layer per scene and mode (stage metadata, the scene as a sublayer, unreal:renderMode).
  • Effects that are global (exposure, light size, colour temperature, dome rotation) vary over frames, rendered by one husk process; everything else compares two prims side by side in one frame.

items.title: Checks
items.text:
A check measures a probe {"frame", "region", "aov", "stat"}; regions are [x0, y0, x1, y1] in the shared camera's view units (-5..5, y up).

Kind Passes when value the stat lies in [min, max] (or equals) ratio stat(a) / stat(b) lies in [min, max] color the region's mean RGB, normalized to sum 1, is within tol of rgb normalized log the regex is found (or, with "present": false, absent) in husk's output metadata the frame's image metadata value named metadata matches the regex match

Stats: luma (mean, default), max, alpha, coverage (alpha > 0.5), soft (0.05 < alpha < 0.95), partial (luma between 5% and 95% of the region's maximum: filtered edges), bbox_aspect, bbox_height, width, height, ids (distinct primId values over at least 3 pixels), instances (distinct primId/instanceId pairs); a probe's "channel": i measures the mean of one channel instead. On a Cryptomatte layer: crypto_ids (distinct rank-0 ids over at least 3 pixels), crypto_id (the most common rank-0 id, hex), crypto_coverage (mean coverage of ranks 0 and 1), crypto_soft (share of pixels with partial rank-0 coverage). All checks are relative or structural; none compares with another renderer.

items.title: Gallery
items.text: Point at a bar or a mark for its value; click a renderer in the legend to hide or show it.

items.title: Cornell box: one feature per scene
items.text:
Every scene is the CC0 Cornell box plus one small layer from samples/cornell/variants, rendered with husk at 512 × 512:

  • hdUE Lumen: realtime mode, 64 warmup frames on a sequence's first frame, then one draw per frame (as Movie Render Queue).
  • hdUE Path Tracer: 512 samples per pixel, up to 32 bounces.
  • Karma XPU (GPU and CPU) and Karma CPU: path traced, 512 samples per pixel, 8 diffuse bounces.
  • Machine: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 and AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core Processor.
  • Times are per frame without process or UE startup: hdUE from the delegate's timing trace of a 16-frame (Lumen) or 4-frame (Path Tracer) husk run, after its first frame (a Lumen time is a sequence frame's, after the first frame's warm-up),Karma as husk's wall time minus its startup on an empty stage.
  • Speed-ups compare with Karma XPU, the GPU renderer, when it was rendered; brightness is the mean luminance relative to Karma CPU, the reference (1.00 = same).

Regenerate with hython scripts/render_gallery.py.

items.title: Sponza: a production-style scene
items.text:
Intel's Sponza 2022 (Frank Meinl and Anton Kaplanyan, CC BY 4.0; not included in this repository), from its main camera. Intel exports UsdPreviewSurface only; samples/sponza/materials.usda gives every material a MaterialX standard_surface network on Intel's textures (stone, metal, wood, sheen and translucent curtains, translucent leaves cut out by their alpha, glass), which hdUE and Karma render. hdUE's Path Tracer image is denoised by UE's default denoiser (NNEDenoiser, PathTracingEnableDenoiser on); Karma's is not. Ray tracing uses Nanite's fallback meshes, as in UE (r.RayTracing.Nanite.Mode 0): the tree and the curtains are simplified in the Path Tracer, and Nanite Ray Tracing (Streamed Out Mesh) traces them in full. The scene has no lights, so samples/sponza/lighting.usda adds a sun and a sky dome fitted to Intel's own renders of the scene, and levels the camera as Intel's render does; samples/sponza/no_decals.usda deactivates the dirt decal meshes. Add-ons from the same package, sublayered unchanged: NewSponza_Curtains_USD_YUp.usda, NewSponza_CypressTree_USDA_YUp.usda. Rendered with husk at 960 × 540:

  • hdUE Lumen: realtime mode, 64 warmup frames on a sequence's first frame, then one draw per frame (as Movie Render Queue).
  • hdUE Path Tracer: 256 samples per pixel, up to 32 bounces.
  • Karma XPU (GPU and CPU) and Karma CPU: path traced, 256 samples per pixel, 8 diffuse bounces.
  • Machine: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 and AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core Processor.
  • Times are per frame without process or UE startup: hdUE from the delegate's timing trace of a 16-frame (Lumen) or 4-frame (Path Tracer) husk run, after its first frame (a Lumen time is a sequence frame's, after the first frame's warm-up),Karma as husk's wall time minus its startup on an empty stage.
  • Speed-ups compare with Karma XPU, the GPU renderer, when it was rendered; brightness is the mean luminance relative to Karma CPU, the reference (1.00 = same).

items.title: Lights
items.text:
hdUE turns each UsdLux light into a UE light: a rect light, a point or spot light, a directional light, or the sky light for a dome. Intensity, exposure, colour and size keep UsdLux's units.

The light types on the chrome ball and grey box: the RectLight key, a sphere light, a spot and a normalized sun.

items.title: Using it in Solaris
items.text:
1. Create a Light LOP (or Distant Light, Dome Light) and pick its Type.
  2. Set Intensity to 1 and tune brightness with Exposure.
  3. UE-only settings are on the Light LOP's Unreal Engine tab (see Unreal Engine properties).

items.title: Light types
items.text:
UsdLux Houdini Light type UE light Notes RectLight Rectangle Light Rect Light Texture (inputs:texture:file) emits an image. DiskLight Disk Light Rect Light with a round mask An approximation of a disk. SphereLight Sphere Light, Point Light Point Light Radius is UE's Source Radius; treatAsPoint sets it to 0. SphereLight + ShapingAPI Sphere Light with Spotlight on Spot Light Cones up to 90°; see Spot lights. CylinderLight Cylinder Light Point Light with a Source Length A capsule: an approximation of a cylinder. DistantLight Distant Light Directional Light Angle is UE's Source Angle. DomeLight, DomeLight_1 Dome Light Sky Light See Dome lights and HDRIs. MeshLightAPI Geometry Light an emissive surface See Mesh lights.

Not supported: GeometryLight, PortalLight and PluginLight prims render nothing, with a warning. VolumeLightAPI is ignored with a warning; the volume renders without emitting, as in UE's USD importer.

items.title: Intensity and exposure
items.text:
Intensity USD attribute inputs:intensity Default 1 (DistantLight: 50000) Exposure USD attribute inputs:exposure Default 0, stops

UsdLux intensity is luminance, in nits, of the light's surface. The light's brightness is

\[ \text{brightness} = \text{Intensity} \times 2^{\text{Exposure}} \]

Each stop of exposure doubles it. Keep Intensity at 1 and set brightness with Exposure.

A DistantLight's intensity is the luminance of its sun disk. Its illuminance is

\[ E = \text{intensity} \times \pi \sin^2\left(\frac{\text{angle}}{2}\right) \]

A 0.53° sun at intensity 1 gives 0.000067 lux. Turn on Normalize Power to set the sun in lux instead.

items.title: Size and normalize
items.text:
Width, Height USD attribute inputs:width, inputs:height Default 1 (RectLight) Radius USD attribute inputs:radius Default 0.5 (SphereLight, DiskLight, CylinderLight) Length USD attribute inputs:length Default 1 (CylinderLight) Normalize Power USD attribute inputs:normalize Default off

A bigger light gives softer shadows and wider highlights. Without Normalize Power, a bigger light also emits more: twice the width and height is 4 times the light. With it on, hdUE divides the intensity by the light's area, so size changes softness only.

A RectLight from 0.25 m to 2 m, normalized.

A 2 × 2 m RectLight with Normalize Power off and on. Off, it is 4 times (2 stops) brighter than the 1 m light it replaced.

A light's size also decides how sharp its reflection is on glossy surfaces. On SideFX's Veach planks, four sphere lights of increasing size shine on planks of increasing roughness: small lights give sharp highlights on the smooth planks, large lights wide ones on the rough planks. Realtime and the Path Tracer:

items.title: Colour and temperature
items.text:
Color USD attribute inputs:color Default (1, 1, 1) Enable Color Temperature USD attribute inputs:enableColorTemperature Default off Color Temperature USD attribute inputs:colorTemperature Default 6500, kelvin

With temperature on, the light's colour is multiplied by the colour of a black body at that temperature. 6500 K is about white; lower is warmer, higher is bluer.

items.title: Diffuse and specular
items.text:
Diffuse Multiplier USD attribute inputs:diffuse Default 1 Specular Multiplier USD attribute inputs:specular Default 1

UE's Diffuse Scale and Specular Scale on the light. Set Specular Multiplier to 0 to remove a light's highlights and reflections while keeping its diffuse light. Dome lights ignore both, with a warning: UE's sky light has one environment.

items.title: Shadows
items.text:
Enable (Shadows) USD attribute inputs:shadow:enable Default on

Off, the light casts no shadows (UE's Cast Shadows). Shadow softness comes from the light's size. The realtime shadow method (Virtual Shadow Maps or ray-traced shadows) is a render setting: see Shadows. Per light, Cast Ray Traced Shadows, Contact Shadow Length and the shadow biases are on the Unreal Engine tab.

Not supported, each with a warning: Color (shadow:color: UE shadows are black), Distance and Falloff (shadow:distance, shadow:falloff: UE lights have no shadow length limit).

items.title: Spot lights
items.text:
Spotlight · applies ShapingAPI to a Sphere Light

Angle USD attribute inputs:shaping:cone:angle Default 90, degrees Softness USD attribute inputs:shaping:cone:softness Default 0

A Sphere Light with a cone of 90° or less becomes a UE Spot Light, as UE's USD importer makes it. Angle is the half-angle of the cone (UE's Outer Cone Angle). UE's spot lights stop at 88°: wider cones up to 90° render at 88°. A sphere light with a wider cone stays a point light.

Softness sets UE's Inner Cone Angle to \(\text{Angle} \times (1 - \text{Softness})\): 0 is a hard edge, 1 fades from the centre.

Cones on rect, disk and cylinder lights are ignored, with a warning: UE spots are point lights. Focus and Focus Tint are not read.

items.title: IES profiles
items.text:
IES · inputs:shaping:ies:file

Normalize USD attribute inputs:shaping:ies:normalize Default off Angle Scale USD attribute inputs:shaping:ies:angleScale Default 0

An IES file shapes a sphere, spot, rect or disk light, read with UE's IES loader and pointed along the light's −Z, as in Karma. The light is scaled by the profile's candela values, as UsdLux defines it; Normalize instead keeps the unshaped light's total power. Angle Scale stretches the profile's vertical angles with the UsdLux formula. IES profiles on distant and dome lights are ignored, with a warning.

items.title: Distant lights and the sun
items.text:
Angle USD attribute inputs:angle Default 0.53, degrees

The angular diameter of the sun disk (UE's Source Angle). Larger angles give softer shadows. With Normalize Power on, the illuminance stays the same.

A distant light is UE's Atmosphere Sun Light by default, so it lights UE's Sky Atmosphere when that is on. Distant lights never use MegaLights.

items.title: Dome lights and HDRIs
items.text:
Texture · inputs:texture:file

Format USD attribute inputs:texture:format Default automatic Pole Axis USD attribute poleAxis (DomeLight_1) Default scene Visible to Camera USD attribute unreal:visibleBackground Default on (Unreal Engine tab)

The dome becomes UE's sky light: it lights the scene, appears in reflections and draws the background. The texture is an HDR, EXR or ordinary image in latitude-longitude layout (latlong or automatic). HDR values are read as linear Rec.709; no OCIO conversion is applied. An image that is not 2:1 is stretched over the sphere, with a warning. Several domes add up into one environment.

The dome's transform, colour, intensity, exposure and colour temperature all apply. Pole Axis turns the dome alone: Z (or scene on a Z-up stage) puts the pole on +Z.

Visible to Camera off keeps the dome's light and reflections and renders black where camera rays escape, as Karma's dome does by default.

The dome is baked into a cube map of Environment Cube Resolution (default 128) pixels per face. Higher values keep more of the HDRI's detail and cost more memory and bake time.

Not supported on domes: light linking, light functions, IES, the diffuse and specular multipliers, and portals.

items.title: Mesh lights
items.text: A mesh with MeshLightAPI (Houdini's Geometry Light type) emits \(\text{Color} \times \text{Intensity} \times 2^{\text{Exposure}}\), colour temperature included, from its surface, as UE lights a scene from emissive surfaces. Normalize Power and light:materialSyncMode are ignored. The Path Tracer lights the surroundings from emissive meshes; Lumen lights them much less from small emitters (about 1% of the Path Tracer on a test wall). Use a rect or sphere light for a small emitter that must light its surroundings in realtime.

items.title: Light linking
items.text:
Light Linker LOP · collection:lightLink, collection:shadowLink

UE has three lighting channels, and hdUE gives each light-link collection one of them. That limits how many links a scene can have:

Scene Linked lights that work Every light is linked 3 distinct collections Some lights stay unlinked 2 distinct collections

Further linked lights light everything, with a warning. Lights whose collection includes everything keep every channel.

  • Links restrict direct light only. In Realtime, Lumen still bounces a linked light's indirect light onto every surface. The Path Tracer honours links exactly.
  • Dome lights have no channels: their light link is ignored, with a warning.
  • Shadow links: UE has no per-light shadow exclusion. An object stops casting shadows only when it is outside the shadow link of every light that casts shadows. With one light this is exact; with several, an object excluded from only some of them still shadows all of them (warned once).

items.title: Light filters and light functions
items.text:
UsdLux light filters (light:filters) are not supported, with a warning: UsdLux defines no standard filter types. UE's light functions are, as a gobo or cookie:

Light Function Texture · unreal:lightFunction:texture (Unreal Engine tab)

Filters a local or distant light with an image, in Realtime and in the Path Tracer. Light Function Scale sizes the projection (1024 cm by default). Light Function Material takes a cooked UE light function material instead. In Volumetric Fog, UE applies light functions from directional, point and spot lights only.

items.title: MegaLights
items.text:
MegaLights USD attribute unreal:megaLights Default on (Unreal Engine tab)

In Realtime, local lights are shaded by UE's MegaLights when the render setting MegaLights is on. Off on a light, that light uses UE's regular deferred lighting. Distant lights never use MegaLights; the Path Tracer has its own lighting.

items.title: Unreal Engine properties
items.text:
The Light LOP's Unreal Engine tab sets properties of the UE light component, by UE's names: unreal:light:<Property>. They apply after the UsdLux translation, so they can override it. The full list, with UE's defaults and ranges, is in Light properties. The ones that change the picture most:

Volumetric Scattering Intensity USD attribute unreal:light:VolumetricScatteringIntensity Default 1

How much the light scatters in Volumetric Fog, as a multiplier of its intensity. It changes the beam, not the lit surfaces.

Cast Volumetric Shadow USD attribute unreal:light:bCastVolumetricShadow Default off (distant lights: on)

Lets objects shadow the fog, so the ball cuts a dark shaft out of the beam. It costs GPU time per light.

Indirect Lighting Intensity USD attribute unreal:light:IndirectLightingIntensity Default 1

Scales the light's bounced light in Realtime (Lumen); 0 removes it. Direct light is unchanged. In the Bistro, the lamps' bounce lights the walls and ceiling.

Rect lights also take UE's barn doors: Barn Door Angle and Barn Door Length. hdUE shortens them to 0.1 cm by default, since UsdLux rect lights have none. Houdini's own barndoor parameters are not read.

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
Sun and sky

  1. Distant Light: Angle 0.53, Normalize Power on, Intensity 1, Exposure 4.
  2. Dome Light: an HDRI sky in Texture, Intensity 1, Exposure 0.
  3. For UE's physical sky instead of the HDRI, deactivate the dome and turn on Sky Atmosphere (Sky and clouds): the distant light lights it.

Soft studio key

  1. Rectangle Light, Width and Height 2, Normalize Power on.
  2. Intensity 1, Exposure 4.
  3. Enable Color Temperature on, Color Temperature 5600 for a daylight key.

Light shafts in fog

As in samples/docs/fog.usda.

  1. Render settings, Fog tab: Exponential Height Fog on, Fog Density 0.3, Volumetric Fog on.
  2. Sphere Light, Radius 0.05, Spotlight on, Angle 15, Softness 0.1.
  3. Intensity 1, Exposure 12.
