  4. Unreal Engine tab: Cast Volumetric Shadow on, so objects in the beam cast shafts.
  5. Raise Volumetric Scattering Intensity for a brighter beam without brighter surfaces.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
A DistantLight is almost black. Its intensity is the luminance of a 0.53° sun disk, not illuminance: intensity 1 gives 0.000067 lux. Turn on Normalize Power, so intensity is in lux.

Symptom Cause Fix A light gets brighter when you scale it up. Normalize Power is off: emission is per area. Turn on Normalize Power. A spot light lights a whole hemisphere. The cone is wider than 90°, so it is a point light. Set Angle to 90 or less. A linked light still brightens other objects in Realtime. Lumen's indirect light ignores links. Set the light's Indirect Lighting Intensity to 0, or render with the Path Tracer. A linked light lights everything, with a warning. More link collections than UE's three lighting channels. Merge collections, or link at most 3 (2 with unlinked lights). A small emissive mesh lights its surroundings only in the Path Tracer. Lumen lights little from small emitters. Add a rect or sphere light. An edited HDRI file does not update the viewport. A changed file alone sends no light update. Touch any dome parameter, or restart the render. The sky shows through gaps in a closed room. The dome is visible to camera rays that escape. Turn off Visible to Camera. The HDRI looks blurred in the background and reflections. Environment Cube Resolution is 128. Raise it to 512 or 1024. An unlit scene renders lit. Light Unlit Scenes adds a camera key and fill when the scene has no lights. Add a light, or turn off Light Unlit Scenes.

items.title: Unreal Engine and Karma
items.text:
• Intensity, exposure, normalize and size follow UsdLux. With a fully rough material under a normalized distant light, hdUE and Karma agree to 0.1%; glossy surfaces come out up to 1.4 times brighter in hdUE, from UE's specular model.
  • UE's Substrate shades diffuse with energy-preserving Oren-Nayar, where Karma's Preview Surface is Lambertian: surfaces seen at grazing angles render about 0.8 to 0.85 times Karma's.
  • On the Cornell box, mean brightness is 1.01 times Karma CPU's with the Path Tracer and 0.98 times with Lumen (Gallery).
  • The dome is visible to the camera by default in hdUE, not in Karma.
  • Disk and cylinder lights are UE approximations (a masked rect, a capsule).
  • Compare renderers with materials bound: unbound prims use each renderer's fallback (white in hdUE, as in UE's USD importer; grey in Karma).

items.title: Materials
items.text:
hdUE renders USD materials with Unreal Engine's material system, Substrate. A material reaches UE by one of four routes: a UsdPreviewSurface, a MaterialX Standard Surface or OpenPBR graph, an hdUE Substrate Builder graph, or a cooked UE asset with its own materials.

The shader ball with four material models: UsdPreviewSurface, then MaterialX Standard Surface with transmission, subsurface and sheen (Realtime).

items.title: Which route a material takes
items.text:
flowchart TD
    M("fal:fa-palette USD Material bound to a prim") --> Q1{"Substrate Builder graph<br/>(outputs:unreal:surface)?"}
    Q1 -- yes --> SB("fal:fa-hammer Prepared by UE's editor<br/>into a native Substrate material")
    Q1 -- no --> Q2{"MaterialX surface<br/>(outputs:mtlx:surface)?"}
    Q2 -- yes --> Q3{"Only nodes hdUE<br/>translates?"}
    Q3 -- yes --> T("fal:fa-zap Translated at render time<br/>(no compile)")
    Q3 -- no --> I("fal:fa-download Imported by UE's MaterialX importer<br/>(translated until ready)")
    Q2 -- no --> PS("fal:fa-zap UsdPreviewSurface<br/>translated at render time")
    N("fal:fa-box unreal:asset on a prim") --> NA("fal:fa-boxes Cooked UE mesh or Blueprint<br/>with its own UE materials")

    classDef host stroke-width:1px
    classDef hdue stroke-width:1px
    classDef unreal stroke-width:1px
    classDef output stroke-width:1px

    class M,N host
    class Q1,Q2,Q3,T,PS hdue
    class SB,I,NA unreal
Route You author Edits Page UsdPreviewSurface A USD Preview Surface VOP, or any UsdPreviewSurface shader Live: every input and texture Preview Surface MaterialX A Material Builder (Karma or MaterialX) with Standard Surface or OpenPBR Live for the nodes hdUE translates; other graphs are imported by UE in the background MaterialX surfaces Substrate Builder An hdUE Substrate Material Builder with Slabs, layers and mixes Values live; wiring changes compile in the background (seconds) Substrate Builder Cooked UE asset unreal:asset on a prim, pointing at a mesh or Blueprint in the runtime project The asset's own materials, edited in UE's editor below

A prim without a bound material renders its displayColor and displayOpacity, as UE's USD importer draws an unbound prim.

items.title: Which material model to choose
items.text:
• UsdPreviewSurface for plastics, metals, painted surfaces, cutout foliage and emissive surfaces. It costs one Substrate slab per pixel, the cheapest UE material.
  • MaterialX Standard Surface or OpenPBR for glass that refracts, skin and wax (subsurface), cloth (sheen), and thin leaves or fabric (thin-walled). A material with subsurface, sheen or coat costs several Substrate closures per pixel.
  • Substrate Builder for layered UE materials no USD model expresses: a water film over a surface, hair, eyes, Single Layer Water, thin film, decals and volume materials.
  • Cooked UE assets to reuse content that already lives in a UE project, with its UE materials unchanged.

items.title: Using it in Solaris
items.text:
1. Create the material in a Material Library LOP: a USD Preview Surface, a Karma Material Builder or MaterialX Standard Surface, or an hdUE Substrate Material Builder (TAB menu > hdUE).
  2. Assign it with Assign Material, or in the Material Library's Geometry Path.
  3. Edit any value. The viewport updates without a restart; a Substrate Builder rewire or an imported MaterialX graph takes a few seconds to compile first.

The three material settings are on hdUE Render Settings > Rendering > Materials:

Setting Default What it does Cooked MaterialX Library (unreal:materialxLibrary) empty A library.json of MaterialX materials cooked ahead of time; they replace the render-time translation Prepared Substrate Library (unreal:substrateLibrary) empty A library.json of Substrate Builder materials prepared ahead of time Prepare Edited Materials (unreal:substrateAutoPrepare) On Compiles Substrate Builder graphs and imports untranslatable MaterialX graphs in the background, in the viewport and in husk

items.title: MaterialX and Substrate
items.text: UE renders every material with Substrate. hdUE's runtime holds up to four closures and 128 bytes per pixel (Substrate's Adaptive GBuffer). A Preview Surface uses one slab; a Standard Surface with coat, sheen or subsurface uses UE's layered Substrate-StandardSurface function, which uses several.

items.title: Automatic import of untranslatable graphs
items.text:
A MaterialX graph with a node hdUE does not translate (the list; for example a mix of two textures, a multiply of two textures, noises, ramps, Houdini's own nodes) is imported by UE's own MaterialX importer, as UE's USD importer does for .mtlx files. With Prepare Edited Materials on:

  • the viewport keeps rendering the translation, with the untranslated inputs at their constants, and switches to the imported material when UE has compiled it (a few seconds);
  • husk imports the graphs a frame needs before rendering it.

Each graph is imported once per runtime: later renders, viewport or husk, reuse it. Numeric and colour inputs of the graph's nodes stay live after the import. Changing a filename, an integer or boolean input, or a value inside a Houdini node imports the graph again.

Importing needs UE's editor and the hdUE backend project on the machine. Without them, for example on a render node with a package install, the graph renders translated and hdUE prints why once.

items.title: Cooked MaterialX libraries
items.text:
For a farm without UE's editor, cook the MaterialX materials once and point Cooked MaterialX Library at the result:

.\scripts\Import-MaterialX.ps1 `
  -Source @('samples/materialx/standard_surface.mtlx') `
  -OutputDirectory out/materialx-import/review
.\scripts\Stage-Runtime.ps1

A cooked material replaces the translation for the materials it maps. A material whose graph changed since it was cooked fails a husk frame with the library's message. Published scalar and colour inputs stay live; structural changes need another import, cook and staging, and a restart.

items.title: Normal maps and UDIMs
items.text:
• Normal maps: connect a raw texture to UsdPreviewSurface normal through scale (2, 2, 2, 1) and bias (-1, -1, -1, 0), or to MaterialX normal through a normalmap node. Both expect OpenGL maps (+Y up), as USD and MaterialX do.
  • UDIMs: write <UDIM> in a texture's file name (wall.<UDIM>.exr). hdUE builds a UE streaming virtual texture of the tiles it finds, with no preparation.

Streamed texture data is cached on disk in %LOCALAPPDATA%\hdUE\VirtualTextureCache (or the folder in HDUE_VIRTUAL_TEXTURE_CACHE). The cache is never trimmed: delete the folder to reclaim space. A first load of a large scene writes tens of gigabytes there (41 GB for NVIDIA's Da Vinci Workshop).

In the Path Tracer, the first frames of a scene with UDIMs are a warm-up while UE streams the texture pages the camera sees. Accumulation starts once the pages stop changing.

items.title: Cooked native assets
items.text:
A Mesh, Xform or Scope prim with unreal:asset renders a cooked UE asset from the runtime project in its place: a Static Mesh, Skeletal Mesh, Actor Blueprint, Level, Sparse Volume Texture or Niagara System (see Game effects).

HoudiniUSD
  1. Add a Render Geometry Settings LOP and select the prims.
  2. On its Unreal Engine tab, set Native Asset to Set or Create and pick the asset from the menu.
def Xform "NativeMesh"
{
    custom string unreal:asset = "/Game/HdUE/SM_Nanite.SM_Nanite" # (1)!
}
  1. The asset's UE object path in the runtime project.

The asset keeps its UE materials, material slots, pivot and centimetre dimensions; the prim's transform places it. Without an asset catalog the menu lists the staged runtime's levels and the assets named with UE's prefixes (SM_, SK_, BP_, SVT_).

An asset from another UE project (a Marketplace pack, your game) is imported with the hdUE Unreal Asset LOP: pick the project and the asset, press Import, and UE's editor cooks it into the running runtime in the background, without a restart. The LOP also creates the prim that places it.

A Sparse Volume Texture (a VDB imported in UE's editor) renders as UE's Heterogeneous Volume, in both render modes. UE reads its VDB in centimetres, so a VDB written in metres needs a scale of 100 on the prim. For a VDB sequence, primvars:unreal:volume:frame picks the frame (0 is the first file); set it on the Render Geometry Settings LOP as Volume Frame, for example $F - 1.

Skeletal meshes render in their reference pose. Blueprint gameplay, time synchronisation and World Partition are limited.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Cause Fix A MaterialX material renders with flat values where a texture or noise should be The graph uses a node hdUE does not translate, and the import has not finished or cannot run Wait for the import (status bar), turn on Prepare Edited Materials, or check the warning naming the node husk fails a frame with a library message A material in the Cooked MaterialX or Prepared Substrate Library changed since it was prepared Prepare it again, or leave Prepare Edited Materials on Disk fills under %LOCALAPPDATA%\hdUE The virtual texture cache of UDIM scenes Delete VirtualTextureCache GPU memory runs out on a scene with many large textures Non-UDIM textures are held whole on the GPU Start with HDUE_UE_ARGS=-DPCVars=r.GlobalTextureLODBias=1 (halves every texture's width and height, a quarter of the memory), or -DPCVars=r.VT.EnableAutoImport=1 to stream textures of 4096 x 4096 and above as virtual textures, as UE's texture import does A native asset renders in the wrong place or size Its VDB or mesh is in centimetres, the stage in metres Scale the prim; the asset keeps UE's centimetre dimensions

items.title: Unreal Engine and Karma
items.text: hdUE translates materials as UE's USD importer and Interchange do: UsdPreviewSurface to UE's Preview Surface reference materials, MaterialX through UE's Substrate-StandardSurface functions and its MaterialX importer. Where UE and Karma differ (cutout opacity, glass reflections, transmission_depth), hdUE follows UE; each page lists the differences.

items.title: Substrate Builder
items.text:
The hdUE Substrate Material Builder builds a UE Substrate material in a Houdini VOP network: slabs, layers, mixes and UE's special BSDFs (hair, eye, water, thin film), wired like a Karma Material Builder. UE's editor compiles the network into a native UE material in the background; you keep working in the viewport.

Use it for what UsdPreviewSurface and MaterialX cannot express: a water film over a material, an iridescent metal, layered paints, hair, eyes, Single Layer Water, decals and volume materials. For ordinary surfaces, a Preview Surface or MaterialX material renders immediately and costs less.

Note

The Substrate Builder is experimental. Preparing a graph needs UE's editor and the hdUE backend project on the machine; a package install without them renders only graphs prepared elsewhere.

items.title: Using it in Solaris
items.text:
1. Add a Material Library LOP.
  2. Inside it, press Tab and choose hdUE > hdUE Substrate Material Builder. It starts with a Substrate Slab wired to the surface output.
  3. Assign the material with the Material Library's Geometry Path or an Assign Material LOP.
  4. Edit values: the viewport updates at once. Add or rewire nodes: the status bar shows the compile, then the new material replaces the old one, typically within 10 to 20 seconds.

The builder also works from /mat: point the Material Library's Material VOP at it. The hdUE shelf has the same tools:

Shelf tool What it does hdUE Substrate Material Builder Creates a builder in /mat Water Coating Example Creates a builder with a water layer over a MaterialX material (recipe) Author Substrate USD Adds a Material Library after the displayed LOP that authors the selected builder at /Looks/<name> and binds it to the Scene Graph selection

items.title: What updates live
items.text:
Edit Result Any numeric or colour value, a Scalar or Color Parameter, UV scale and offset, Normal Map strength, Extract Channel selection Live, no compile A Float Mask Primvar's name or the primvar's values Live, no compile Adding, removing or rewiring nodes, a parameter's name, a Slab's subsurface mode, parameter blending, a texture's file, colour space or address mode Compiled in the background (seconds) A Float Ramp or Color Ramp's keys Compiled in the background An image file's content, changed on disk without a USD edit Not detected: prepare the graph again

While a graph compiles, the viewport keeps the last valid image. A graph with a missing connection shows an error in the status bar and resumes when you reconnect it.

items.title: Nodes
items.text:
Surface nodes:

Node Inputs Use it for Substrate Slab Diffuse Albedo (0.18), F0 (0.04), Roughness (0.5), Normal, Mean Free Path (0), Subsurface mode (none, simple_volume); optional F90, Second Roughness and its weight, Emission Every ordinary surface: UE's Slab BSDF Substrate Vertical Layer Top, Base, Thickness (0.01 cm) A coat over a surface: varnish, water, dust Substrate Horizontal Mix Background, Foreground, Mix (0.5) Two materials side by side, by a mask Substrate Weight Surface, Weight (1) Partial coverage of a layer Substrate Add Two surfaces Light that adds, such as a glow over a surface Substrate Select Two surfaces, Select One surface or the other, by a threshold Substrate Unlit Emission Emission only, unlit Substrate Hair Base color, scatter, specular, roughness, backlit, tangent, emission UE's Hair BSDF Substrate Eye Diffuse color, roughness, cornea, iris normals, iris mask and distance, emission UE's Eye BSDF Substrate Single Layer Water Base color, metallic, specular, roughness, opacity, water albedo, extinction, phase, colour behind the water UE's water surface MaterialX Surface A USD material path An existing MaterialX material as a layer of the graph

Value nodes:

Node What it does Scalar Parameter, Color Parameter A named value, shared by every prim bound to the material Float Constant, Color Constant A value, editable live Float Multiply, Float Saturate, Float to Color Arithmetic Float Mask Primvar [0..1] A float primvar of the mesh, per point or face, for masks painted in SOPs Texture Sample An image: outputs RGB, RGBA, R, G, B, A. Colour space srgb (colour) or raw (data); address wrap, clamp or mirror; <UDIM> patterns UV Coordinates UV0 with Scale and Offset Extract Channel One channel of an RGBA input Normal Map Decodes a raw normal texture; Strength; Flip Green (on: OpenGL +Y maps; off: DirectX -Y maps) Metalness to Albedo and F0 Base color, metallic and specular, as in UE's Default Lit, into a Slab's Diffuse Albedo and F0 Haziness to Second Roughness A haze over the base roughness Transmittance to MFP A colour seen through a given thickness (cm), into a Slab's Mean Free Path Substrate Thin Film Thickness (micrometres) and IOR of a film, into a Slab's F0 and F90 Float Ramp, Color Ramp A Houdini ramp Blackbody A colour from a temperature in kelvin

Volume and decal outputs: Substrate Volumetric Fog Cloud, Volume Field and Substrate Convert To Decal (see below).

Unconnected inputs take UE's own defaults. Hair, Eye, Single Layer Water and Unlit must be the graph's output: UE's Substrate cannot layer or mix them.

items.title: Water film over a material
items.text:
The Water Coating Example shelf tool builds this graph. Set its MaterialX Surface to your material.

Node Values MaterialX Surface Material: the dry material, for example /Looks/Base Substrate Slab (water) Diffuse Albedo (0, 0, 0), F0 (0.0201, 0.0201, 0.0201) (IOR 1.33), Mean Free Path (1000000, 1000000, 1000000), Subsurface simple_volume Scalar Parameter WaterRoughness 0.08, into the water Slab's Roughness Scalar Parameter Coverage → Float Saturate 1 Float Mask Primvar Primvar wetness Float Multiply The saturated Coverage times the mask Substrate Weight Surface: the water Slab; Weight: the product Substrate Vertical Layer Top: the Weight; Base: the MaterialX Surface; Thickness 0.01 (cm)

Paint primvars:wetness (0..1) in SOPs to place the water. For the same effect without a graph, see Wet surfaces.

items.title: Iridescent metal
items.text:
From samples/substrate/bsdfs.usda, material Iridescent:

Node Values Metalness to Albedo and F0 Base color (0.9, 0.6, 0.2), Metallic 1, Specular 0.5 Substrate Thin Film F0 from the node above, F90 (1, 1, 1), IOR 1.44, Thickness 0.4 (µm) Haziness to Second Roughness Base roughness 0.2, Haziness 0.3 Substrate Slab Diffuse Albedo and F0, F90 from above; Roughness 0.2; Second Roughness and its weight from the haze

items.title: Wax
items.text:
Material Wax in the same file:

Node Values Transmittance to MFP Transmittance (0.9, 0.6, 0.4), Thickness 1 (cm) Substrate Slab Diffuse Albedo (0.9, 0.8, 0.6), F0 (0.04, 0.04, 0.04), Roughness 0.5, Mean Free Path from above, Subsurface simple_volume

items.title: Textured slab
items.text: samples/substrate/textures.usda: an sRGB checker into Diffuse Albedo, a packed texture's G (raw) through Extract Channel into Roughness, its A as a top layer's coverage, and a raw normal texture through Normal Map into the base Slab's Normal.

items.title: Volume materials
items.text: A builder whose output is a Substrate Volumetric Fog Cloud is a volume material. Create one with hdue_substrate.create(preset="volume") in Houdini's Python shell, and bind it to a Volume prim. It replaces hdUE's default volume material in the viewport, husk and usdview. Volume Field reads the volume's density grid or its emission field. Left unconnected, the Fog Cloud renders as the default volume material does.

items.title: Decal materials
items.text: A builder whose output is a Substrate Convert To Decal (hdue_substrate.create(preset="decal")) is a decal material: a UE Deferred Decal of the Slab wired to it, with Coverage as its opacity. Bind it to an UnrealDecal prim (decals).

items.title: Rendering with husk and on a farm
items.text:
Prepare Edited Materials (unreal:substrateAutoPrepare, hdUE Render Settings > Rendering > Materials, on by default) applies to husk too: husk prepares the graphs a frame needs before rendering it. A graph is prepared once per runtime folder and reused by every later render, viewport or husk; render nodes sharing a runtime prepare it once for the farm. Eight materials took 14 s to prepare and 8 s to render the first time, 8 s in all the second time.

For render nodes without UE's editor, prepare the materials on a workstation and set Prepared Substrate Library (unreal:substrateLibrary) to the result:

.\scripts\Prepare-Substrate.ps1 -InputUsd scene.usda -OutputDirectory out/prepared

With Prepare Edited Materials off, an unprepared graph shows the library's message in the viewport and fails a husk frame.

items.title: Background preparation
items.text:
• The status bar shows each compile and its errors.
  • Edits made while a graph compiles are kept: the newest graph is compiled next, and value edits apply to the result.
  • Returning to a graph already compiled in this session does not compile again.
  • Retry material preparation (on the hdUE settings subnet) retries a failed graph after you fix its cause, such as a missing file.

items.title: Limits
items.text:
• Opaque surfaces on USD meshes. No transmission or glass authoring, no displacement.
  • Up to 256 connected nodes, one MaterialX Surface and one Float Mask Primvar per graph.
  • Substrate's budget in hdUE's runtime: 4 closures and 128 bytes per pixel. The water example uses 3 closures and 92 bytes.
  • Textures read UV0 only. op: and opdef: images must be written to files first.
  • Parameters are shared by every prim bound to the material; use separate materials for separate values. Float masks vary per mesh.
  • Native UE asset materials and arbitrary UE material expressions are out of scope.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
Symptom Cause Fix The viewport keeps the old material after a rewire The graph is compiling, or failed Read the status bar; fix the error, then Retry material preparation The status bar reports a disconnected surface A required input or the output is not connected Reconnect it; preparation resumes A Normal Map connection is rejected The Texture Sample is srgb Set it to raw A normal map lights bumps from the wrong side A DirectX map with Flip Green on Turn Flip Green off A changed texture file does not update File contents are not tracked Prepare the graph again husk fails a frame with a library message The graph changed since the library was prepared, and Prepare Edited Materials is off Turn it on, or prepare the library again UE rejects a material at compile Substrate's graph rules (Hair, Eye, Water and Unlit cannot be layered), or the closure budget Make that BSDF the output; simplify the layering

How the graph is stored in USD and compiled is described in Substrate Builder internals.

items.title: Wet surfaces
items.text:
Wet Surface coats a material with a thin film of water, per prim, without editing the material: a clear layer with the reflectance of water (IOR 1.33) over the original surface. Amount and a painted mask primvar place it; Roughness sets how sharp its reflections are.

It works on MaterialX Standard Surface and OpenPBR materials cooked with a wet profile. For a water film on any graph, or other layers, build it in the Substrate Builder.

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
The bound material must be in a Cooked MaterialX Library imported with the wet profile:

.\scripts\Import-MaterialX.ps1 -Source @('looks.mtlx') -WetProfile -OutputDirectory out/materialx-wet
.\scripts\Stage-Runtime.ps1

Then set Cooked MaterialX Library (hdUE Render Settings > Rendering > Materials) to out/materialx-wet/library.json and restart Houdini on the staged runtime.

A material qualifies when it is:

  • a Standard Surface or OpenPBR surface;
  • opaque;
  • without an active subsurface, transmission or sheen (OpenPBR subsurface_weight, transmission_weight, fuzz_weight): each must be 0 and not connected.

Its normal maps, coat, metalness and UDIM textures stay as they are under the water.

items.title: Using it in Solaris
items.text:
1. Add a Render Geometry Settings LOP after the material assignment.
  2. Set Primitives to the meshes, their GeomSubsets, or a parent prim.
  3. On the Unreal Engine tab, under Wet Surface, set each control to Set or Create and turn Wet Surface on.
  4. Set Amount, Roughness and, for a painted mask, Mask Primvar.

From Houdini's Python shell, hdue_surface.create() adds this LOP for the prims selected in the Scene Graph Tree, with Wet Surface on.

Amount, roughness and mask edits are live: no compile. The Path Tracer restarts its accumulation.

items.title: Wet Surface
items.text:
Wet Surface USD attribute unreal:surface:wet:enabled Default off

Turns the coating on for the prim, its GeomSubsets and the meshes below it. Set it off on a child to keep that child dry.

items.title: Amount
items.text:
Amount USD attribute unreal:surface:wet:amount Default 1 Range 0 to 1

The fraction of the surface the water covers, multiplied by the mask. It is coverage, not water depth: 0.5 is a surface half covered, not a thinner film. 0 renders the original material.

items.title: Roughness
items.text:
Roughness USD attribute unreal:surface:wet:roughness Default 0.08 Range 0 to 1

Roughness of the water's surface. 0.08 is a still film; raise it for drizzled or dirty water.

items.title: Mask Primvar
items.text:
Mask Primvar USD attribute unreal:surface:wet:maskPrimvar Default empty

The base name of a float primvar on the mesh that scales the coverage, for example wetness for primvars:wetness. Empty covers the whole surface.

  • Paint the primvar in SOPs, as a point, vertex, primitive or detail attribute. Values are clamped to 0..1 and read as linear data.
  • Mask edits update the mesh's mask only, without re-sending its geometry.
  • A named primvar that is missing, has the wrong count or holds NaN is an error naming the prim.

To see the mask, turn on Preview Primvar mask on the hdUE settings subnet: the wet meshes show their coverage in grey levels.

items.title: In USD
items.text:
The four attributes can sit on a Mesh, a material-binding GeomSubset or any ancestor prim. Each mesh uses the nearest authored value, from the subset up through its ancestors. Two meshes sharing one material keep their own wet settings.

over "World"
{
    over "Asset"
    {
        custom bool unreal:surface:wet:enabled = true # (1)!
        custom float unreal:surface:wet:amount = 0.8
        custom float unreal:surface:wet:roughness = 0.08
        custom token unreal:surface:wet:maskPrimvar = "wetness" # (2)!

        over "Panel"
        {
            float[] primvars:wetness = [0, 0, 1, 1] ( # (3)!
                interpolation = "vertex"
            )
        }
    }
}
  1. Authored on the ancestor Asset: every mesh below it is wet unless a nearer prim sets it off.
  2. The primvar's base name, without primvars:.
  3. The mask: 0 dry, 1 wet, clamped to 0..1.

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
Look Amount Roughness Mask Primvar Rain-soaked surface 1 0.08 empty Puddles and dry patches 1 0.05 a painted wetness, 0 dry, 1 wet Damp, half-dried surface 0.5 0.2 empty

The water does not darken the material under it. For a soaked look, darken and smooth the base material too (lower its base colour and roughness).

items.title: Limits
items.text:
• One water layer per material, over the whole original surface.
  • Opaque Standard Surface and OpenPBR materials only: no glass, subsurface, sheen, cutouts, hair or native UE asset materials.
  • Masks are float primvars only; image masks need the Substrate Builder.
  • Meshes with a wet surface are not displaced.
  • The GPU may store the mask at 8 bits per value (steps of 1/255).

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
Symptom Cause Fix An error "wet profile unavailable" naming the prim The bound material is not in the Cooked MaterialX Library, or was imported without -WetProfile Import it with -WetProfile and select that library "Wet v1 does not support an active subsurface input" (or transmission, sheen) The material uses a lobe the wet profile does not cover Set that input to 0, or use a Substrate Builder graph "missing float wet mask" Mask Primvar names a primvar the mesh does not have, or not a float Fix the name (no primvars: prefix) or the attribute type "use the mask base name without 'primvars:'" The name includes the namespace Write wetness, not primvars:wetness The wet surface looks like the dry one Amount 0, or the base already has a glossy coat with the same roughness Check Amount; raise the base's roughness to compare

Implementation details are in Wet surface internals.

items.title: Writing the user guide
items.text: The user guide is written for the artist or TD rendering with hdUE in Houdini, not for hdUE's developers. Its model is Autodesk's Arnold User Guide: short reference pages built around images, and tutorials named after the result they produce. Implementation details (how hdUE drives UE, why a code path exists) go to the Developer pages.

items.title: Two kinds of pages
items.text:
Reference pages describe one feature: a light, the camera, a material model, a render setting group.

  1. Title, then one or two sentences saying what the feature is, then a hero image.
  2. Using it in Solaris: the LOP or parameter that sets it, as numbered steps when there is more than one.
  3. Parameters: one ## section per parameter, in the order the UI shows them. Each section:
    • the parameter's label in bold, its unreal:* attribute or USD property, and its default;
    • one to three sentences: what it does, its unit, what raising it costs;
    • a figure when the effect is visible: a slider for two values, a scrubber for more, the default marked;
    • a tip or a note only when there is a symptom, a cause and a fix to give.
  4. Recipes ("How to get…"): exact values for an effect, ready to type in.
  5. Troubleshooting: symptom, cause, fix. One line each where possible.
  6. Unreal Engine and Karma: where hdUE follows UE and where the result differs from Karma, briefly.

Tutorials produce one result: "Lighting a room", "Removing noise", "Glass and liquids".

  1. The final image first, then what the reader will build and roughly how long it takes.
  2. The starting scene: a file in samples/ the reader opens.
  3. ## sections, one per stage (Lights, Materials, Render settings, Final render). Each holds short imperative steps with exact values, each followed by one sentence of why.
  4. A render after each stage that changes the image.
  5. Final render settings, as a short list.

items.title: Images
items.text:
• Every comparison is rendered by scripts/render_docs_images.py from a scene in samples/, so a rebuild refreshes it. No hand-made screenshots of renders.
  • One small scene per kind of effect, chosen so the effect reads: SideFX's lookdev shader ball (docs/lookdev.usda) for materials, SideFX's Veach planks (docs/veach.usda) for light size against roughness, the chrome ball and box (docs/lights.usda) for light types and shadows, the beam in fog (docs/fog.usda) for scattering, the row of rubber toys (docs/row.usda) for focus, the Bistro (docs/bistro.usda, a local download) for interiors and global illumination, the Cornell box for render settings. Keep the camera and lighting fixed across a page.
  • Captions are the value only ("0.5"), with "(default)" after the default. Add the render time when the setting costs time.
  • Two values: before/after slider. Three to six: the picture with a strip of thumbnails (tap one, or swipe the picture). Pick values that span the useful range, not the full numeric range.
  • A figure spec that shows one setting names it: "settings": ["unreal:postProcess:BloomIntensity"]. generate_render_settings.py and generate_node_docs.py then show the figure under that setting in the reference and on the node pages. The reference's own figures (docs/figures/ref-*.json) come from one table in scripts/generate_reference_figures.py: add a row there, run it, render the new figure, then rerun both generators.
  • Scenes built in Houdini are written by scripts, so they can be rebuilt: scripts/build_docs_box.py (the light study's bevelled box) and scripts/build_docs_volumes.py (the mist volumes).
  • Houdini UI screenshots only where the step cannot be said in words (a network to wire, a menu to find), and cropped to the panel. They live in docs/images/houdini/, taken in a Launch-Houdini.ps1 -InputUsd samples/cornell/cornell.usda session with the window at 1920 × 1080, Unreal Engine picked in the Scene Viewer, and each pane grabbed from the screen (a floating pane for a wider parameter editor); crop out personal shelves and menus.

items.title: Parameters and formulas
items.text:
• A page's own parameters sit in the parameter grid the node pages use: the name beside a facts strip (USD attribute, Default, Range, badges such as "Realtime only"). Copy a block from docs/lights.md: <div class="hdue-params" markdown>, one hdue-param per parameter, each value in <dd markdown="span"> so code and links work. The reference and node pages write the same markup from generate_render_settings.py and generate_node_docs.py.
  • A formula is math, not prose with ×: $\text{Intensity} \times 2^{\text{Exposure}}$ inline, or $$ … $$ on lines of its own for one the sentence leads to. MathJax typesets it (Zensical's math setup, pymdownx.arithmatex).

items.title: Diagrams
items.text:
Every Mermaid diagram looks the same: docs/assets/hdue-mermaid.js draws it in the site's colours, and docs/architecture.md is the model.

  • Rounded nodes, A("…"), with a Lucide icon before the text: "fal:fa-monitor Solaris viewport" (fal is Lucide here, the prefix Mermaid reads in a label). Decisions stay diamonds, {"…?"}, without an icon.
  • Colour comes from four classes, never from a style or a colour in a classDef: host for Houdini and USD, hdue for the delegate, unreal for Unreal Engine, output for images and files. Declare them with classDef host stroke-width:1px (and the same for the others), then class S,V host.
  • Group by process or side in a subgraph with the same class and an icon in its title.
  • The site's gallery and README are rendered by scripts; a diagram is the one figure written by hand.

items.title: Houdini node reference
items.text: docs/reference/nodes/ is generated: hython scripts/generate_node_docs.py turns each digital asset's help card (its Help section, written by build_render_settings_hda.py and build_substrate_hda.py, and shown by Houdini on F1) into a page like SideFX's node help, and writes its navigation into zensical.toml. Run it after rebuilding an asset; to change a node's page, change its builder's help text, never the generated Markdown.

items.title: Writing
items.text:
• Second person, present tense, imperative for steps: "Set Exposure to 2."
  • Sentences under about 20 words. One idea per sentence.
  • Name parameters as the UI does, in bold, with the attribute in code the first time: Fog Density (unreal:heightFog:FogDensity).
  • Numbers, not adjectives: "doubles the render time", "1 stop brighter", not "slower", "brighter".
  • Say what UE does, citing the UE setting it maps to. Do not explain hdUE's internals on a user page.
  • Every claim must be true of the current build. When a behaviour is not verified, leave it out or say so.
  • No marketing words. No "simply", "just", "easily".

items.title: Geometry internals
items.text: Implementation notes behind the user pages on meshes, subdivision, displacement, Nanite, volumes, fog and sky.

items.title: Nanite
items.text:
Meshes from the native asset catalog render with Nanite when their cooked asset has Nanite data (unreal:requireNanite enforces it). Static meshes hdUE builds from Hydra, and instancer prototypes, become Nanite meshes too. Batch renders (husk) build Nanite data and Lumen cards before the first frame; interactive hosts (Houdini's viewport, which start UE with HDUE_INIT_INTERACTIVE) first draw regular static meshes, build both on worker threads, then swap each mesh, one per frame. Those first-pass meshes are full resolution, so they are made smallest first only while their estimated GPU memory stays under r.HdUE.InteractiveFirstPassMemory (2,048 MB; Windows also charges a process's D3D12 allocations to its commit); the other meshes appear when their build is swapped in, as UE draws no static mesh while it compiles (UStaticMeshComponent::ShouldCreateRenderState). Copies of a mesh in later uploads draw its first pass too. The viewport keeps drawing while builds are pending and converges once the last one is in. A mesh's root page stays on the GPU and its other pages stream from system memory when the view needs them, as UE streams a cooked mesh's pages from disk (UE's non-editor streaming reads only cooked files, so Apply-ResidencyPatch.ps1 compiles in the editor's path for pages in memory; building). The pool is UE's (r.Nanite.Streaming.StreamingPoolSize, 512 MB), and a view whose unique geometry overcommits it draws Nanite's coarser clusters, as UE does (r.Nanite.Streaming.QualityScale.*): 16 grids of 1M triangles in a 512-pixel frame differ from fully resident pages by 0.6% of the mean brightness at 512 MB and match them (within run-to-run noise) at 1,900 MB. A Nanite mesh's LOD 0, which draws where Nanite does not and which ray tracing (Lumen's, the Path Tracer) traces, is the Nanite builder's fallback mesh, as UE's static mesh build makes it (BuildNanite, StaticMeshBuilder.cpp), at UE's default relative error (Fallback Target Auto: r.Nanite.Builder.FallbackTargetAutoRelativeError, 1); a mesh that ends up without Nanite (a translucent material, a full root page pool) keeps all its triangles. Identical meshes share one static mesh, as UE's USD importer shares one asset between identical prims (UUsdAssetCache3, keyed by a hash of the mesh, USDGeomMeshTranslator.cpp). Animated or edited meshes stay dynamic. HDUE_NANITE=0 turns Nanite off.

Building Nanite data is most of a scene's mesh conversion, so builds are cached across processes, as UE's derived data cache keeps a static mesh's (FStaticMeshRenderData::Cache, StaticMesh.cpp): one file per mesh in Saved/NaniteCache (under %LOCALAPPDATA%\hdUE, or HDUE_USER_DIR), keyed by the Nanite builder's version, the fallback's relative error and the mesh's vertices and triangles, its streaming pages and fallback mesh appended after the resources, and removed after a week unused. UE's cache itself does not run in a cooked runtime such as hdUE's (GetCache() creates none where RequiresCookedData(), DerivedDataCacheModule.cpp; cooked games get their derived data from the cook, and these meshes only exist at render time). 450 meshes of 9,800 triangles: 10.5 s to build, 0.7 s from the cache (75 MB), the same image. UE keeps all of a scene's Nanite root pages in one GPU buffer of at most 2 GB on NVIDIA (4 GB on AMD) less its 512 MB streaming pool, and ends the process when one more does not fit; each mesh keeps one root page there, so it holds tens of thousands of meshes; hdUE stops attaching Nanite data at 90% of that pool and renders the remaining meshes as regular static meshes, with a warning in UE's log. In Houdini's viewport the card and Nanite builds start while their memory fits, as UE's editor schedules asset builds (FMemoryBoundQueuedThreadPoolWrapper, AssetCompilingManager.cpp): each is estimated at 7 times its mesh data (UStaticMesh::GetBuildRequiredMemoryEstimate) and holds that until its mesh is swapped in. r.HdUE.MeshBuildMaxMemoryUsage (GB, 0 by default) caps them below the available memory, as UE's Editor.AsyncAssetCompilationMaxMemoryUsage does. In a Windows job with a memory limit (a farm container), the available memory is the job's: the runtime sets UE's memory.WindowsPlatformMemoryUseContainerMemory.

This sets the scale hdUE renders from Hydra geometry. NVIDIA's Da Vinci Workshop (617M triangles, 6,750 meshes, of which 1,700 distinct) renders under husk at 960 x 540 in the realtime mode with a job memory peak of 22 GB: 11 minutes with an empty Nanite cache (3.6 GB written), 2 minutes from it (see architecture). Its lights are bright (exposure 1 to 7 on intensities of 100 to 2,000) and its camera authors no exposure, so the image needs an exposure of its own. In Houdini's viewport, in render purpose, it converges in about 3.5 minutes with a job memory peak of 30 to 33 GB. UE's own runtime USD import of the shot passed 62 GB, and its editor import crashes on one of the scene's UDIM textures. Cooked UE static meshes referenced through unreal:asset (cooked native assets) keep their geometry out of the host: their pages stream from their cooked files, as in a UE project.

items.title: Displacement
items.text:
The Preview Surface displacement input and MaterialX ND_displacement_float (displacement × scale) move the mesh's points along their normals by that distance, in the mesh's object space and units, before the mesh is uploaded, so Lumen, the Path Tracer and Nanite see the same surface. A textured displacement first dices the mesh uniformly: each triangle splits into four per level, up to about one triangle per two texels and at most about a million triangles per mesh. Normals are then recomputed from the displaced surface; a UV seam splits the surface only where the texture differs across it, and hard edges open. A constant displacement moves the points without dicing. Meshes with wet-surface effects are not displaced. Displacement is not adaptive (Karma dices by screen size). UE's Nanite tessellation and World Position Offset are not used: UE 5.8's ray-traced geometry, which the Path Tracer renders, ignores both. MaterialX vector displacement is not translated.

Dicing is HdUEDiceLevels in src/hydra/displacement.h: levels until the triangle count reaches \(\min(\text{texels} / 2,\ 2^{20})\).

items.title: Meshes and instancing
items.text:
Generic Hydra translation supports meshes, cameras, materials, and distant, sphere, rect, disk, cylinder, and dome lights.

Meshes reach UE indexed: the triangle corners of a point share one vertex unless a face-varying normal, UV, color or wet mask differs between them, so UE holds about as many vertices as the USD mesh has points. A mesh UE cannot take (more than about 715 million vertices, or broken indices) is skipped with a warning naming it in the UE log; the rest of the scene still loads.

Material-binding GeomSubsets partition triangles by their original USD face while preserving UVs, normals, transforms, visibility, and picking paths. Unassigned faces retain the mesh material; overlapping or invalid material subsets are rejected. Subset edits and removals update the generated meshes.

Meshes follow USD's doubleSided, as UE's USD importer does: single-sided meshes draw a one-sided twin of their material and cull their back faces. unreal:cullBackface = 0 renders every mesh on both sides, as Karma does (its karma:object:cull_backface defaults to off). Karma's per-object karma:object:cull_backface primvar is not read; doubleSided is the per-mesh switch.

Missing or zero normals are generated from area-weighted vertex adjacency before subset partitioning, so material boundaries share the same shading normals. Authored normals are retained. Author explicit face-varying normals or split vertices where hard edges are required; normal generation does not apply subdivision creases.

Hydra instancers (USD PointInstancers, including nested ones) are translated: each prototype mesh is built once as a runtime static mesh, or uses its native cooked asset, and drawn through one instanced static mesh component with per-instance transforms composed as in hdEmbree. Preview Surface and ID materials are cooked with instanced-static-mesh usage; prepared MaterialX or Substrate materials need that usage too before they render on instances. Instanceable references (USD native instancing) reach the delegate as Hydra instancers too, in Solaris as elsewhere. Instances hidden by invisibleIds or deactivated by inactiveIds are not drawn (Hydra leaves them out of the instance indices), orientations (half) and orientationsf (float) are normalized as UsdGeomPointInstancer does, an instance-rate primvar that a bound Preview Surface's base colour reads through a primvar reader colours each instance (as an unbound prototype's displayColor does), and volumes under an instancer are drawn once per instance (sharing one density grid on the Hydra side). UE instances are FTransforms, which hold no shear, so instances whose transform shears (a rotated prototype under a non-uniform instance scale) are baked into the vertices of one companion mesh per prototype, as a sheared mesh outside an instancer is; the others stay UE instances (instancer/shear). With motion blur, the companion is baked again per sub-frame. A prototype with a native cooked asset has no vertices to bake, so its sheared instances render without shear, with a warning.

Implicit Cube, Sphere, Cone, Cylinder, Capsule and Plane prims are converted to meshes by Hydra's implicit-surface scene index (HdUE_ImplicitSurfaceSceneIndexPlugin), as for hdEmbree.

Points render as one shared sphere instanced per point, sized by widths (0.1 when unauthored). BasisCurves render as six-sided tubes with flat end caps on open curves: linear curves follow their vertices, cubic Bezier, B-spline and Catmull-Rom curves are evaluated in their basis, and widths set the diameter (0.01 when unauthored). Points and curves under a PointInstancer are drawn once per instance.

Hair. BasisCurves with the constant primvar primvars:unreal:groom = 1 (Hydra passes curves their primvars, not other attributes; Hair Strands on the Unreal Engine tab of Render Geometry Settings LOPs, on the curves or an ancestor) render as UE hair strands instead of tubes: hdUE builds the groom asset UE's importer would make, with UE's own groom builder, from the evaluated curve points and per-point widths: one group, guides generated from every strand (no simulation), drawn by a groom component, in realtime and in the Path Tracer (its strand geometry). Its groom_* primvars become the groom's attributes under the same names, as UE's USD importer reads them (USDGroomConversion.cpp; HdueGroomAttribute), with colour, roughness and AO spread per point since UE's builder reads them only there. The strands draw with a bound material that has UE's hair strands usage (a prepared Substrate Hair or MaterialX chiang_hair_bsdf graph; HairUsage.h sets the usage when it prepares one), else with M_HdUEHair (UE's HairDefaultMaterial copied, its Base Color and Roughness switched to a bound translated material's constants or to the Hair Attributes node) when there is a colour or roughness to show, else with UE's default hair material. Curves under an instancer build one groom asset drawn by one component per instance. UE's groom physics does not run.

Mesh UVs come from the primvar that the bound material's UsdPrimvarReader_float2 reads (varname, such as st, or map1 from 3ds Max exports), or from st when the material names none. Each texture reads the UV set its own st input names (also through a UsdTransform2d): the mesh carries every UV primvar its material reads, up to four, chosen through its own binding (else its first bound GeomSubset's). The UV transform is still one per material, from the first textured input.

Unbound geometry uses displayColor/displayOpacity. A displayColor that varies (uniform, vertex or face-varying on meshes, per point on Points, per vertex or per curve on BasisCurves, per instance on a PointInstancer, from the nearest of nested instancers that authors it) is multiplied into M_PreviewSurface as vertex colors or per-instance custom data. Dynamic mesh vertex colors are stored in 8 bits, so very dark colors band slightly. Varying displayOpacity, and colors on meshes that also carry a wet-surface mask (the mask reuses the vertex colors), are not translated. The unbound default is a Preview Surface (roughness 0.5) whose base colour is displayColor, as UE's USD importer draws unbound prims (its DisplayColor reference material feeds the vertex colour straight into Base Color); a prim with no displayColor is white, the vertex colour UE's importer gives it (Karma draws such prims grey).

items.title: Volumes
items.text:
Volumes (Houdini build) render the density field, or the first field, of a Volume prim as a UE heterogeneous volume with M_HdUEVolume (albedo 0.8; density is extinction per scene unit). The field can be:

  • an OpenVDBAsset pointing to a .vdb file, read with OpenVDB;
  • an unsaved SOP volume in the Solaris viewport: OpenVDBAsset or HoudiniFieldAsset prims whose filePath is an op: SOP layer. hdUE takes the cooked geometry from Houdini's locked-geometry registry, or cooks the SOP;
  • a .bgeo / .bgeo.sc file, which is where the USD Render ROP writes native Houdini volumes for husk.

From Houdini geometry, the VDB or Houdini volume primitive named after fieldName is used, else the fieldIndex-th one. Grids are densified over their active bounding box and point-sampled with a stride above 512 voxels per axis. A bound Substrate Builder volume material replaces M_HdUEVolume in Houdini's viewport (volume materials); other volume materials, tapered Houdini volumes and frustum VDBs are not translated.

Emission. The constant primvar primvars:unreal:emissionField on the Volume prim (Hydra passes a volume its primvars, not other attributes; Houdini detail attributes become them) names another of its fields (temperature, flame, ...) that emits light: UE's BlackBody of the field's value times primvars:unreal:temperatureScale (kelvin per unit, 1 by default), times primvars:unreal:emissionIntensity (1). The field is sampled at the density's voxels (nearest voxel, 0 outside its own grid). As in UE, nothing emits unless asked: UE's heterogeneous volumes emit what their material makes of an imported grid, and UE prescribes no field or mapping. Both modes render it.

Measured against Karma: in realtime, a fog's brightness is within about 15%. Volumes shadow the scene in both modes. In realtime this is UE's heterogeneous volume Shadow Casting (r.HeterogeneousVolumes.Shadows, on in this project), with one shadow projection fitted around the volumes (r.HeterogeneousVolumes.Shadows.Cascades 0: with Virtual Shadow Maps, UE's default single cascade left the volume's shadow map empty). As in UE 5.8, the shadow reaches lights shaded by UE's deferred light loop: distant lights, and local lights with unreal:megaLights off (MegaLights does not support heterogeneous volumes); a light also needs Cast Volumetric Shadow (unreal:light:bCastVolumetricShadow, on by default for distant lights). The Path Tracer casts it (optical depth 1.4 against Karma's 1.9) and includes multiple scattering. It re-voxelizes volumes for each frame; batch renders use the shading rate 1 and 512 MB that UE's docs recommend for cinematic renders (r.HeterogeneousVolumes.{Frustum,Ortho}Grid.ShadingRate, .MaxBottomLevelMemoryInMegabytes; 4 and 128 MB by default, which made silhouettes blocky).

items.title: Fog, sky and clouds
items.text:
The Fog tab of hdUE Render Settings places UE's Exponential Height Fog in the scene, as an Exponential Height Fog actor does in a level. Exponential Height Fog (unreal:heightFog) turns it on; Fog Height (unreal:heightFogHeight, scene units along the stage's up axis) is the actor's height, where the density is Fog Density. Every other parameter is a UExponentialHeightFogComponent property (unreal:heightFog:<Property>), generated from the engine source with UE's categories, names, ranges and defaults; distances are in UE centimeters, as in UE's Details panel. UE's USD importer imports no fog, so there is no USD schema to follow.

Volumetric Fog (unreal:heightFog:bEnableVolumetricFog) gives lit, shadowed fog and light shafts: lights scatter into it by their Volumetric Scattering Intensity. UE's Path Tracer renders the height fog only with Volumetric Fog on (PathTracing.cpp), and limits its density growth below the fog height with r.PathTracing.FogDensityClamp. The fog is part of the scene, so colour AOVs show it too. Changing a fog setting rebuilds the fog, which restarts volumetric fog's temporal history.

items.title: Scene prims for fog, sky and clouds
items.text: The height fog, sky atmosphere and clouds can also be placed by prims, as their actors are placed in a UE level, so they live in the scene rather than in the render settings: UnrealExponentialHeightFog, UnrealSkyAtmosphere and UnrealVolumetricCloud (codeless schemas in resources/generatedSchema.usda, generated with the same properties as the render settings' tabs, with UE's constructor defaults as fallbacks). Their attributes are the render settings' names: unreal:heightFog:<Property>, unreal:skyAtmosphere:<Property>, unreal:volumetricCloud:<Property>. A prim takes the place of its render settings counterpart (whose switch and properties are then ignored); UE draws one of each, so the first visible prim of a kind by path is used. A height fog's height is the prim's world position along the up axis (its density is Fog Density there), as an Exponential Height Fog actor's Z; a sky atmosphere's position counts only when its Transform Mode places the planet at the component. hdUE Height Fog, hdUE Sky Atmosphere and hdUE Volumetric Cloud (TAB menu > hdUE > Visual Effects) create or edit them, with the render settings' Fog and Sky properties, each at Do Nothing (the prim's fallback, UE's default) until turned on. render_settings/height_fog_prim checks the fog, its height and that the prim wins over the render settings' fog; render_settings/sky_atmosphere_prim the sky and, in realtime, the clouds.

items.title: Local fog volumes
items.text:
An UnrealLocalFogVolume prim is a UE Local Fog Volume: a sphere of fog that fades out radially, combined with a height fog along its up axis. hdUE Local Fog Volume (TAB menu > hdUE > Visual Effects, integrations/houdini/otls/hdue_localfogvolume.hda) creates or edits one, as Karma Sky Atmosphere does Karma's sky: a primitive path, Houdini's transform section (Uniform Scale is the radius, 1 by default: UE's volume is a sphere of radius 500 cm, scaled uniformly), and UE's properties, each with a control menu. In Create mode every property is authored, at UE's defaults too (Houdini's viewport is not told about an attribute added to an existing prim, so one authored only once changed would not update it); Edit mode changes existing prims (Houdini). The prim type is a codeless schema shipped with the delegate (resources/generatedSchema.usda, generated by scripts/generate_render_settings.py from ULocalFogVolumeComponent): an Xformable whose attributes are unreal:localFogVolume:<Property>, with UE's defaults as fallbacks. The unit sphere of the prim's local space is UE's base volume; its local up axis is the stage's.

As in UE:

  • Local fog volumes render in realtime only; UE's Path Tracer ignores them.
  • UE draws none nearer than 10 m to the camera (r.LocalFogVolume.GlobalStartDistance, in Engine Quality's console variables or as unreal:cvar:r:LocalFogVolume:GlobalStartDistance); a volume's own Start Distance can only push it further.
  • Height Fog Density 0 hides the whole volume: UE combines the radial and height fog as the product of their coverages (LocalFogVolumeCommon.ush), so use a small value for radial fog alone.
  • With Volumetric Fog on the height fog, the volumes are also lit and shadowed through it (r.LocalFogVolume.RenderIntoVolumetricFog).

The Sky tab places UE's Sky Atmosphere and Volumetric Cloud, as their actors do in a level. Sky Atmosphere (unreal:skyAtmosphere) turns on UE's physical sky; every USkyAtmosphereComponent property is unreal:skyAtmosphere:<Property>, generated like the fog's (UE's atmosphere is in kilometres, its planet top at the world origin by default). Distant lights light it as Atmosphere Sun Lights, UE's default for a directional light (unreal:light:bAtmosphereSunLight, index 0 the sun and 1 the moon). Without a DomeLight, hdUE adds a Sky Light with Real Time Capture so the sky lights the scene, as UE's default level has: Lumen needs it, and UE's Path Tracer renders the atmosphere only through it (or with Reference Atmosphere, Path Tracing tab). A DomeLight's environment takes its place.

Volumetric Cloud (unreal:volumetricCloud, unreal:volumetricCloud:<Property>) needs the Sky Atmosphere. Its default material is UE's /Engine/EngineSky/VolumetricClouds/m_SimpleVolumetricCloud_Inst, cooked with the runtime from this version on (a runtime staged before has no cloud material); unreal:volumetricCloud:Material takes another cooked material. UE's Path Tracer renders clouds with Reference Atmosphere on.

items.title: Materials internals
items.text: The user pages are Materials, Preview Surface, MaterialX surfaces, Opacity and glass and COP textures. This page records how hdUE implements them. The translation is src/hydra/materials.cpp (constants and textures into HdUEMaterialData) and the parent selection Scene.cpp in the backend (M_PreviewSurface, M_PreviewSurfaceMasked, M_PreviewSurfaceTranslucent, M_StandardSurface[Masked][Thin], M_StandardSurfaceTranslucent[Thin], each with a VT twin for virtual textures).

items.title: Prepared MaterialX
items.text:
Prepared MaterialX rendering uses UE's editor-side Interchange importer to create native Substrate materials, followed by cook and staging. The runtime does not load USD or MaterialX importers. The usdview integration maps source materials to prepared native assets and applies supported public parameter edits.

.\scripts\Import-MaterialX.ps1 `
  -Source @('samples/materialx/standard_surface.mtlx','samples/materialx/open_pbr_surface.mtlx') `
  -OutputDirectory out/materialx-import/review
.\scripts\Stage-Runtime.ps1
.\scripts\Launch-Usdview.ps1 `
  -InputUsd samples/materialx/showcase.usda -CameraPath /Camera `
  -MaterialXLibrary out/materialx-import/review/library.json

Inline USD graphs use Import-UsdMaterialX.ps1 with samples/materialx/inline.usda and a fresh output directory. The supported subset includes Standard Surface, OpenPBR, color/vector/float images, float normal-map strength, UV0 coordinates, color/float multiplication, and float inversion. Nested NodeGraphs and interfaces are resolved during preparation. Cycles, unresolved images, incompatible connections and extra UV sets are rejected; displacement and volume outputs are exported with the surface. Imported materials are marked for instanced static meshes so they render on PointInstancer prototypes; that flag is set by the importer but has not been exercised on this branch.

Published scalar and color inputs can be edited without resending geometry. Structural or source-file changes require preparation, cook, staging, and restart. Dependency hashes detect stale registries. Texture overrides require prepared native texture paths.

The experimental Substrate Builder adds Houdini VOP authoring, typed USD graphs, and preparation into native UE Substrate materials. Texture Sample, UV Coordinates, Extract Channel, and Normal Map nodes connect images directly to Slabs and layer masks; explicit UDIM patterns use streaming virtual textures. Numeric/color inputs, UV transforms, channel selection, and normal controls update live through automatically generated material parameters. Node and wiring edits compile/cook in the background and replace the material in the same Houdini/UE process when ready. The earlier wet surface layer draft records the original fixed-profile proposal.

usdview and Solaris both accept the cooked registry through -MaterialXLibrary. In Solaris, the same file is the unreal:materialxLibrary render setting (hdUE Render Settings, Rendering > Materials > Cooked MaterialX Library), else the local runtime profile's materialx_library key. Preparation runs in Houdini's viewport; husk applies them as the viewport does: the delegate runs the same library code on the stage it renders (hdue_batch.py, through Houdini's Python) before each frame, and a material the library maps whose graph changed since its preparation fails the frame with the library's message instead of rendering a fallback. Bindings follow reference composition and validate the graph before applying native assets and parameters on the owner thread. A MaterialX material the library does not map renders through hdUE's own render-time translation, as with no library selected. Restart with a staged runtime containing the prepared materials; importing alone does not add them to an already running UE process.

items.title: Automatic import of untranslatable graphs
items.text:
A MaterialX graph hdUE's render-time translation cannot express (a surface other than Standard Surface, OpenPBR or UsdPreviewSurface, or an input reached through a node outside its list: mix, place2d, noises, ramps, Houdini's own nodes, ...) is prepared through UE's MaterialX importer, as UE's USD importer translates MaterialX it finds in .mtlx files (MaterialXUSDShadeMaterialTranslator.cpp, Interchange). The live preparation that prepares Substrate Builder graphs does it, under the same render setting, Prepare Edited Materials (unreal:substrateAutoPrepare): the viewport keeps rendering the translation while UE's editor imports the graph in the background, then shows the imported material; husk prepares the graphs a frame needs before rendering it. Off, the graph renders translated, with the inputs it cannot translate at their constants. So does a graph whose preparation fails, in husk too: a machine without UE's editor and this repository's backend project (a package) cannot prepare, and prints why once. scripts/live_materials.py decides which graphs need it (usd_materialx_graph.needs_import, the node list of materials.cpp).

The graph is written as a MaterialX document (export_usd_materialx.py): MaterialX's standard nodes as they are, and Houdini's nodes (its library under houdini/materialx/libraries, node graphs over standard nodes) flattened into theirs, since UE reads only the standard libraries. A connected input's value is dropped: Houdini's generated node graphs carry both, which MaterialX 1.39's validation rejects. Every node graph UE does not translate whole (its CategoriesToSkip) is flattened too, then materialx_lowering.py rewrites what UE's importer reads differently or not at all (MaterialX 1.38 nodes, integers, matrices, flakes, primvar readers, and the graphs it fails or crashes on; the list is in Nodes UE imports). scripts/Test-MaterialXCoverage.ps1 -Export writes a document of every node Houdini ships, in chunks for Import-MaterialX.ps1. One editor imports it (HdUEImportMaterialX, the commandlet Import-MaterialX.ps1 runs) and cooks it with the job's other materials. Inputs the import keeps as material parameters (numeric and colour inputs of the graph's own nodes) stay live: editing them changes the material without a new import; values it bakes in (inside a flattened Houdini node, filenames, integer and boolean inputs) prepare the graph again. A prepared graph binds wherever it appears, at any path, and every later process on the runtime reuses it.

UE 5.8.4's place2d rotates by rotate/360 radians instead of rotate degrees: its MX_Place2D function scales the angle to turns for UE's Rotator, which reads radians (UMaterialExpressionRotator::Compile). HdUEImportMaterialX multiplies the input by 2π after the import, as it corrects UE's normal-map scale. samples/materialx/procedural.usda (place2d rotated 30 degrees, Houdini's checkers node, a mix) is the check: tests/husk_prepared_materials.py renders it translated and imported, and Launch-Houdini.ps1 -TestKind materialx-live -InputUsd samples\materialx\procedural.usda prepares an edit of it in the viewport.

items.title: Reference-safe MaterialX sample
items.text:
Use samples/materialx/showcase_solaris.usda with Solaris Asset Reference. Its single default prim contains geometry, materials, lights, and cameras, and uses Y-up/meters. All 21 meshes retain bindings when referenced below another prim.

Each sample material references its material in the .mtlx document through USD's MaterialX file format (references = @standard_surface.mtlx@</MaterialX/Materials/SS_Glass>), so USD, Karma and hdUE's own translation all read the same graph; the cooked library maps the material by that document and material name. An older form, a Shader with info:mtlx:sourceAsset and a subIdentifier naming the material, still maps, but USD expects a nodedef name there and warns ("Invalid MaterialX NodeDef"). hdUE warns about a surface shader it cannot translate unless the library renders that material.

The original showcase.usda is a complete-stage sample. Its materials are outside the default geometry prim, so open it as a stage or sublayer. Referencing only the geometry prim drops its material bindings.

Regenerate the reference-safe scene through uv run with the configured Houdini Python executable and scripts/generate_solaris_materialx_sample.py.

items.title: Normal maps, UDIMs and texture memory
items.text:
samples/materialx/normal_udim_showcase/normal_udim.usda contains synthetic color and normal UDIM fixtures. Prepare it with Import-UsdMaterialX.ps1 and a fresh output directory.

Normal maps use raw vector images through the float normal-map node. Import disables sRGB, uses normal compression, and adjusts the green channel for the UV convention. Strength scales decoded XY components before normalization. Custom tangent frames and vector-valued strength are unsupported.

UDIM validation covers conventional numbering, power-of-two resolutions, common aspect ratio, mixed resolutions, sparse tile sets, coordinates, and dependency hashes.

Live materials (UsdPreviewSurface, and the MaterialX graphs hdUE translates) read <UDIM> patterns at runtime, with no preparation: the backend builds UE's streaming virtual texture of the tiles it finds next to the pattern (VirtualTextureBuild.cpp), with UE's layout and choices (blocks placed for UE's flipped V, smaller tiles as mip-biased blocks, a mip tail block shared by all tiles, the project's r.VT.TileSize and r.VT.TileBorderSize). UE builds virtual textures only in the editor, so this is its builder's layout written again for the runtime. As the editor streams the chunks it builds from its virtual texture DDC cache files, hdUE writes each chunk once to its virtual texture cache, one file per chunk named by its hash, and UE's virtual texture system streams it from there through its file cache (Apply-ResidencyPatch.ps1): a set never stays in memory. A manifest per set, keyed by its tiles (path, time, size) and the build's choices, lets a reload skip decoding. The cache is %LOCALAPPDATA%\hdUE\VirtualTextureCache, or HDUE_VIRTUAL_TEXTURE_CACHE; it is never evicted (delete the folder, or use the Unreal menu, to reclaim space). Without a writable folder the chunks stay in memory, with a warning in the backend log. A material with a UDIM texture draws on the VT twin of its parent (M_PreviewSurfaceVT, ...), every texture of it virtual, as UE's USD import picks its VT reference material. Tiles that are not a power of two are stretched to one, where UE's import refuses them. Colour tiles in a colour space OCIO converts are converted one by one. The Path Tracer streams the pages its camera rays sample through UE's virtual texture feedback (PathTracingMaterialHitShader.usf): its first draws are a warm-up, with feedback from every pixel and UE's page upload throttle off, as Movie Render Queue's renders, and its accumulation restarts once the pages of the textures' physical pools stay the same for r.vt.FeedbackLatency + 2 draws, each after the GPU finished the one before. Locking every page of every mip instead, as hdUE did before, needed 2.1M pages on NVIDIA's Da Vinci Workshop against a pool of 7,224, and the Path Tracer never started. Surfaces seen only by secondary rays sample the pages that are resident, as in UE.

Live 2D textures are built at load, as UE's cooker builds them, and are not streamed: each is held whole, in memory until its upload and then on the GPU. The backend strips the top mips UE's cook would strip (TextureLODSettings.cpp, CalculateLODBias): the device profile's World texture group LODBias plus r.GlobalTextureLODBias, keeping at most the group's MaxLODSize (16384 by default). UE reads that variable when a texture is built, so set it at startup: HDUE_UE_ARGS=-DPCVars=r.GlobalTextureLODBias=1 halves every texture's width and height and holds a quarter of the memory. Virtual (UDIM) textures take the group's LODBias_VT instead, plus the same variable, up to MaxLODSize_VT, as UE cooks them: their tiles are halved as they load. With r.VT.EnableAutoImport (UE's "Enable virtual texture on texture import", off by default), a material with a texture of at least AutoVTSize x AutoVTSize texels (4096, UE's Texture Import setting; hdUE reads it from the engine ini, [/Script/TextureUtilitiesCommon.TextureImportSettings]) draws on the virtual parents too, as UE's texture import makes such textures virtual (TextureImportSettings.cpp, ShouldTextureBeVirtualByAutoImportSize), so its textures stream from the cache instead of staying whole on the GPU. The size comes from the image's header (PNG and JPEG; other formats stay 2D). The Da Vinci Workshop's materials read 2,100 UDIM sets (6,700 tiles, 62 gigapixels) and 1,280 other textures (15 GB block-compressed): with HDUE_UE_ARGS=-DPCVars=r.VT.EnableAutoImport=1 its husk render at full resolution peaks at 19 GB, where the textures alone held more than 40 GB in memory; the first load writes 41 GB of chunks.

The Path Tracer waits for all required streaming virtual-texture pages and mappings before accumulating. Planning and requests are spread across frames without synchronous file-I/O waits. Capacity limits and timeout fail rather than accumulating low-resolution images. The default pool is 128 MiB per physical format. Runtime UDIM sets are gated the same way. Adaptive virtual textures and automatic pool expansion are outside the current scope.

items.title: Cutout coverage mips
items.text: As UE's Interchange imports MaterialX: an image, or a constant below 1, is a cutout (masked) at UMaterial's default clip value 0.3333; a standard_surface with transmission is see-through instead (OpenPBR's geometry_opacity stays the cutout). The MaterialX spec, and Karma, render opacity as fractional coverage with no threshold, so moving a scene between them calls for material adjustments: Lumen reads the cutout from mipmaps, where thin foliage averages below the clip and would thin with distance. hdUE therefore scales the mips of every texture that drives a cutout (MaterialX opacity, UsdPreviewSurface with opacityThreshold) to keep its alpha coverage at the clip value, as UE's "scale mips for alpha coverage" texture setting does, with three fixes to UE's algorithm (ComputeAlphaScale in TextureCompressorModule.cpp): each level's scale is measured on that level rather than the previous one, the closest tested scale is kept rather than an untested midpoint, and a level is only ever scaled up. A 9x-distant thin-branch card keeps 0.42 of its near coverage (plain mips 0.05, UE's version less than plain); the Path Tracer reads the top mip and is unaffected

items.title: Layered Standard Surface parents
items.text: Materials with subsurface, sheen or a clear coat above 0 render with the layered Standard Surface parents: UE's own Substrate-StandardSurface-Opaque material function (the one UE's Interchange uses for MaterialX), fed the same texture slots, in four cooked variants (opaque or masked, solid or thin-walled; thin_walled is a static input of the function). Everything else, including standard_surface materials without subsurface, sheen or coat, uses the single-slab Preview Surface parents. The layered function mixes metal and dielectric slabs and layers coat and sheen vertically, so it costs several Substrate closures per pixel where Preview Surface costs one; keeping it to the materials that need it bounds that cost. In the Sponza gallery shot (960 x 540, Lumen, curtains covering about half the frame), the layered curtains cost about 1 to 2 ms per frame over the same curtains on Preview Surface (husk, 1500 realtime frames, measured twice).

items.title: COP texture export
items.text: The scene keeps its op: paths. Only Houdini can evaluate them, so the host exports each image the displayed stage's shaders and lights use to an EXR, outside LOP cooks, and passes the delegate the file for each path (hdue_set_viewport_textures in include/hdue/viewport_api.h); materials and lights then re-read their textures. Dirty and time-dependent outputs are checked on each host tick. Changed images receive immutable content-hash paths and reset Path Tracer accumulation. Unchanged images are reused. Cache files and the helper ROP are removed on shutdown. A path the host has not exported yet renders as untextured. husk does not evaluate op: paths (it has no node to cook): it renders them untextured with a warning naming each path, so save COP images to files for husk.

items.title: Glass profiles (usdview)
items.text: Optical glass uses a local profile that selects meshes and supplies IOR, roughness, attenuation color/distance, thickness, and coverage. Optical properties are not inferred from display opacity. Realtime refraction uses a thickness approximation; the Path Tracer follows geometry and absorption. Profiles and scene-specific generators stay local and ignored. usdview takes the profile with Launch-Usdview.ps1 -GlassProfile (scripts/glass_controls.py, /Game/HdUE/M_Glass); it applies to meshes on the displayColor fallback material.

items.title: Cooked native asset placement
items.text:
In Houdini, Render Geometry Settings' Native Asset field (Unreal Engine tab) offers them as a menu: the levels, meshes, Blueprints and Sparse Volume Textures of the runtime profile's asset catalog (Prepare-ProjectAssets.ps1), or, without one, the staged runtime's levels and assets named with UE's prefixes for those types (SM_, SK_, BP_, SVT_). The delegate turns each such prim into a bounds mesh carrying the asset (a Mesh carries it itself; another prim gets a __HdUEAssetProxy child box, sized from the catalog's bounds, else 1 m), in every host alike: Houdini's viewport, husk and usdview render the same placements from the stage, which is not changed. Native assets retain their pivot, material slots, and centimeter dimensions. Authored and parent transforms follow stage units without double unit conversion.

A Sparse Volume Texture (a VDB imported in the UE editor) renders as UE's Heterogeneous Volume, with a dynamic instance of UE's SparseVolumeMaterial (/Game/HdUE/MI_HdUESparseVolume) bound to it, in both render modes. It keeps its VDB's transform, whose units UE reads as centimetres: a VDB written in metres needs a 100x scale on the prim. An animated SVT (a VDB sequence) shows the frame in primvars:unreal:volume:frame, UE's Heterogeneous Volume Frame, 0 for the sequence's first file (default 0). Key it over time as Sequencer keys Frame; there is no free-running playback, so a render is the same at any speed. A constant primvar, it can sit on the asset prim and reach the bounds proxy under it; Render Geometry Settings LOPs set it as Volume Frame (for example $F - 1). samples/conformance/volume/sparse_volume_texture.usda places the Cornell fog this way, sparse_volume_sequence.usda animates a two-file sequence.

Transform, visibility, deletion, and re-creation are supported. Level transforms reload the instance. Virtual-texture waiting also covers native materials. Skeletal meshes use reference poses; Blueprint game progression, time synchronization, and World Partition coverage remain limited.

Prepare-ProjectAssets.ps1 accepts explicit private content inputs and a required map. Keep all input projects, catalogs, generated scenes, and runtime profiles local and ignored.

items.title: Post-processing, colour and AOVs: internals
items.text: Developer notes moved out of the user pages (Post-processing, Colour management, AOVs, Alpha).

items.title: Colour management
items.text:
src/hydra/color_management.cpp relates the host's OCIO config to OCIO's built-in Linear Rec.709 (sRGB) through the config's interchange role. The beauty goes through HdUEToSceneLinear; authored colours through HdUEFromSceneLinear; colour textures through HdUELinearRec709Texture, cached as EXRs in %TEMP%/hdue_ocio. HDUE_COLOR_MANAGEMENT=0 or a config OCIO cannot relate leaves everything linear Rec.709.

HdUEViewTransformsDisplay decides whether the config's default view is a display transform of its own: it sends an sRGB-encoded ramp through the view's inverse and compares it with the plain conversion to scene_linear. When it is, the delegate sends tonemap mode 2 (no tone curve), as UE's OCIO viewport display and Movie Render Queue's Color Output force Disable Tone Curve (MoviePipelineColorSetting.cpp).

With the tone curve, the backend captures SCS_FinalToneCurveHDR (the film curve's output as linear Rec.709, as UE writes float back buffers); without it, SCS_FinalColorHDR.

items.title: Post-process settings
items.text:
The delegate sends every unreal:postProcess:* name and value as text; the backend imports them into an FPostProcessSettings by reflection and sets the override flags. Unknown names or values are skipped with a warning in the UE log. Texture settings take a cooked path or an image file, imported at render time with UE's texture defaults (8-bit sRGB, float linear, unfiltered mips) and re-imported when the file's time or size changes. Ambient Cubemap converts a lat-long into a cubemap with box-filtered mips.

Order of blending (ApplyPostProcess in Bridge.cpp): hdUE's defaults (manual exposure, bias 0), then the world's post-process volumes (UWorld::AddPostProcessingSettings), then what the request decides (render mode, samples, lighting components, the USD camera's depth of field), then the render settings, as Movie Render Queue blends a camera's settings after the volumes (MoviePipelineUtils.cpp, DoPostProcessBlend). With the tonemapper on, the USD camera's exposure is added to AutoExposureBias; with it off, the delegate multiplies the beauty by the camera's linear exposure scale.

The render settings generator (scripts/generate_render_settings.py) leaves out WeightedBlendables (use unreal:postProcessMaterials), PathTracingSamplesPerPixel (use unreal:samplesPerPixel), mobile depth of field, and the fixed-size arrays LensFlareTints and DepthOfFieldMatteBoxFlags.

UE 5.8.4's AmbientCubemapComposite.usf never defines SUBSTRATE_LOAD_FROM_MATERIALCONTAINER, so with Substrate's adaptive GBuffer it adds nothing; Apply-ResidencyPatch.ps1 adds the define (repro).

items.title: Viewport and husk parity
items.text: On the Cornell box with the tonemapper on, the viewport's converged frame is 1.03x husk's mean, its 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles within 1.5/255 in sRGB; husk with the viewport's quality profile renders 0.98x.
