Standard Surface OpenPBR Default What it does subsurface_color subsurface_color (1, 1, 1) Colour of the scattered light subsurface_radius subsurface_radius_scale (1, 1, 1) Relative scattering distance per channel: red furthest for skin subsurface_scale subsurface_radius 1 Scattering distance, in scene units

Subsurface Scale multiplies Subsurface Radius into a mean free path in scene units. In a stage in metres, the default 1 is a metre of scattering: the object looks like jelly. A 9 cm shader ball wants about 0.02.

items.title: Sheen
items.text:
Sheen USD attribute sheen (OpenPBR fuzz_weight) Default 0

A soft, bright rim at grazing angles, from fibres: velvet, felt, dust. hdUE renders it as Substrate fuzz. sheen_color (default (1, 1, 1)) tints it and sheen_roughness (default 0.3) widens it.

items.title: Coat
items.text:
Coat USD attribute coat (OpenPBR coat_weight) Default 0

A clear layer over the base: varnish, car paint, lacquer. coat_roughness (default 0.1) is its own roughness; coat_color (default (1, 1, 1)) tints what is under it.

coat_IOR and coat_normal are not translated: the coat's IOR is 1.5.

items.title: Emission
items.text:
Emission × Emission Color USD attribute emission × emission_color (OpenPBR emission_luminance × emission_color) Default 0 × (1, 1, 1)

Emitted light, as Preview Surface Emissive Color. OpenPBR's emission_luminance is used as a plain multiplier, not in nits.

items.title: Geometry
items.text:
Standard Surface OpenPBR Default In UE Opacity opacity geometry_opacity 1 A cutout (UE's Masked blend mode) at 0.3333, UE's default clip value, when it is a texture or a constant below 1 Thin Walled thin_walled geometry_thin_walled off A thin two-sided shell that lets its subsurface colour through: leaves, paper, curtains Normal normal geometry_normal Tangent-space normal map, through a MaterialX Normal Map node

A Standard Surface with Transmission above 0 is see-through instead of cut out. See Opacity and glass.

items.title: Nodes hdUE translates
items.text:
Each surface input is a constant or reaches an image through these nodes. Anything else is imported by UE.

Node What hdUE does MaterialX Image, Tiled Image (uvtiling, uvoffset), USD UV Texture The texture, with its colour space and address modes Texture Coordinate, Geometry Property Value (vector2), USD Primvar Reader Selects the UV set (st, map1, ...) Place 2D, USD Transform 2D Transforms the UVs of the image it feeds Geometry Property Value (color3, vector3) Reads a vertex colour primvar Extract Picks one channel (alpha for cutouts: Image color4 → Extract index 3) Normal Map Tangent-space decode, with its scale Multiply by a constant Scales the texture Mix with one of fg, bg, mix connected Offsets and scales that input Convert, Dot, Constant Passed through, or the value

Texture colour spaces follow the image's colorspace: srgb_texture decodes sRGB, lin_rec709 and raw read linear.

items.title: Nodes UE imports
items.text:
Any other graph is imported in the background by UE's own MaterialX importer (Interchange), which reads MaterialX 1.39.4; Houdini 22 writes 1.39.5. Before the import, hdUE rewrites what UE's importer cannot read, so every node Houdini ships reaches UE except the ones in the last row:

Nodes What hdUE writes for UE Houdini's MaterialX 1.38 nodes (swizzle, atan2 with its old inputs, ...) MaterialX's own upgrade (upgradeVersion) Integer and boolean nodes (and, or, not, integer maths, conversions) The same values as floats, as UE computes everything in floats Matrix nodes (creatematrix, transformmatrix, invertmatrix, determinant, transpose, matrix maths) Their scalar maths, with MaterialX's column-major conventions flake2d, flake3d (MaterialX 1.39.5) MaterialX's own flake code in a UE Custom node (unreal/HdUEBackend/Shaders/MaterialXFlake.ush), the same flakes for the same coordinates; a flake whose size, roughness or coverage comes from another node uses a graph of standard nodes instead (statistically the same flakes, much heavier to compile) geompropvalue, primvar readers The UV set or vertex colour hdUE uploads for the primvar; other primvars use their fallback value curveadjust Linear interpolation between the knots frame The frame at 24 fps ambientocclusion 1: UE's Lumen and Path Tracer occlude the lighting themselves disney_principled, thin_surface, generalized_schlick_edf, a lone thin_film The nearest node UE imports Graphs UE's importer fails on as written Written as it reads them: a mix of displacement shaders as one displacement of the mixed height; a Standard Surface mixed with another shader carries its base weight in base_color (UE's importer reads any input named base as a Substrate layer's bottom); inputs it has no slot for (thin film on BSDFs, color82, thin_walled on surface) left out, with a warning when set Light shaders (light, point_light, spot_light, directional_light), osl_set_ci, arrays no node reads Not imported: USD lights are UsdLux prims, and the others exist only in OSL or in no graph

scripts/Test-MaterialXCoverage.ps1 checks this: it wires each of the 898 node definitions Houdini ships into a material, exports it, and lists what UE would not import (-Export -One -Only ND_<name> writes one document per node for UE's importer).

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
How to get these looks on a Standard Surface. Inputs not listed stay at their default.

Look Inputs Skin base_color (0.8, 0.5, 0.4), specular_roughness 0.4, subsurface 1, subsurface_color (0.9, 0.45, 0.3), subsurface_radius (1, 0.35, 0.2), subsurface_scale 0.02 (a 9 cm object in metres; scale it with the object) Velvet base_color (0.3, 0.05, 0.1), specular_roughness 0.7, sheen 1, sheen_color (1, 0.85, 0.9), sheen_roughness 0.3 Lacquered wood wood texture into base_color, specular_roughness 0.5, coat 1, coat_roughness 0.05 Leaf leaf texture into base_color, subsurface 0.5, subsurface_color (0.4, 0.6, 0.1), thin_walled on; alpha through Extract into opacity Glass See glass recipes

items.title: Layers that need no second texture
items.text:
hdUE translates a MaterialX graph at render time when each input reads at most one texture. Two layers of standard_surface add detail within that limit:

  • A wet surface: a water film is a clear coat. coat 1 (or a grunge map, for puddles), coat_IOR 1.33, coat_roughness 0.03, coat_color (0.7, 0.7, 0.72) to darken what is under the water, as wet stone darkens. Lower the surface's own roughness too.
  • Grime over any texture: a coat of coat_IOR 1.0 reflects nothing and only tints what is under it. Feed coat_color from a mix between white and a dirt colour, driven by a grime map read in a second UV set (geompropvalue uv2): the dirt varies over the whole building instead of repeating with the texture's tile.

Both are used on the Bistro street (scripts/convert_bistro.py).

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Cause Fix An input renders flat, with a warning "MaterialX node ... is not translated" A node outside the list, and the import is not finished or cannot run Wait for the background import; on a machine without UE's editor, replace the node or cook the material (cooked libraries) Subsurface looks like jelly or glows through the whole object subsurface_scale is in scene units: the default 1 is a metre Lower it to the object's scattering distance A textured base, sheen or subsurface weight renders as its constant Textured weights are not translated Put the texture in the colour input instead subsurface_color or sheen_color ignores its texture They follow a texture only when it is base_color's Use base_color's texture, or let UE import the graph Leaves or foliage cut out too much or too little compared with Karma UE cuts opacity at 0.3333; Karma blends fractional coverage Adjust the alpha in the texture, or use a Preview Surface with your own Opacity Threshold

items.title: Unreal Engine and Karma
items.text:
• hdUE follows UE's Interchange MaterialX import: the same Substrate-StandardSurface material functions, cutout opacity at UE's default clip value (0.3333), refraction on the translucent function.
  • Karma renders opacity as fractional coverage with no threshold; the MaterialX specification does too.
  • A material with coat, sheen or subsurface uses UE's layered Standard Surface function, which costs several Substrate closures per pixel. In the Sponza gallery shot (960 x 540, Lumen), layered curtains cost 1 to 2 ms per frame more than the same curtains on Preview Surface. Other Standard Surface materials cost what a Preview Surface does.
  • Subsurface uses Substrate's per-material mean free path; UE subsurface profiles are not created. One UV transform per material, from the first textured input. Thin film and dispersion are not translated.
  • Position-based nodes (position, noise3d, flake3d, ...) read UE's local position in metres, as UE's importer translates position. hdUE uploads meshes in UE's axes, so a 3D pattern can be turned compared with Karma's: same density and size, different cells.

items.title: Opacity and glass
items.text:
UE has three ways to let the background through a surface, and hdUE picks one from the material: a partly present surface (translucent), a cutout (masked), or glass that refracts (transmission). Only transmission bends light.

The figures on this page use the shader ball (samples/docs/lookdev.usda). Below: Preview Surface at opacity 0.2, then Standard Surface with transmission 1 (Realtime, Ray Traced translucency).

items.title: Which one you get
items.text:
You author UE blend mode Bends light Use it for Preview Surface Opacity below 1, Opacity Threshold 0 Translucent No Thin films, holograms, fades Preview Surface Opacity Threshold above 0 Masked: cut at the threshold No Leaves, fences, cut-out cards MaterialX Opacity (opacity, geometry_opacity) textured or below 1 Masked: cut at 0.3333 No Foliage from MaterialX MaterialX Transmission above 0 Translucent Standard Surface, with refraction Yes Glass, water, liquids, plastics displayOpacity on a prim with no material Translucent No Quick previews

A Standard Surface with transmission is never cut out by its opacity. An OpenPBR surface with a geometry_opacity cutout ignores its transmission.

See Preview Surface for the opacity inputs, with figures.

items.title: Using it in Solaris
items.text:
1. Build a MaterialX Standard Surface in a Karma Material Builder or Material Library.
  2. Set Transmission to 1 and Base to 0. Glass gets its colour from transmission, not from the base.
  3. Set Specular IOR: 1.5 for glass, 1.33 for water.
  4. In Realtime, set Translucency Method (unreal:postProcess:TranslucencyType, hdUE Render Settings > Rendering Features > Translucency) to Ray Traced.

items.title: Translucency Method
items.text:
Translucency Method USD attribute unreal:postProcess:TranslucencyType Default Raster

Realtime only

How UE draws translucent surfaces in Realtime. Raster draws them over the scene; refraction is a screen-space offset. Ray Traced traces refraction and reflection rays through them and comes much closer to the Path Tracer. The Path Tracer always traces glass.

With Ray Traced, its section shows UE's own settings: Max Roughness (default 0.6), Max. Refraction Rays (default 3) and the shadow type. Ray Traced costs more GPU time than Raster.

items.title: Specular Roughness
items.text:
Specular Roughness USD attribute specular_roughness Default 0.2

On a transmissive surface, roughness blurs both the reflection and what is seen through the glass: frosted glass. With Ray Traced translucency, roughness above Max Roughness (0.6) fades out the traced refraction.

items.title: Transmission Color and Transmission Depth
items.text:
Transmission Color USD attribute transmission_color Default (1, 1, 1) Transmission Depth USD attribute transmission_depth Default 0, scene units

Light travelling through the glass reaches Transmission Color after Transmission Depth: thick parts are darker and more saturated than thin ones, as in a bottle. UE turns the pair into an absorption distance (its Substrate-StandardSurface-Translucent function, as Interchange imports it). Path Tracer below, on a 9 cm ball.

Note

At Transmission Depth 0 (the Standard Surface default), Transmission Color tints the glass at its surface, without absorption inside: both render modes show the same tint whatever the object's thickness. Set a depth for the colour to deepen with thickness, as in a bottle.

items.title: Alpha behind glass
items.text: The beauty's alpha behind glass is the alpha of what the glass shows: an opaque object seen through a pane keeps alpha 1, so you can composite it over a background. See Alpha.

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
How to get these looks on a MaterialX Standard Surface. Inputs not listed stay at their default. In Realtime, set Translucency Method to Ray Traced.

Look Inputs Clear glass base 0, specular_roughness 0, specular_IOR 1.5, transmission 1 Frosted glass base 0, specular_roughness 0.3, specular_IOR 1.5, transmission 1 Green bottle glass base 0, specular_roughness 0, specular_IOR 1.5, transmission 1, transmission_color (0.3, 0.7, 0.45), transmission_depth 0.02 (2 cm in metres) Water base 0, specular_roughness 0, specular_IOR 1.33, transmission 1 Thin window pane (a single quad) Clear glass, plus thin_walled on

samples/materialx/glass.usda shows an object behind clear glass and behind glass whose roughness follows a fractal smudge.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Cause Fix Glass shows bright rims or a flat overlay in Realtime, but looks right in the Path Tracer Translucency Method is Raster Set it to Ray Traced A see-through surface does not refract It uses Preview Surface Opacity, which is presence Use MaterialX Transmission Frosted glass loses its refraction above a roughness Ray Traced translucency fades out above Max Roughness (0.6) Raise Max Roughness, or check in the Path Tracer A prim's displayOpacity varies per point but renders uniform, with a warning A material carries one opacity Bind a material with an opacity texture Cutout foliage thins with distance in Realtime Distant pixels read smaller mips See Preview Surface troubleshooting

items.title: Unreal Engine and Karma
items.text:
• Transmission follows UE's Interchange import of MaterialX: the translucent Standard Surface function, coloured transmittance, refraction from the material's IOR. UE's Path Tracer refracts only with that refraction method, which hdUE uses.
  • A Preview Surface with partial opacity keeps about 0.8 of Karma's Fresnel reflections at its rims, since UE's opacity fades the whole surface.
  • MaterialX cutouts use UE's clip value 0.3333; Karma renders fractional coverage.

items.title: Preview Surface
items.text:
UsdPreviewSurface is USD's portable material. hdUE renders every input of it, constant or textured, on UE's Preview Surface reference material: one Substrate slab, the cheapest material UE has.

The figures on this page use SideFX's shader ball (samples/docs/lookdev.usda) in Realtime, with the ball's diffuseColor (0.8, 0.25, 0.08) and roughness 0.3 unless a figure changes them.

items.title: Using it in Solaris
items.text:
1. In a Material Library LOP, create a USD Preview Surface VOP.
  2. For a texture, wire a USD UV Texture VOP into the input, with a USD Primvar Reader (st) into its ST.
  3. Assign the material with Assign Material or the library's Geometry Path.

Every input updates live in the viewport and the Path Tracer restarts its accumulation. Defaults below are the UsdPreviewSurface specification's.

items.title: Diffuse Color
items.text:
Diffuse Color USD attribute inputs:diffuseColor Default (0.18, 0.18, 0.18)

The surface colour: UE's Base Color. With Metallic 1 it is the metal's reflectance colour instead.

items.title: Emissive Color
items.text:
Emissive Color USD attribute inputs:emissiveColor Default (0, 0, 0)

Light the surface emits: UE's Emissive Color. Values above 1 are allowed and needed for a surface that reads as a light source.

Note

In the Path Tracer, emissive surfaces light the scene (Emissive Materials, on by default). In Realtime, Lumen picks up their light only through its global illumination, much weaker for small emitters: on the conformance mesh-light scene a wall gets about 1% of the Path Tracer's light. Light a scene with UsdLux lights, and use emission for what the camera sees.

items.title: Use Specular Workflow and Specular Color
items.text:
Use Specular Workflow USD attribute inputs:useSpecularWorkflow Default 0 Specular Color USD attribute inputs:specularColor Default (0, 0, 0)

At 1, Diffuse Color is the diffuse colour and Specular Color the reflectance at normal incidence (F0), as in UE's specular reflection. Metallic and IOR are then ignored. At 0 (the metalness workflow), Specular Color is ignored.

items.title: Metallic
items.text:
Metallic USD attribute inputs:metallic Default 0

0 is a dielectric (plastic, wood, paint), 1 a metal. A metal has no diffuse lobe: Diffuse Color becomes its reflection colour. Use 0 or 1; values between are for texture transitions such as rust edges.

items.title: Roughness
items.text:
Roughness USD attribute inputs:roughness Default 0.5

Microfacet roughness of the specular reflection, UE's Roughness: 0 is a mirror, 1 fully diffuse-looking.

Tip

In Realtime, Lumen traces dedicated reflection rays only up to Max Roughness To Trace (default 0.4). Rougher surfaces reflect Lumen's cheaper radiance cache, as in UE.

items.title: Clearcoat
items.text:
Clearcoat USD attribute inputs:clearcoat Default 0

A clear, white varnish layer over the surface, with an IOR of 1.5. Above 0, the material renders with UE's layered Standard Surface material: the coat is a second Substrate slab over the base, which costs more per pixel than a plain Preview Surface.

Note

With Use Specular Workflow 1, or with Opacity below 1, the coat is not layered: it becomes a second specular lobe of the base (Substrate's haziness), which reads like a coat on most surfaces.

items.title: Clearcoat Roughness
items.text:
Clearcoat Roughness USD attribute inputs:clearcoatRoughness Default 0.01

Roughness of the coat alone; the base keeps Roughness. A rough base under a sharp coat is the usual varnished look.

items.title: Opacity
items.text:
Opacity USD attribute inputs:opacity Default 1

Below 1 (with Opacity Threshold 0) the surface is partly present, on UE's translucent material: what is behind it shows through, unbent. Opacity scales the whole surface, its reflections and emission too, so it reads as a thin film or a ghost, not as glass. For glass that refracts, use MaterialX transmission (Opacity and glass).

items.title: Opacity Threshold
items.text:
Opacity Threshold USD attribute inputs:opacityThreshold Default 0

Above 0, Opacity becomes a cutout mask (UE's Masked blend mode): pixels with an opacity below the threshold are removed, the rest are fully opaque. Use it with a texture's alpha for leaves, fences and decals. Here the ball's opacity is 0.4 throughout: at 0.3 it is opaque, at 0.5 it is cut out entirely.

items.title: IOR
items.text:
IOR USD attribute inputs:ior Default 1.5

Index of refraction of a dielectric. It sets the reflectance facing the camera, F0 = ((ior - 1) / (ior + 1))²: 0.02 for water (1.33), 0.04 for glass and plastics (1.5), 0.17 for diamond (2.4). It does not refract. Ignored with Use Specular Workflow 1.

items.title: Normal
items.text:
Normal USD attribute inputs:normal Default (0, 0, 1)

A tangent-space normal map. Read the texture with Source Color Space raw, Scale (2, 2, 2, 1) and Bias (-1, -1, -1, 0), which turn texel values from 0..1 into -1..1. The map must be OpenGL-style (+Y up), as USD specifies.

items.title: Displacement
items.text:
Displacement USD attribute inputs:displacement Default 0

Moves the surface along its normals, in scene units, before rendering, so Lumen, the Path Tracer and Nanite all see the displaced shape. A textured displacement first subdivides the mesh to about one triangle per two texels (at most about a million triangles per mesh). See Displacement.

items.title: Occlusion
items.text:
Occlusion USD attribute inputs:occlusion Default 1

Baked ambient occlusion, UE's Ambient Occlusion input: below 1 it darkens the ambient light reaching the surface. Checked in Realtime.

items.title: Textures
items.text:
A USD UV Texture (UsdUVTexture) can drive every input above. hdUE reads:

Input What it does file The image. <UDIM> patterns stream as UE virtual textures (UDIMs); op: paths read Copernicus images (COP textures) st The UV primvar, usually through a USD Primvar Reader (st). A material reads up to 4 UV primvars wrapS, wrapT repeat, clamp, mirror or black. The default, useMetadata, falls back to black sourceColorSpace raw (data), sRGB (8-bit colour), auto (default: sRGB for colour inputs, raw for the others) scale, bias Multiply then add to the texel fallback The value when the file cannot be read; (0, 0, 0, 1) by default outputs:rgb, r, g, b, a The colour, or one channel for a float input such as roughness or opacity

A USD Transform 2D (UsdTransform2d) between the primvar reader and the texture scales, rotates and offsets the UVs. A material uses one UV transform: the first textured input's.

Floating-point images (EXR, HDR) in colour inputs are read in the OCIO scene_linear space and converted to UE's linear Rec.709; with Houdini's default OCIO config this changes nothing. See Colour management.

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
How to get these looks on a Preview Surface. Inputs not listed stay at their default.

Look Diffuse Color Metallic Roughness Other Mirror chrome (0.9, 0.9, 0.9) 1 0 Rough metal (aluminium) (0.91, 0.92, 0.92) 1 0.35 Gold (1, 0.71, 0.29) 1 0.2 Plastic (0.05, 0.3, 0.8) 0 0.25 Car paint (0.4, 0.01, 0.02) 0 0.4 Clearcoat 1, Clearcoat Roughness 0.02 Emissive panel (0, 0, 0) 0 0.5 Emissive Color (5, 4.5, 4) Cutout leaf texture rgb 0 0.5 Opacity from the texture's a, Opacity Threshold 0.5
  • Brushed metal: Preview Surface and the MaterialX translation have no anisotropy. Use a rough metal with a roughness texture of fine streaks, or a normal map.
  • Emissive panel: raise Emissive Color until the panel reads as a light at the scene's exposure; add a RectLight in front of it to light the scene in Realtime.
  • Glass: Preview Surface does not refract. Use the glass recipes.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Cause Fix A texture is black outside the 0..1 UV square (tiling UVs show one tile) wrapS/wrapT default to useMetadata, which falls back to black Set Wrap S and Wrap T to repeat A colour texture looks washed out Read as raw Set Source Color Space to sRGB or auto A roughness or mask texture reads too dark (surface too glossy) Read as sRGB Set Source Color Space to raw A texture input renders black or flat The file does not resolve, so fallback is used Fix the path A normal map lights bumps from the wrong side A DirectX-style map (-Y) Use Scale (2, -2, 2, 1) and Bias (-1, 1, -1, 0) to flip green Cutout leaves thin out with distance in Realtime Distant pixels read smaller mips, where alpha averages below the threshold hdUE rescales each mip to keep the alpha coverage, as UE's "Scale Mips for Alpha Coverage"; a branch 9 times further keeps 0.42 of its near coverage (0.05 with plain mips). The Path Tracer reads the full-resolution mip and does not thin A clear coat looks like a hazy second highlight, not a layer Use Specular Workflow 1 or Opacity below 1 Use the metalness workflow and full opacity A see-through surface looks like a ghost, without refraction Opacity is presence, not transmission Use MaterialX transmission for glass

items.title: Unreal Engine and Karma
items.text:
• hdUE maps Preview Surface as UE's USD importer does onto its Preview Surface reference materials: opaque, masked (with Opacity Threshold) or translucent.
  • opacityMode is not read. Partial opacity is presence in hdUE, so it fades reflections too: the rims of a thin see-through pane render at about 0.8 of Karma's.
  • Occlusion: the specification notes that path tracers may ignore it.

items.title: Alpha
items.text: The beauty's alpha channel is the coverage of each pixel: how much of it the camera sees covered by geometry. You use it to composite the render over a plate or another layer.

items.title: What alpha holds
items.text:
Pixel Alpha Opaque geometry 1 Nothing but empty space 0 Anti-aliased edge, depth-of-field blur, motion blur Between 0 and 1: the covered fraction Translucent surface (glass, a translucent material) over empty space Between 0 and 1 Opaque object seen through glass 1 Cutout (masked opacity) 1 where kept, 0 where cut Visible dome light background (Realtime) 0

Alpha works in Realtime and Path Tracer modes. DLSS upscales it too (DLSS Alpha Upscaling, on by default). hdUE turns on UE's alpha output (r.PostProcessing.PropagateAlpha) for every render; there is nothing to set.

items.title: Premultiplication
items.text:
Where nothing is behind the geometry, the colour is the geometry's colour times its coverage: an edge pixel half covered by a white object is (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) with alpha 0.5. That is premultiplied (associated) alpha, what EXR and Houdini's compositing expect. Composite with a plain Over; do not premultiply again.

A visible background breaks this: a dome light drawn behind the geometry fills the colour where alpha is 0. For a layer you composite, hide the background.

items.title: How to render a layer for comp
items.text:
1. Select the dome light. Turn off Visible to Camera (unreal:visibleBackground = 0). It still lights the scene and appears in reflections.
  2. Write the beauty as color4f (RGBA): hdUE Standard Render Vars' Beauty does.
  3. In comp, put the layer Over the plate.

Effects that spread light (bloom, lens flares) brighten the colour beyond the alpha edge: turn them off for layers, and add them in comp.

items.title: Holdouts and mattes
items.text: hdUE has no holdout (matte) objects. UsdRenderPass matte and cameraVisibility collections are not applied; prune collections are. To cut an object out of a layer, render it into a separate layer, or use Cryptomatte or primId as a matte in comp.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Cause Fix Alpha 0 behind the object, but the environment shows in the colour A visible dome fills the colour; alpha counts geometry only Hide the background for comp layers (above). Dark fringe around the object in comp The render was premultiplied again, or unpremultiplied colour was assumed Composite with Over without an extra Premultiply. Glow from bloom outside the alpha Bloom and lens flares are image effects, not geometry Turn them off for layers. A matte collection has no effect hdUE does not apply matte collections Use Cryptomatte or a separate layer.

items.title: Unreal Engine and Karma
items.text:
• hdUE uses UE's own alpha output, the project setting Alpha Output (r.PostProcessing.PropagateAlpha). UE stores 1 minus the coverage; hdUE outputs the coverage itself.
  • Karma also writes coverage alpha, and supports holdout mattes, which hdUE does not.

items.title: AOVs
items.text: AOVs (render vars) are extra images written next to the beauty: surface data such as albedo and normals, the beauty split into lighting components, object IDs and Cryptomatte mattes. hdUE uses Karma's render var names and light path expressions, so a Karma AOV setup selects the same outputs.

items.title: Setting up AOVs in Solaris
items.text:
With hdUE Render Settings (the quickest):

  1. Open Image Output > AOVs (Render Vars) on hdUE Render Settings.
  2. Turn on the AOVs you need. husk writes them as layers of the output picture.

With hdUE Standard Render Vars (the counterpart of Karma Standard Render Vars):

  1. Add hdUE Standard Render Vars (TAB menu > hdUE > Rendering) above hdUE Render Settings or hdUE Render Products.
  2. Turn on AOVs in its Beauty, Surface, Lighting, Utility and Cryptomatte sections. Beauty, Depth and Normal are on by default.
  3. Set each AOV's Precision: 16 Bit (half) or 32 Bit (float).
  4. On hdUE Render Settings, turn on Import Upstream Render Vars (or wire the node into the second input and turn on Import Render Vars From Second Input).

With Render Var LOPs: set Source Name to an AOV's name from the tables below (sourceName, source type raw), or to its light path expression (source type lpe). The render var and its channel may be named anything: hdUE matches the source name.

The beauty is the render var whose source name is color, C, Ci or beauty, or the light path expression C.*[LO] or C.*.

items.title: Surface AOVs
items.text:
Surface AOVs describe the nearest opaque surface. They are UE's buffer visualizations, the same buffers as UE's Buffer Visualization view mode.

AOV (sourceName) Karma name Type Holds albedo baseColor, CDA color3f Base colour. Path Tracer: the Path Tracer's albedo (see below) normal N, ray:hitN normal3f World-space shading normal, USD axes, normalized roughness float Roughness metallic float Metallic specular float UE's specular (0.5 is 4% reflectance) occlusion float Material ambient occlusion ambientOcclusion AO float Screen-space ambient occlusion (1 is unoccluded) opacity float UE's GBuffer opacity: subsurface and foliage data, 0 for other surfaces. Not the beauty's alpha subsurfaceColor color3f Subsurface colour, black for other surfaces anisotropy float Anisotropy tangent normal3f World-space tangent, USD axes, normalized shadingModel color3f UE's shading model, coloured as its Shading Model view velocity color3f Motion vectors, as Movie Render Queue writes them (below) customDepth, customStencil float UE's custom depth and stencil. hdUE meshes do not write them: far and 0

Surface AOVs have no anti-aliasing, motion blur, depth of field or transparency: one sample per pixel, at the frame's time. They line up pixel for pixel with the beauty.

Path Tracer albedo and normal. In Path Tracer mode, albedo and normal are the buffers the Path Tracer accumulates for its denoiser. They are anti-aliased, carry the beauty's depth of field, and cost nothing extra. The albedo is the denoiser albedo: diffuse and specular reflectance, followed through mirrors and glass, not the base colour. With motion blur on, they fall back to the unblurred surface buffers.

Motion vectors. velocity holds the screen motion since the previous frame, in UE's encoding: x in red, y in green, 0.5 for no motion. A motion of v in normalized device coordinates (2 is the full frame width) is stored as v × 0.2495 + 0.5. Deforming meshes and volumes show no motion of their own.

items.title: Lighting AOVs
items.text:
Lighting AOVs are the beauty restricted to one kind of light path, using UE's Lighting Components (the same switches Movie Render Queue's render layers use).

AOV (sourceName) Light path expression Holds combineddiffuse (diffuse) C<RD>.*L Diffuse reflection, direct and indirect directdiffuse C<RD>L Diffuse reflection of direct light indirectdiffuse C<RD>.+L Diffuse reflection of indirect light (realtime: Lumen GI) combinedglossyreflection (glossy) C<RG>.*L Specular reflection and transmission, direct and indirect directglossyreflection C<RG>L Specular reflection of direct light indirectglossyreflection C<RG>.+L Specular reflection of indirect light (realtime: Lumen reflections) directemission (emission) CO Emission seen directly combinedvolume (volume) CV.*L Volume scattering, direct and indirect. Path Tracer only directvolume CVL Volume scattering of direct light. Path Tracer only indirectvolume CV.+L Volume scattering of indirect light. Path Tracer only

All are color3f, in the config's scene_linear space, with the camera's exposure applied as on the beauty. They are not post-processed: no Unreal Tonemapper, bloom or grade.

In realtime mode, components are approximations: emission stays in every component, and volumes are not split (volume AOVs are cleared, with a warning). UE has no light path expressions, so other expressions are not supported.

items.title: ID AOVs and depth
items.text:
AOV (sourceName) Type Holds depth float Distance from the camera plane, in stage units primId int Hydra prim ID of the visible mesh, -1 for background instanceId int Instance index of an instanced prototype, -1 elsewhere

ID AOVs are unlit raster passes: no anti-aliasing, motion blur, depth of field or transparency. Meshes placed from the native asset catalog read as background.

items.title: Cryptomatte
items.text:
hdUE writes Cryptomatte (specification 1.2), as Movie Render Queue's Object ID pass does.

  1. On hdUE Standard Render Vars, open Cryptomatte.
  2. Turn on Crypto Object (one ID per prim path), Crypto Material (one ID per bound material), or both.
  3. Each adds three 32-bit float4 render vars, CryptoObject00 to CryptoObject02 (or CryptoMaterial00 to 02): six ranks.

husk writes each layer's metadata and manifest (cryptomatte/<key>/name, hash, conversion, manifest) into every image, as the specification defines, so Cryptomatte tools in comp find the names.

Coverage comes from 16 samples per pixel on a 4 x 4 grid, so edges are anti-aliased. Like the ID AOVs, Cryptomatte ignores depth of field, motion blur and transparency. Geometry with no bound material has no Crypto Material ID.

Keep Cryptomatte at 32 bit

The IDs are float bit patterns: a 16-bit (half) channel destroys them. hdUE Standard Render Vars writes them as 32-bit float4.

Karma's Cryptomatte LOP authors Karma-only render vars, which hdUE does not read. Use hdUE Standard Render Vars instead.

items.title: What each AOV costs
items.text:
AOVs render after the beauty converges, from the same camera and time. The beauty itself is not slowed down.

AOVs Extra cost per frame All surface AOVs together One short raster render (two with velocity: it renders the previous frame first) Path Tracer albedo and normal Nothing Each lighting AOV One full render of the beauty: its mode, samples, warmup and exposure Each ID AOV (primId, instanceId) One short raster render Cryptomatte, any number of layers 16 short raster renders depth Nothing: read back with the beauty

With three lighting AOVs, a frame takes about four times as long as the beauty alone. Pick the components you will use.

items.title: How to rebuild the beauty in comp
items.text:
Use Path Tracer mode with the Unreal Tonemapper off: the beauty and the lighting AOVs are then the same scene-linear radiance.

  1. Turn on combineddiffuse, combinedglossyreflection and directemission, plus combinedvolume if the shot has volumes.
  2. In comp, add them: diffuse + glossy + emission (+ volume).
  3. Grade each layer, then compare the sum with the beauty using a Difference.

Do the components add up?

Conformance tests check that direct and indirect diffuse add up to combined diffuse. The full sum against the beauty is not tested: check the difference on your shot before relying on it. In realtime mode, emission is in every component, so the components do not add up to the beauty.

items.title: How to set up a comp-ready AOV set
items.text:
1. hdUE Standard Render Vars: Beauty (16 Bit), Depth (32 Bit), Normal (16 Bit), Albedo, Combined Diffuse, Combined Glossy Reflection, Direct Emission.
  2. Cryptomatte: Crypto Object and Crypto Material.
  3. hdUE Render Settings: Unreal Tonemapper off; Import Upstream Render Vars on.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Cause Fix An AOV is black, with a warning naming it The source name is not one hdUE renders, or a light path expression it does not support Use a name or expression from the tables above. Volume AOVs black in realtime Realtime does not split volumes Render in Path Tracer mode. customDepth far, customStencil 0 hdUE meshes do not write UE's custom depth or stencil Use depth and primId instead. Cryptomatte selects nothing in comp Written as 16-bit half Keep Cryptomatte at 32 bit (float4). Cryptomatte from Karma's Cryptomatte LOP missing Karma's render vars are Karma-only Use hdUE Standard Render Vars' Cryptomatte section. Lighting AOVs do not match the beauty The Unreal Tonemapper is on: the beauty is tone-mapped, the AOVs are not Turn the tonemapper off for comp renders. Albedo and normal blurry or soft at the edges in Path Tracer mode They are the Path Tracer's anti-aliased buffers, with depth of field Expected. Use depth and Cryptomatte for hard mattes. Viewport selection highlight lags one frame after an edit AOVs follow the converged beauty, and Solaris tints its selection from primId Expected. It catches up once the frame converges.

items.title: Unreal Engine and Karma
items.text:
• Every output is one UE already provides: buffer visualizations, the Path Tracer's denoiser buffers, Lighting Components and Movie Render Queue's Object ID recipe for Cryptomatte.
  • Karma's names and light path expressions select the same AOVs. Karma computes every light path expression in one render; UE has no light path expressions, so each lighting AOV is a render of its own.
  • Karma's surface AOVs are anti-aliased; hdUE's realtime surface AOVs are single-sample, like UE's buffer visualizations.
  • UE's buffer visualizations of the image itself (SceneColor, PreTonemapHDRColor, FinalImage, ...) are not offered: they are states of the beauty.

items.title: Light properties
items.text: UE light component properties hdUE reads from unreal:light:<Property> attributes on UsdLux lights (the Unreal Engine tab of Light LOPs), with UE's tooltips and defaults. See Lights.

items.title: Indirect Lighting Intensity
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 6USD attributeunreal:light:IndirectLightingIntensityHoudini parameterxn__unreallightIndirectLightingIntensity_pzbf

Scales the indirect lighting contribution from this light. A value of 0 disables any GI from this light. Default is 1.

items.title: Volumetric Scattering Intensity
items.text:
Default1Range0.25 to 4USD attributeunreal:light:VolumetricScatteringIntensityHoudini parameterxn__unreallightVolumetricScatteringIntensity_75bf

Intensity of the volumetric scattering from this light. This scales Intensity and LightColor.

items.title: Cast Volumetric Shadow
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:light:bCastVolumetricShadowHoudini parameterxn__unreallightbCastVolumetricShadow_6sbf

Whether the light shadows volumetric fog. Disabling this can save GPU time. Distant lights default to on (UDirectionalLightComponent). It also lets heterogeneous volumes shadow the scene in realtime.

items.title: Affect Translucent Lighting
items.text:
DefaultOnUSD attributeunreal:light:bAffectTranslucentLightingHoudini parameterxn__unreallightbAffectTranslucentLighting_c1bf

Whether the light affects translucency or not. Disabling this can save GPU time when there are many small lights.

items.title: Transmission
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:light:bTransmissionHoudini parameterxn__unreallightbTransmission_5fbf

Whether light from this light transmits through surfaces with subsurface scattering profiles. Requires light to be movable.

items.title: Cast Ray Traced Shadows
items.text: DefaultUseProjectSettingUSD attributeunreal:light:CastRaytracedShadowHoudini parameterxn__unreallightCastRaytracedShadow_xpbf Value Label ECastRayTracedShadow::Disabled Disabled ECastRayTracedShadow::UseProjectSetting UseProjectSetting ECastRayTracedShadow::Enabled Enabled

items.title: Contact Shadow Length
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 0.1USD attributeunreal:light:ContactShadowLengthHoudini parameterxn__unreallightContactShadowLength_xpbf

Length of screen space ray trace for sharp contact shadows. Zero is disabled.

items.title: Contact Shadow Length In World Space Units
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:light:ContactShadowLengthInWSHoudini parameterxn__unreallightContactShadowLengthInWS_gwbf

Where Length of screen space ray trace for sharp contact shadows is in world space units or in screen space units.

items.title: Shadow Resolution Scale
items.text:
Default1Range0.125 to 8USD attributeunreal:light:ShadowResolutionScaleHoudini parameterxn__unreallightShadowResolutionScale_6sbf

Scales the resolution of shadowmaps used to shadow this light. By default shadowmap resolution is chosen based on screen size of the caster. Setting the scale to zero disables shadow maps, but does not disable, e.g., contact shadows. Note: shadowmap resolution is still clamped by 'r.Shadow.MaxResolution'

items.title: Shadow Bias
items.text:
Default0.5Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:light:ShadowBiasHoudini parameterxn__unreallightShadowBias_99af

Controls how accurate self shadowing of whole scene shadows from this light are. At 0, shadows will start at the their caster surface, but there will be many self shadowing artifacts. larger values, shadows will start further from their caster, and there won't be self shadowing artifacts but object might appear to fly. around 0.5 seems to be a good tradeoff. This also affects the soft transition of shadows

items.title: Shadow Slope Bias
items.text:
Default0.5Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:light:ShadowSlopeBiasHoudini parameterxn__unreallightShadowSlopeBias_fjbf

Controls how accurate self shadowing of whole scene shadows from this light are. This works in addition to shadow bias, by increasing the amount of bias depending on the slope of a surface. At 0, shadows will start at the their caster surface, but there will be many self shadowing artifacts. larger values, shadows will start further from their caster, and there won't be self shadowing artifacts but object might appear to fly. around 0.5 seems to be a good tradeoff. This also affects the soft transition of shadows

items.title: Light Function Material
items.text:
Default(empty)USD attributeunreal:light:LightFunctionMaterialHoudini parameterxn__unreallightLightFunctionMaterial_6sbf

The light function material to be applied to this light. Note that only non-lightmapped lights (UseDirectLightMap=False) can have a light function. Light functions are supported within VolumetricFog, but only for Directional, Point and Spot lights. Rect lights are not supported. Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

items.title: Light Function Scale
items.text:
Default1024, 1024, 1024USD attributeunreal:light:LightFunctionScaleHoudini parameterxn__unreallightLightFunctionScale_bobf

Scales the light function projection. X and Y scale in the directions perpendicular to the light's direction, Z scales along the light direction.

items.title: Fade Distance
items.text:
Default100000USD attributeunreal:light:LightFunctionFadeDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unreallightLightFunctionFadeDistance_pzbf

Distance at which the light function should be completely faded to DisabledBrightness. This is useful for hiding aliasing from light functions applied in the distance.

items.title: Disabled Brightness
items.text:
Default0.5Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:light:DisabledBrightnessHoudini parameterxn__unreallightDisabledBrightness_bobf

Brightness factor applied to the light when the light function is specified but disabled, for example in scene captures that use SceneCapView_LitNoShadows. This should be set to the average brightness of the light function material's emissive input, which should be between 0 and 1.

items.title: Light Shaft Bloom
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:light:bEnableLightShaftBloomHoudini parameterxn__unreallightbEnableLightShaftBloom_tubf

Whether to render light shaft bloom from this light. For directional lights, the color around the light direction will be blurred radially and added back to the scene. for point lights, the color on pixels closer than the light's SourceRadius will be blurred radially and added back to the scene.

items.title: Bloom Scale
items.text:
Default0.2Range0 to 10USD attributeunreal:light:BloomScaleHoudini parameterxn__unreallightBloomScale_99af

Scales the additive color.

items.title: Bloom Threshold
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 4USD attributeunreal:light:BloomThresholdHoudini parameterxn__unreallightBloomThreshold_shbf

Scene color must be larger than this to create bloom in the light shafts.

items.title: Bloom Tint
items.text:
Default1, 1, 1USD attributeunreal:light:BloomTintHoudini parameterxn__unreallightBloomTint_n8af

Multiplies against scene color to create the bloom color.

items.title: Atmosphere Sun Light
items.text:
DefaultOnUSD attributeunreal:light:bAtmosphereSunLightHoudini parameterxn__unreallightbAtmosphereSunLight_xpbf

Whether the directional light can interact with the atmosphere, cloud and generate a visual disk. All of which compose the visual sky.

items.title: Atmosphere Sun Light Index
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:light:AtmosphereSunLightIndexHoudini parameterxn__unreallightAtmosphereSunLightIndex_gwbf

Two atmosphere lights are supported. For instance: a sun and a moon, or two suns.

items.title: Atmosphere Sun Disk Color Scale
items.text:
Default1, 1, 1USD attributeunreal:light:AtmosphereSunDiskColorScaleHoudini parameterxn__unreallightAtmosphereSunDiskColorScale_y2bf

A color multiplied with the sun disk luminance.

items.title: Cast Shadows On Clouds
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:light:bCastShadowsOnCloudsHoudini parameterxn__unreallightbCastShadowsOnClouds_krbf

Whether the light should cast any shadows from opaque meshes onto clouds. This is disabled when 'Atmosphere Sun Light Index' is set to 1.

items.title: Cast Shadows On Atmosphere
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:light:bCastShadowsOnAtmosphereHoudini parameterxn__unreallightbCastShadowsOnAtmosphere_2xbf

Whether the light should cast any shadows from opaque meshes onto the atmosphere.

items.title: Cast Cloud Shadows
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:light:bCastCloudShadowsHoudini parameterxn__unreallightbCastCloudShadows_ombf

Whether the light should cast any shadows from clouds onto the atmosphere and other scene elements.

items.title: Cloud Shadow Strength
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:light:CloudShadowStrengthHoudini parameterxn__unreallightCloudShadowStrength_xpbf

The overall strength of the cloud shadow, higher value will block more light.

items.title: Cloud Shadow On Atmosphere Strength
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:light:CloudShadowOnAtmosphereStrengthHoudini parameterxn__unreallightCloudShadowOnAtmosphereStrength_h9bf

The strength of the shadow on atmosphere. Disabled when 0.

items.title: Cloud Shadow On Surface Strength
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:light:CloudShadowOnSurfaceStrengthHoudini parameterxn__unreallightCloudShadowOnSurfaceStrength_l4bf

The strength of the shadow on opaque and transparent meshes. Disabled when 0.

items.title: Cloud Scattered Luminance Scale
items.text:
Default1, 1, 1USD attributeunreal:light:CloudScatteredLuminanceScaleHoudini parameterxn__unreallightCloudScatteredLuminanceScale_l4bf

Scales the lights contribution when scattered in cloud participating media. This can help counter balance the fact that our multiple scattering solution is only an approximation. Setting this to 0 on the secondary atmospheric light will optimise the cloud tracing to only use a single light.

items.title: Light Shaft Occlusion
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:light:bEnableLightShaftOcclusionHoudini parameterxn__unreallightbEnableLightShaftOcclusion_c1bf

Whether to occlude fog and atmosphere inscattering with screenspace blurred occlusion from this light.

items.title: Occlusion Mask Darkness
items.text:
Default0.05Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:light:OcclusionMaskDarknessHoudini parameterxn__unreallightOcclusionMaskDarkness_6sbf

Controls how dark the occlusion masking is, a value of 1 results in no darkening term.

items.title: Occlusion Depth Range
items.text:
Default100000Range0 to 500000USD attributeunreal:light:OcclusionDepthRangeHoudini parameterxn__unreallightOcclusionDepthRange_xpbf

Everything closer to the camera than this distance will occlude light shafts.

items.title: Dynamic Shadow Distance MovableLight
items.text:
Default40000Range0 to 20000USD attributeunreal:light:DynamicShadowDistanceMovableLightHoudini parameterxn__unreallightDynamicShadowDistanceMovableLight_qdcf

How far Cascaded Shadow Map dynamic shadows will cover for a movable light, measured from the camera. A value of 0 disables the dynamic shadow.

items.title: Num Dynamic Shadow Cascades
items.text:
Default4Range0 to 4USD attributeunreal:light:DynamicShadowCascadesHoudini parameterxn__unreallightDynamicShadowCascades_6sbf

Number of cascades to split the view frustum into for the whole scene dynamic shadow. More cascades result in better shadow resolution, but adds significant rendering cost.

items.title: Barn Door Angle
items.text:
Default88Range0 to 90USD attributeunreal:light:BarnDoorAngleHoudini parameterxn__unreallightBarnDoorAngle_5fbf

Angle of barn door attached to the light source rect.

items.title: Barn Door Length
items.text:
Default0.1Range0 to 10USD attributeunreal:light:BarnDoorLengthHoudini parameterxn__unreallightBarnDoorLength_shbf

Length of barn door attached to the light source rect. hdUE shortens UE's 20 cm barn doors to 0.1 cm by default (UsdLux rect lights have none).

items.title: USD prim types
items.text: hdUE's codeless USD schemas (resources/generatedSchema.usda): Xformables whose properties are UE's, with UE's defaults as fallbacks. hdUE's Solaris LOPs author them.

items.title: UnrealLocalFogVolume
items.text: A UE Local Fog Volume (ULocalFogVolumeComponent), rendered by hdUE: UE's base volume, a sphere of radius 500 cm, fills the unit sphere of the prim's local space. Realtime only: UE's Path Tracer does not render local fog volumes.

items.title: Radial Fog Density
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 2USD attributeunreal:localFogVolume:RadialFogExtinctionHoudini parameterxn__unreallocalFogVolumeRadialFogExtinction_l4bo

The density of the radial fog representing its extinction coefficient at the center of the sphere. The final look of the volume is determined by combining the "Coverage=1-Transmittance" of both radial and height fog in order to achieve both soft edges and height fog.

items.title: Height Fog Density
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 2USD attributeunreal:localFogVolume:HeightFogExtinctionHoudini parameterxn__unreallocalFogVolumeHeightFogExtinction_l4bo

The density of the radial fog representing its extinction coefficient at height 0 in the unit sphere. The final look of the volume is determined by combining the "Coverage=1-Transmittance" of both radial and height fog in order to achieve both soft edges and height fog.

items.title: Height Fog Falloff
items.text:
Default1000Range1 to 5000USD attributeunreal:localFogVolume:HeightFogFalloffHoudini parameterxn__unreallocalFogVolumeHeightFogFalloff_pzbo

Controls how the density decreases as height increases. Smaller values make the visible transition larger. 1.0 is the lowest value before visual artifact are visible at the horizon.

items.title: Height Fog Offset
items.text:
Default0Range-2 to 2USD attributeunreal:localFogVolume:HeightFogOffsetHoudini parameterxn__unreallocalFogVolumeHeightFogOffset_2xbo

Height offset, relative to the actor Z position.

items.title: Scattering Distribution
items.text:
Default0.2Range0 to 0.999USD attributeunreal:localFogVolume:FogPhaseGHoudini parameterxn__unreallocalFogVolumeFogPhaseG_bobo

Controls the phase G parameter, describing the directionality of the scattering within this fog volume.

items.title: Fog Albedo
items.text:
Default1, 1, 1Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:localFogVolume:FogAlbedoHoudini parameterxn__unreallocalFogVolumeFogAlbedo_bobo

Controls the albedo of this fog volume.

items.title: Fog Emissive
items.text:
Default0, 0, 0USD attributeunreal:localFogVolume:FogEmissiveHoudini parameterxn__unreallocalFogVolumeFogEmissive_krbo

Controls the emissive color of this fog volume. (Unit = Luminance)

items.title: Start Distance
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 10USD attributeunreal:localFogVolume:FogStartDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unreallocalFogVolumeFogStartDistance_pzbo

Controls the distance after which this volume starts to appear. (Unit = Centimeter) This distance is clamped to be greater than r.LocalFogVolume.GlobalStartDistance.

items.title: Fog Sort Priority
items.text:
Default0Range-127 to 127USD attributeunreal:localFogVolume:FogSortPriorityHoudini parameterxn__unreallocalFogVolumeFogSortPriority_2xbo

The priority can be used as a way to override the sorting by distance. A lower value means the volume will be considered further away, i.e. it will draw behind the one with a higher priority value.

items.title: UnrealPostProcessVolume
items.text: A UE Post Process Volume (APostProcessVolume), rendered by hdUE: a box filling the cube from -1 to 1 of the prim's local space (a Cube prim's default extent), whose unreal:postProcess:\<FPostProcessSettings property> attributes blend into the view by UE's own rules (priority, blend radius and weight, unbound) while the camera is inside or near it. The render settings' unreal:postProcess:* apply after the volumes, as a camera's do in UE.

items.title: Priority
items.text:
Default0USD attributeunreal:postProcessVolume:PriorityHoudini parameterxn__unrealpostProcessVolumePriority_krbr

Priority of this volume. In the case of overlapping volumes the one with the highest priority overrides the lower priority ones. The order is undefined if two or more overlapping volumes have the same priority.

items.title: Blend Radius
items.text:
Default100Range0 to 6000USD attributeunreal:postProcessVolume:BlendRadiusHoudini parameterxn__unrealpostProcessVolumeBlendRadius_gwbr

World space radius around the volume that is used for blending (only if not unbound).

items.title: Blend Weight
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:postProcessVolume:BlendWeightHoudini parameterxn__unrealpostProcessVolumeBlendWeight_gwbr

0:no effect, 1:full effect

items.title: Enabled
items.text:
DefaultOnUSD attributeunreal:postProcessVolume:bEnabledHoudini parameterxn__unrealpostProcessVolumebEnabled_krbr

Whether this volume is enabled or not.

items.title: Infinite Extent (Unbound)
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:postProcessVolume:bUnboundHoudini parameterxn__unrealpostProcessVolumebUnbound_krbr

Whether this volume covers the whole world, or just the area inside its bounds.

items.title: UnrealExponentialHeightFog
items.text: A UE Exponential Height Fog (UExponentialHeightFogComponent), rendered by hdUE: its density is FogDensity at the prim's height (its world position along the up axis). It takes the place of the render settings' unreal:heightFog; UE draws one height fog, the first prim by path.

items.title: Fog Density
items.text:
Default0.02Range0 to 0.05USD attributeunreal:heightFog:FogDensityHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogFogDensity_shbj

Global density factor.

items.title: Fog Height Falloff
items.text:
Default0.2Range0.001 to 2USD attributeunreal:heightFog:FogHeightFalloffHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogFogHeightFalloff_krbj

Height density factor, controls how the density increases as height decreases. Smaller values make the visible transition larger.

items.title: Second Fog Density
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 0.05USD attributeunreal:heightFog:SecondFogData:FogDensityHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogSecondFogDataFogDensity_y2bjn

Global density factor for this fog. Density 0 turns the second fog off.

items.title: Second Fog Height Falloff
items.text:
Default0.2Range0.001 to 2USD attributeunreal:heightFog:SecondFogData:FogHeightFalloffHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogSecondFogDataFogHeightFalloff_qdcjn

Height density factor, controls how the density increases as height decreases. Smaller values make the visible transition larger.

items.title: Second Fog Height Offset
items.text:
Default0USD attributeunreal:heightFog:SecondFogData:FogHeightOffsetHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogSecondFogDataFogHeightOffset_3bcjn

Height offset, relative to the actor position Z.

items.title: Fog Inscattering Color
items.text:
Default0, 0, 0USD attributeunreal:heightFog:FogInscatteringLuminanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogFogInscatteringLuminance_l4bjRealtime only

Note: when r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored and the volumetric fog Emissive is used instead.

items.title: Sky Atmosphere Ambient Contribution Color Scale
items.text:
Default1, 1, 1USD attributeunreal:heightFog:SkyAtmosphereAmbientContributionColorScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogSkyAtmosphereAmbientContributionColorScale_wycjRealtime only

Color used to modulate the SkyAtmosphere component contribution to the non directional component of the fog. Only effective when r.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog>0

items.title: Inscattering Color Cubemap
items.text:
Default(empty)USD attributeunreal:heightFog:InscatteringColorCubemapHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogInscatteringColorCubemap_l4bjRealtime only

Cubemap that can be specified for fog color, which is useful to make distant, heavily fogged scene elements match the sky. When the cubemap is specified, FogInscatteringColor is ignored and Directional inscattering is disabled. Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

items.title: Sky Light Capture In-Scattering Strength
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:heightFog:SkyLightCaptureAffectsHeightFogStrengthHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogSkyLightCaptureAffectsHeightFogStrength_0tcjRealtime only

When >0 and when r.SupportsSkyLightCaptureAffectsHeightFogInScattering is true, this will make the sky light capture inject scattered light into the height fog.

items.title: Sky Light Capture In-Scattering Roughness
items.text:
Default0.15Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:heightFog:SkyLightCaptureAffectsHeightFogRoughnessHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogSkyLightCaptureAffectsHeightFogRoughness_nvcjRealtime only

This is the roughness at which the sky light capture cubemap will be sample to simulate scattering dispersion due to a phase function.

items.title: Inscattering Color Cubemap Angle
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 360USD attributeunreal:heightFog:InscatteringColorCubemapAngleHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogInscatteringColorCubemapAngle_qdcjRealtime only

Angle to rotate the InscatteringColorCubemap around the Z axis.

items.title: Inscattering Texture Tint
items.text:
Default1, 1, 1USD attributeunreal:heightFog:InscatteringTextureTintHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogInscatteringTextureTint_y2bjRealtime only

Tint color used when InscatteringColorCubemap is specified, for quick edits without having to reimport InscatteringColorCubemap.

items.title: Fully Directional Inscattering Color Distance
items.text:
Default100000Range1000 to 1000000USD attributeunreal:heightFog:FullyDirectionalInscatteringColorDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogFullyDirectionalInscatteringColorDistance_9wcjRealtime only

Distance at which InscatteringColorCubemap should be used directly for the Inscattering Color.

items.title: Non Directional Inscattering Color Distance
items.text:
Default1000Range1000 to 1000000USD attributeunreal:heightFog:NonDirectionalInscatteringColorDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogNonDirectionalInscatteringColorDistance_0tcjRealtime only

Distance at which only the average color of InscatteringColorCubemap should be used as Inscattering Color.

items.title: Directional Inscattering Exponent
items.text:
Default4Range2 to 64USD attributeunreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringExponentHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogDirectionalInscatteringExponent_zgcjRealtime only

Controls the size of the directional inscattering cone, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - there must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored and the volumetric fog Scattering Distribution is used instead.

items.title: Directional Inscattering Start Distance
items.text:
Default10000USD attributeunreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringStartDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogDirectionalInscatteringStartDistance_4ocjRealtime only

Controls the start distance from the viewer of the directional inscattering, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - There must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored.

items.title: Directional Inscattering Color
items.text:
Default0, 0, 0USD attributeunreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringLuminanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogDirectionalInscatteringLuminance_micjRealtime only

Controls the color of the directional inscattering, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - there must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored.

items.title: Fog Max Opacity
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:heightFog:FogMaxOpacityHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogFogMaxOpacity_ombjRealtime only

Maximum opacity of the fog. A value of 1 means the fog can become fully opaque at a distance and replace scene color completely, A value of 0 means the fog color will not be factored in at all.

items.title: Start Distance
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 5000USD attributeunreal:heightFog:StartDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogStartDistance_ombjRealtime only

Distance from the camera that the fog will start, in world units.

items.title: End Distance
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 500000USD attributeunreal:heightFog:EndDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogEndDistance_fjbjRealtime only

Distance from the camera, on the horizontal XY plane, that the fog will end integrating the lighting and transmittance. Disabled when 0.

items.title: Fog Cutoff Distance
items.text:
Default0Range100000 to 20000000USD attributeunreal:heightFog:FogCutoffDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogFogCutoffDistance_6sbjRealtime only

Scene elements past this distance will not have fog applied. This is useful for excluding skyboxes which already have fog baked in.

items.title: Volumetric Fog
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:heightFog:bEnableVolumetricFogHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogbEnableVolumetricFog_2xbj

Whether to enable Volumetric fog. Scalability settings control the resolution of the fog simulation. Note that Volumetric fog currently does not support StartDistance, FogMaxOpacity and FogCutoffDistance. Volumetric fog also can't match exponential height fog in general as exponential height fog has non-physical behavior.

items.title: Scattering Distribution
items.text:
Default0.2Range-0.9 to 0.9USD attributeunreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogScatteringDistributionHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogScatteringDistribution_incj

Controls the scattering phase function - how much incoming light scatters in various directions. A distribution value of 0 scatters equally in all directions, while .9 scatters predominantly in the light direction. In order to have visible volumetric fog light shafts from the side, the distribution will need to be closer to 0.

items.title: Albedo
items.text:
Default1, 1, 1USD attributeunreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogAlbedoHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogAlbedo_gwbj

The height fog particle reflectiveness used by volumetric fog. Water particles in air have an albedo near white, while dust has slightly darker value.

items.title: Emissive
items.text:
Default0, 0, 0USD attributeunreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogEmissiveHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogEmissive_pzbjRealtime only

Light emitted by height fog. This is a density so more light is emitted the further you are looking through the fog. In most cases skylight is a better choice, however right now volumetric fog does not support precomputed lighting, So stationary skylights are unshadowed and static skylights don't affect volumetric fog at all.

items.title: Extinction Scale
items.text:
Default1Range0.1 to 10USD attributeunreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogExtinctionScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogExtinctionScale_3bcj

Scales the height fog particle extinction amount used by volumetric fog. Values larger than 1 cause fog particles everywhere absorb more light.

items.title: View Distance
items.text:
Default6000Range1000 to 10000USD attributeunreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogDistance_pzbj

Distance over which volumetric fog should be computed, after the start distance. Larger values extend the effect into the distance but expose under-sampling artifacts in details.

items.title: Start Distance
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 5000USD attributeunreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogStartDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogStartDistance_u7bjRealtime only

Distance from the camera that the volumetric fog will start, in world units.

items.title: Near Fade In Distance
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 1000USD attributeunreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogNearFadeInDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogNearFadeInDistance_zgcjRealtime only

Distance over which volumetric fog will fade in from the start distance.

items.title: Static Lighting Scattering Intensity
items.text: Default1Range0 to 10USD attributeunreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogStaticLightingScatteringIntensityHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogStaticLightingScatteringIntensity_f5cjRealtime only

items.title: Override Light Colors With Fog Inscattering Colors
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:heightFog:bOverrideLightColorsWithFogInscatteringColorsHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogbOverrideLightColorsWithFogInscatteringColors_s3cjRealtime onlyAdvanced

Whether to use FogInscatteringColor for the Sky Light volumetric scattering color and DirectionalInscatteringColor for the Directional Light scattering color. Make sure your directional light has 'Atmosphere Sun Light' enabled! Enabling this allows Volumetric fog to better match Height fog in the distance, but produces non-physical volumetric lighting that may not match surface lighting.

items.title: Enable Fog Screen Space Scattering
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:heightFog:bEnableFSSSHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogbEnableFSSS_fjbjRealtime onlyAdvanced

Enable FSSS (Fog Screen Space Scattering) to approximate multiple scattering.

items.title: Scene Color Scattering Amount Scale
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:heightFog:FSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogFSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountScale_incjRealtime onlyAdvanced

The amount of scene color injected into the fog screen space scattering technique. When 0, only the fog luminance will be scattered. When 1, fog and scene luminance will be scattered. When above 1, more scene color can be injected to increase the brightness of the multiple scattering effect, even when the fog is not too intense. We cannot scatter more than the scene color however.

items.title: Scene Color Scattering Amount Power
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 2USD attributeunreal:heightFog:FSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountPowerHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogFSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountPower_incjRealtime onlyAdvanced

Apply a power over the amount of scattered scene luminance after it is evaluated using Scene Color Scattering Amount Scale. A value smaller than 1 can show more scattering where the fog is less intense.

items.title: Spread Scale
items.text:
Default0.1Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:heightFog:FSSSSpreadScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogFSSSSpreadScale_xpbjRealtime onlyAdvanced

The scale of the spread for the fog multiple scattering. This basically scales mip level sampled from the blurred screen space FSSS texture. Increasing will make scene and thicker fog look fuzzier. But too high values can cause artifacts such as halos around depth discontinuities.

items.title: Blur Control
items.text:
Default0.5Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:heightFog:FSSSBlurControlHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogFSSSBlurControl_xpbjRealtime onlyAdvanced

When generating the the blurred screen space FSSS texture, this controls how much of the blurred lower mip levels is injected back into the sharper higher mip levels. A higher value will result in a blurrier result. But when = 1, multiple scattering will be a single average color of the FSSS texture.

items.title: Holdout
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:heightFog:bHoldoutHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogbHoldout_jebjAdvanced

If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

items.title: Render In Main Pass
items.text:
DefaultOnUSD attributeunreal:heightFog:bRenderInMainPassHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogbRenderInMainPass_6sbjAdvanced

If true, this component will be rendered in the main pass (basepass, transparency)

items.title: Visible In Reflection Captures
items.text:
DefaultOnUSD attributeunreal:heightFog:bVisibleInReflectionCapturesHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogbVisibleInReflectionCaptures_3bcjRealtime onlyAdvanced

If true, this component will be visible in reflection captures.

items.title: Visible In Real Time Sky Captures
items.text:
DefaultOnUSD attributeunreal:heightFog:bVisibleInRealTimeSkyCapturesHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogbVisibleInRealTimeSkyCaptures_qdcjRealtime onlyAdvanced

If true, this component will be visible in real-time sky light reflection captures.

items.title: UnrealSkyAtmosphere
items.text: A UE Sky Atmosphere (USkyAtmosphereComponent), rendered by hdUE, at the prim's world position (UE's Transform Mode decides whether it is used). It takes the place of the render settings' unreal:skyAtmosphere; UE draws one, the first prim by path.

items.title: Transform Mode
items.text:
DefaultPlanetTopAtAbsoluteWorldOriginUSD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:TransformModeHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereTransformMode_6sbn

The ground albedo that will tint the atmosphere when the sun light will bounce on it. Only taken into account when MultiScattering>0.0.

Value Label ESkyAtmosphereTransformMode::PlanetTopAtAbsoluteWorldOrigin PlanetTopAtAbsoluteWorldOrigin ESkyAtmosphereTransformMode::PlanetTopAtComponentTransform PlanetTopAtComponentTransform ESkyAtmosphereTransformMode::PlanetCenterAtComponentTransform PlanetCenterAtComponentTransform

items.title: Ground Radius
items.text:
Default6360Range0.1 to 10000USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:BottomRadiusHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereBottomRadius_krbn

The radius in kilometers from the center of the planet to the ground level.

items.title: Ground Albedo
items.text:
Default0.401978, 0.401978, 0.401978USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:GroundAlbedoHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereGroundAlbedo_krbn

The ground albedo that will tint the atmosphere when the sun light will bounce on it. Only taken into account when MultiScattering>0.0.

items.title: Atmosphere Height
items.text:
Default60Range0.1 to 200USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:AtmosphereHeightHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereAtmosphereHeight_2xbn

The height of the atmosphere layer above the ground in kilometers.

items.title: MultiScattering
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 100USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:MultiScatteringFactorHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereMultiScatteringFactor_75bnRealtime only

Factor applied to multiple scattering only (after the sun light has bounced around in the atmosphere at least once). Multiple scattering is evaluated using a dual scattering approach. A value of 2 is recommended to better represent default atmosphere when r.SkyAtmosphere.MultiScatteringLUT.HighQuality=0.

items.title: Trace Sample Count Scale
items.text:
Default1Range0.25 to 8USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:TraceSampleCountScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereTraceSampleCountScale_75bnRealtime onlyAdvanced

Scale the atmosphere tracing sample count. Quality level scalability The sample count is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.SkyAtmosphere.SampleCountMax' when 'r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT' is 0. The sample count is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT.SampleCountMax' when 'r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT' is 1. The sample count is still clamped for aerial perspective according to 'r.SkyAtmosphere.AerialPerspectiveLUT.SampleCountMaxPerSlice'.

items.title: Rayleigh Scattering Scale
items.text:
Default0.0331Range0 to 2USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:RayleighScatteringScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereRayleighScatteringScale_h9bn

Rayleigh scattering coefficient scale.

items.title: Rayleigh Scattering
items.text:
Default0.1752870090634441, 0.40960725075528703, 1USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:RayleighScatteringHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereRayleighScattering_c1bn

The Rayleigh scattering coefficients resulting from molecules in the air at an altitude of 0 kilometer.

items.title: Rayleigh Exponential Distribution
items.text:
Default8Range0.001 to 20USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:RayleighExponentialDistributionHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereRayleighExponentialDistribution_incn

The altitude in kilometer at which Rayleigh scattering effect is reduced to 40%.

items.title: Mie Scattering Scale
items.text:
Default0.003996Range0 to 5USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:MieScatteringScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereMieScatteringScale_c1bn

Mie scattering coefficient scale.

items.title: Mie Scattering
items.text:
Default1, 1, 1USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:MieScatteringHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereMieScattering_6sbn

The Mie scattering coefficients resulting from particles in the air at an altitude of 0 kilometer. As it becomes higher, light will be scattered more.

items.title: Mie Absorption Scale
items.text:
Default0.000444Range0 to 5USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:MieAbsorptionScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereMieAbsorptionScale_c1bn

Mie absorption coefficient scale.

items.title: Mie Absorption
items.text:
Default1, 1, 1USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:MieAbsorptionHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereMieAbsorption_6sbn

The Mie absorption coefficients resulting from particles in the air at an altitude of 0 kilometer. As it becomes higher, light will be absorbed more.

items.title: Mie Anisotropy
items.text:
Default0.8Range0 to 0.999USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:MieAnisotropyHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereMieAnisotropy_6sbn

A value of 0 mean light is uniformly scattered. A value closer to 1 means lights will scatter more forward, resulting in halos around light sources.

items.title: Mie Exponential Distribution
items.text:
Default1.2Range0.001 to 10USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:MieExponentialDistributionHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereMieExponentialDistribution_dfcn

The altitude in kilometer at which Mie effects are reduced to 40%.

items.title: Absorption Scale
items.text:
Default0.001881Range0 to 0.2USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:OtherAbsorptionScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereOtherAbsorptionScale_l4bn

Absorption coefficients for another atmosphere layer. Density increase from 0 to 1 between 10 to 25km and decreases from 1 to 0 between 25 to 40km. This approximates ozone molecules distribution in the Earth atmosphere.

items.title: Absorption
items.text:
Default0.34556087187666135, 1, 0.045188729399255716USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:OtherAbsorptionHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereOtherAbsorption_gwbn

Absorption coefficients for another atmosphere layer. Density increase from 0 to 1 between 10 to 25km and decreases from 1 to 0 between 25 to 40km. The default values represents ozone molecules absorption in the Earth atmosphere.

items.title: Sky Luminance Factor
items.text:
Default1, 1, 1USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:SkyLuminanceFactorHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereSkyLuminanceFactor_c1bnRealtime only

Scales the luminance of pixels representing the sky. This will impact the captured sky light.

items.title: Sky And Aerial Perspective Luminance Factor
items.text:
Default1, 1, 1USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:SkyAndAerialPerspectiveLuminanceFactorHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereSkyAndAerialPerspectiveLuminanceFactor_wycnRealtime only

Scales the luminance of pixels representing the sky and the aerial perspective. This will impact the captured sky light.

items.title: Aerial Perspective View Distance Scale
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 3USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:AerialPespectiveViewDistanceScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereAerialPespectiveViewDistanceScale_rqcnRealtime only

Makes the aerial perspective look thicker by scaling distances from view to surfaces (opaque and translucent).

items.title: Height Fog Contribution
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:HeightFogContributionHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereHeightFogContribution_75bnRealtime only

Scale the sky and atmosphere lights contribution to the height fog when SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog project setting is true.

items.title: Transmittance Min Light Elevation Angle
items.text:
Default-90Range-90 to 90USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:TransmittanceMinLightElevationAngleHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereTransmittanceMinLightElevationAngle_0tcnRealtime only

The minimum elevation angle in degree that should be used to evaluate the sun transmittance to the ground. Useful to maintain a visible sun light and shadow on meshes even when the sun has started going below the horizon. This does not affect the aerial perspective.

items.title: Aerial Perspective Start Depth
items.text:
Default0.1Range0.001 to 10USD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:AerialPerspectiveStartDepthHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphereAerialPerspectiveStartDepth_zgcnRealtime only

The distance (kilometers) at which we start evaluating the aerial perspective. Having the aerial perspective starts away from the camera can help with performance: pixels not affected by the aerial perspective will have their computation skipped using early depth test.

items.title: Holdout
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:bHoldoutHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmospherebHoldout_1kbnAdvanced

If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

items.title: Render In Main Pass
items.text:
DefaultOnUSD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphere:bRenderInMainPassHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmospherebRenderInMainPass_pzbnAdvanced

If true, this component will be rendered in the main pass (basepass, transparency)

items.title: UnrealVolumetricCloud
items.text: A UE Volumetric Cloud (UVolumetricCloudComponent), rendered by hdUE with a Sky Atmosphere. It takes the place of the render settings' unreal:volumetricCloud; UE draws one, the first prim by path.

items.title: Layer Bottom Altitude
items.text:
Default5Range0 to 20USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:LayerBottomAltitudeHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudLayerBottomAltitude_75bp

The altitude at which the cloud layer starts. (kilometers above the ground)

items.title: Layer Height
items.text:
