Default10Range0.1 to 20USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:LayerHeightHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudLayerHeight_6sbp

The height of the the cloud layer. (kilometers above the layer bottom altitude)

items.title: Tracing Start Max Distance
items.text:
Default350Range1 to 500USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:TracingStartMaxDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudTracingStartMaxDistance_qdcp

The maximum distance of the volumetric surface, i.e. cloud layer upper and lower bound, before which we will accept to start tracing. (kilometers)

items.title: Tracing Start Distance From Camera
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 100USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:TracingStartDistanceFromCameraHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudTracingStartDistanceFromCamera_4ocpRealtime only

The distance from which the tracing will start. This is useful when the camera for instance is inside the layer of cloud. (kilometers)

items.title: Tracing Max Distance
items.text:
Default50Range0.1 to 500USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:TracingMaxDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudTracingMaxDistance_l4bp

The maximum distance that will be traced inside the cloud layer. (kilometers)

items.title: Planet Radius
items.text:
Default6360Range0.1 to 10000USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:PlanetRadiusHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudPlanetRadius_tubp

The planet radius used when there is not SkyAtmosphere component present in the scene.

items.title: Ground Albedo
items.text:
Default0.401978, 0.401978, 0.401978USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:GroundAlbedoHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudGroundAlbedo_tubp

The ground albedo used to light the cloud from below with respect to the sun light and sky atmosphere. This is only used by the cloud material when the 'Volumetric Advanced' node have GroundContribution enabled.

items.title: Material
items.text:
Default(empty)USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:MaterialHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudMaterial_bobp

The material describing the cloud volume. It must be a Volume domain material. Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

items.title: Use Per Sample Atmospheric Light Transmittance
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:bUsePerSampleAtmosphericLightTransmittanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudbUsePerSampleAtmosphericLightTransmittance_o8cpRealtime only

Whether to apply atmosphere transmittance per sample, instead of using the light global transmittance.

items.title: Sky Light Cloud Bottom Occlusion
items.text:
Default0.5Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:SkyLightCloudBottomOcclusionHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudSkyLightCloudBottomOcclusion_vlcpRealtime only

Occlude the sky light contribution at the bottom of the cloud layer. This is a fast approximation to sky lighting being occluded by cloud without having to trace rays or sample AO texture. Ignored if the cloud material explicitely sets the ambient occlusion value.

items.title: View Sample Count Scale
items.text:
Default1Range0.05 to 8USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:ViewSampleCountScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudViewSampleCountScale_u7bpRealtime only

Scale the tracing sample count in primary views. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.ViewRaySampleCountMax'.

items.title: Reflection View Sample Count Scale Value
items.text:
Default1Range0.05 to 8USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:ReflectionViewSampleCountScaleValueHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudReflectionViewSampleCountScaleValue_9wcpRealtime only

Scale the tracing sample count in reflection views. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.ReflectionRaySampleMaxCount'.

items.title: Shadow View Sample Count Scale
items.text:
Default1Range0.05 to 8USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:ShadowViewSampleCountScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudShadowViewSampleCountScale_micpRealtime only

Scale the shadow tracing sample count in primary views, only used with Advanced Output ray marched shadows. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.Shadow.ViewRaySampleMaxCount'.

items.title: Shadow Reflection View Sample Count Scale Value
items.text:
Default1Range0.05 to 8USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:ShadowReflectionViewSampleCountScaleValueHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudShadowReflectionViewSampleCountScaleValue_16cpRealtime only

Scale the shadow tracing sample count in reflection views, only used with Advanced Output ray marched shadows. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.Shadow.ReflectionRaySampleMaxCount'.

items.title: Shadow Tracing Distance
items.text:
Default15Range0.01 to 50USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:ShadowTracingDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudShadowTracingDistance_h9bpRealtime only

The shadow tracing distance in kilometers, only used with Advanced Output ray marched shadows.

items.title: Stop Tracing Transmittance Threshold
items.text:
Default0.005Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:StopTracingTransmittanceThresholdHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudStopTracingTransmittanceThreshold_0tcpRealtime only

When the mean transmittance is below this threshold, we stop tracing. This is a good way to reduce the ray marched sample count, and thus to increase performance.

items.title: Aerial Pespective Rayleigh Scattering Start Distance
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 100USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveRayleighScatteringStartDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudAerialPespectiveRayleighScatteringStartDistance_thdpRealtime only

Specify the aerial perspective start distance on cloud for Rayleigh scattering only. (kilometers)

items.title: Aerial Pespective Rayleigh Scattering Fade Distance
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 100USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveRayleighScatteringFadeDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudAerialPespectiveRayleighScatteringFadeDistance_6fdpRealtime only

Specify the distance over which the Rayleigh scattering will linearly ramp up to full effect. (kilometers)

items.title: Aerial Pespective Mie Scattering Start Distance
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 100USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveMieScatteringStartDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudAerialPespectiveMieScatteringStartDistance_o8cpRealtime only

Specify the aerial perspective start distance on cloud for Mie scattering only. (kilometers)

items.text:
Default0Range0 to 100USD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveMieScatteringFadeDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudAerialPespectiveMieScatteringFadeDistance_16cpRealtime only

Specify the distance over which the Rayleigh scattering will linearly ramp up to full effect. (kilometers)

If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

items.title: Visible In Real Time Sky Captures
items.text:
DefaultOnUSD attributeunreal:volumetricCloud:bVisibleInRealTimeSkyCapturesHoudini parameterxn__unrealvolumetricCloudbVisibleInRealTimeSkyCaptures_incpRealtime onlyAdvanced

If true, this component will be visible in real-time sky light reflection captures.

items.title: UnrealDecal
items.text: A UE decal (UDecalComponent), rendered by hdUE: its material projected onto the surfaces inside a box filling the cube from -1 to 1 of the prim's local space, along the prim's local down axis (the stage's up axis, negated). Its material is the bound material (a prepared Substrate Builder decal material), else unreal:decal:DecalMaterial, a cooked path.

items.title: Decal Material
items.text:
Default(empty)USD attributeunreal:decal:DecalMaterialHoudini parameterxn__unrealdecalDecalMaterial_5fbf

Decal material. Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

items.title: Sort Order
items.text:
Default0USD attributeunreal:decal:SortOrderHoudini parameterxn__unrealdecalSortOrder_n8af

Controls the order in which decal elements are rendered. Higher values draw later (on top). Setting many different sort orders on many different decals prevents sorting by state and can reduce performance.

items.title: Fade Screen Size
items.text: Default0.01USD attributeunreal:decal:FadeScreenSizeHoudini parameterxn__unrealdecalFadeScreenSize_shbf

items.title: Decal Color
items.text:
Default1, 1, 1USD attributeunreal:decal:DecalColorHoudini parameterxn__unrealdecalDecalColor_99af

Decal color, can be accessed using the material Decal Color node.

items.title: Houdini nodes
items.text: The digital assets hdUE installs, with the help Houdini shows for them (F1 on a node), generated from the assets themselves.

items.title: Solaris nodes (LOPs)
items.text: Node Summary hdUE Decal Creates or edits a UE decal: a box projecting its material onto the surfaces it covers. hdUE Height Fog Creates or edits a UE Exponential Height Fog: fog thickest below the prim's height. hdUE Local Fog Volume Creates or edits a UE Local Fog Volume: a sphere of fog that fades out radially, rendered by hdUE. hdUE Local Fog Volume 1.0 Creates a UE Local Fog Volume: a sphere of fog that fades out radially, rendered by hdUE. hdUE Post Process Volume Creates or edits a UE Post Process Volume: a box whose post-process settings blend in while the camera is inside or near it. hdUE Render Products Creates render products sharing common settings. hdUE Render Settings Renders the stage with Unreal Engine: render settings, camera, resolution, output and AOVs. hdUE Sky Atmosphere Creates or edits a UE Sky Atmosphere: UE's physical sky, lit by the distant lights. hdUE Standard Render Vars Creates the render vars (AOVs) hdUE renders. hdUE Unreal Asset Places an asset from a UE project (a Niagara effect, a mesh, a Blueprint, a level) and imports it into hdUE. hdUE Volumetric Cloud Creates or edits a UE Volumetric Cloud layer, drawn with a Sky Atmosphere.

items.title: Substrate Builder nodes (VOPs)
items.text: Node Summary Blackbody The color of a black body at a temperature (UE's BlackBody expression), for fire and hot gases. Color Constant A constant color. Color Parameter A named color parameter of the material, editable on the material without recompiling. Color Ramp Maps a float to a color through a ramp (a UE curve in the material's curve atlas), for example density to smoke color. Extract Channel Extracts one channel of an RGBA value. Float Constant A constant float. Float Mask Primvar [0..1] Reads a float primvar of the mesh in [0, 1] as a mask, for example wetness. One per graph. Float Multiply Multiplies two floats. Float Ramp Remaps a float through a ramp (a UE curve in the material's curve atlas). Float Saturate Clamps a float to [0, 1]. Float to Color Copies a float into red, green and blue. Haziness to Second Roughness Converts a roughness and a haziness into a Slab's second roughness and its weight (a hazy gloss). MaterialX Surface A MaterialX material on the stage, from the prepared MaterialX library, used as a Substrate surface. Metalness to Albedo and F0 Converts metalness-workflow values (base color, metallic, specular) into a Slab's diffuse albedo and F0. Normal Map Decodes a tangent-space normal map for a Slab's Normal input. Scalar Parameter A named float parameter of the material, editable on the material without recompiling. Substrate Add Adds two surfaces' light (Substrate Add), as for a glow over a surface. Substrate Convert To Decal A decal material for hdUE Decal prims: UE's Substrate Convert To Decal over a surface, projected onto what the decal's box covers. Wire it to the builder's output, and bind the material to the decal prim. Substrate Eye UE's Substrate Eye BSDF, for eyes modeled as UE's eye shading expects (cornea, iris and their normals). Substrate Hair UE's Substrate Hair BSDF, for hair cards. Substrate Horizontal Mix Mixes two surfaces side by side (Substrate horizontal mixing). Substrate Select Picks one of two surfaces where Select is below or above the threshold (Substrate Select). Substrate Single Layer Water UE's Substrate Single Layer Water BSDF: a water surface with its medium below, rendered by UE's water pass. It must be the material's whole surface. Substrate Slab One Substrate slab: diffuse and specular reflection, with optional simple-volume subsurface scattering. Substrate Thin Film Iridescence of a thin film (soap bubbles, oil, coatings): F0 and F90 for a Slab (Substrate Thin-Film). Substrate Unlit An emissive surface without lighting. Substrate Vertical Layer Layers one surface over another (Substrate vertical layering). Substrate Volumetric Fog Cloud A volume material for Volume prims: UE's Substrate Volumetric Fog Cloud BSDF, rendered as a heterogeneous volume. Wire it to the builder's output, and bind the material to a Volume prim. Substrate Weight Scales a surface's coverage. Texture Sample Samples an image file, or UDIM tiles from a  pattern. Transmittance to MFP Converts the color light keeps through a thickness into a Slab's mean free path. UV Coordinates The mesh's UV set, scaled then offset. Volume Field A grid of the Volume prim at the shaded point. hdUE Substrate Builder Composes a UE Substrate material from hdUE Substrate nodes. Like a Karma Material Builder, it goes in a Material Library LOP (or /mat, with the library's Material VOP pointing at it), which authors the material's typed USD graph; hdUE prepares that graph into a native Substrate material.

items.title: hdUE Decal
items.text:
ContextLOP nodeTypehdue::hduedecal::1.0

Creates or edits a UE decal: a box projecting its material onto the surfaces it covers.

Like a Decal Actor placed in a UE level, it creates or edits an UnrealDecal prim: a box filling the cube from -1 to 1 of its local space (Uniform Scale 1 is a 2-unit box), projecting along the prim's local down axis. Its material is the material bound to the prim (Assign Material LOP), a Substrate Builder decal material (hdUE Substrate Material Builder, decal preset) prepared for hdUE, applied in Houdini's viewport; else Decal Material, a cooked Deferred Decal material path. Decal Color tints it, Sort Order orders overlapping decals, and Fade Screen Size hides it below that screen size.

items.title: Decal
items.text:
Decal Material

Decal material. Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

USD attribute unreal:decal:DecalMaterial Sort Order

Controls the order in which decal elements are rendered. Higher values draw later (on top). Setting many different sort orders on many different decals prevents sorting by state and can reduce performance.

USD attribute unreal:decal:SortOrder Default 0 Decal Color

Decal color, can be accessed using the material Decal Color node.

USD attribute unreal:decal:DecalColor Default 1, 1, 1

items.title: hdUE Height Fog
items.text:
ContextLOP nodeTypehdue::hdueheightfog::1.0

Creates or edits a UE Exponential Height Fog: fog thickest below the prim's height.

Like an Exponential Height Fog placed in a UE level, it creates or edits an UnrealExponentialHeightFog prim: the fog's density is Fog Density at the prim's height (its world position along the up axis), with UE's properties (Volumetric Fog included). A prim takes the place of hdUE Render Settings' Fog tab; UE draws one height fog, the first prim by path. Each property's control starts at Do Nothing: the prim's fallback is UE's default.

items.title: Exponential Height Fog Component
items.text:
Fog Density

Global density factor.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:FogDensity Default 0.02 Fog Height Falloff

Height density factor, controls how the density increases as height decreases. Smaller values make the visible transition larger.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:FogHeightFalloff Default 0.2 Second Fog Density

Global density factor for this fog. Density 0 turns the second fog off.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:SecondFogData:FogDensity Default 0 Second Fog Height Falloff

Height density factor, controls how the density increases as height decreases. Smaller values make the visible transition larger.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:SecondFogData:FogHeightFalloff Default 0.2 Second Fog Height Offset

Height offset, relative to the actor position Z.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:SecondFogData:FogHeightOffset Default 0 Fog Inscattering Color

Note: when r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored and the volumetric fog Emissive is used instead.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:FogInscatteringLuminance Default 0, 0, 0 Sky Atmosphere Ambient Contribution Color Scale

Color used to modulate the SkyAtmosphere component contribution to the non directional component of the fog. Only effective when r.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog>0

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:SkyAtmosphereAmbientContributionColorScale Default 1, 1, 1 Fog Max Opacity

Maximum opacity of the fog. A value of 1 means the fog can become fully opaque at a distance and replace scene color completely, A value of 0 means the fog color will not be factored in at all.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:FogMaxOpacity Default 1 Start Distance

Distance from the camera that the fog will start, in world units.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:StartDistance Default 0 End Distance

Distance from the camera, on the horizontal XY plane, that the fog will end integrating the lighting and transmittance. Disabled when 0.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:EndDistance Default 0 Fog Cutoff Distance

Scene elements past this distance will not have fog applied. This is useful for excluding skyboxes which already have fog baked in.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:FogCutoffDistance Default 0

items.title: Inscattering Texture
items.text:
Inscattering Color Cubemap

Cubemap that can be specified for fog color, which is useful to make distant, heavily fogged scene elements match the sky. When the cubemap is specified, FogInscatteringColor is ignored and Directional inscattering is disabled. Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:InscatteringColorCubemap Sky Light Capture In-Scattering Strength

When >0 and when r.SupportsSkyLightCaptureAffectsHeightFogInScattering is true, this will make the sky light capture inject scattered light into the height fog.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:SkyLightCaptureAffectsHeightFogStrength Default 0 Sky Light Capture In-Scattering Roughness

This is the roughness at which the sky light capture cubemap will be sample to simulate scattering dispersion due to a phase function.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:SkyLightCaptureAffectsHeightFogRoughness Default 0.15 Inscattering Color Cubemap Angle

Angle to rotate the InscatteringColorCubemap around the Z axis.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:InscatteringColorCubemapAngle Default 0 Inscattering Texture Tint

Tint color used when InscatteringColorCubemap is specified, for quick edits without having to reimport InscatteringColorCubemap.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:InscatteringTextureTint Default 1, 1, 1 Fully Directional Inscattering Color Distance

Distance at which InscatteringColorCubemap should be used directly for the Inscattering Color.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:FullyDirectionalInscatteringColorDistance Default 100000 Non Directional Inscattering Color Distance

Distance at which only the average color of InscatteringColorCubemap should be used as Inscattering Color.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:NonDirectionalInscatteringColorDistance Default 1000

items.title: Directional Inscattering
items.text:
Directional Inscattering Exponent

Controls the size of the directional inscattering cone, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - there must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored and the volumetric fog Scattering Distribution is used instead.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringExponent Default 4 Directional Inscattering Start Distance

Controls the start distance from the viewer of the directional inscattering, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - There must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringStartDistance Default 10000 Directional Inscattering Color

Controls the color of the directional inscattering, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - there must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringLuminance Default 0, 0, 0

items.title: Volumetric Fog
items.text:
Volumetric Fog

Whether to enable Volumetric fog. Scalability settings control the resolution of the fog simulation. Note that Volumetric fog currently does not support StartDistance, FogMaxOpacity and FogCutoffDistance. Volumetric fog also can't match exponential height fog in general as exponential height fog has non-physical behavior.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:bEnableVolumetricFog Default Off Scattering Distribution

Controls the scattering phase function - how much incoming light scatters in various directions. A distribution value of 0 scatters equally in all directions, while .9 scatters predominantly in the light direction. In order to have visible volumetric fog light shafts from the side, the distribution will need to be closer to 0.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogScatteringDistribution Default 0.2 Albedo

The height fog particle reflectiveness used by volumetric fog. Water particles in air have an albedo near white, while dust has slightly darker value.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogAlbedo Default 1, 1, 1 Emissive

Light emitted by height fog. This is a density so more light is emitted the further you are looking through the fog. In most cases skylight is a better choice, however right now volumetric fog does not support precomputed lighting, So stationary skylights are unshadowed and static skylights don't affect volumetric fog at all.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogEmissive Default 0, 0, 0 Extinction Scale

Scales the height fog particle extinction amount used by volumetric fog. Values larger than 1 cause fog particles everywhere absorb more light.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogExtinctionScale Default 1 View Distance

Distance over which volumetric fog should be computed, after the start distance. Larger values extend the effect into the distance but expose under-sampling artifacts in details.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogDistance Default 6000 Start Distance

Distance from the camera that the volumetric fog will start, in world units.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogStartDistance Default 0 Near Fade In Distance

Distance over which volumetric fog will fade in from the start distance.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogNearFadeInDistance Default 0 Override Light Colors With Fog Inscattering Colors

Whether to use FogInscatteringColor for the Sky Light volumetric scattering color and DirectionalInscatteringColor for the Directional Light scattering color. Make sure your directional light has 'Atmosphere Sun Light' enabled! Enabling this allows Volumetric fog to better match Height fog in the distance, but produces non-physical volumetric lighting that may not match surface lighting.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:bOverrideLightColorsWithFogInscatteringColors Default Off

items.title: Fog Screen Space Scattering - EXPERIMENTAL
items.text:
Enable Fog Screen Space Scattering

Enable FSSS (Fog Screen Space Scattering) to approximate multiple scattering.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:bEnableFSSS Default Off Scene Color Scattering Amount Scale

The amount of scene color injected into the fog screen space scattering technique. When 0, only the fog luminance will be scattered. When 1, fog and scene luminance will be scattered. When above 1, more scene color can be injected to increase the brightness of the multiple scattering effect, even when the fog is not too intense. We cannot scatter more than the scene color however.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:FSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountScale Default 1 Scene Color Scattering Amount Power

Apply a power over the amount of scattered scene luminance after it is evaluated using Scene Color Scattering Amount Scale. A value smaller than 1 can show more scattering where the fog is less intense.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:FSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountPower Default 1 Spread Scale

The scale of the spread for the fog multiple scattering. This basically scales mip level sampled from the blurred screen space FSSS texture. Increasing will make scene and thicker fog look fuzzier. But too high values can cause artifacts such as halos around depth discontinuities.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:FSSSSpreadScale Default 0.1 Blur Control

When generating the the blurred screen space FSSS texture, this controls how much of the blurred lower mip levels is injected back into the sharper higher mip levels. A higher value will result in a blurrier result. But when = 1, multiple scattering will be a single average color of the FSSS texture.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:FSSSBlurControl Default 0.5

items.title: Rendering
items.text:
Holdout

If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:bHoldout Default Off Render In Main Pass

If true, this component will be rendered in the main pass (basepass, transparency)

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:bRenderInMainPass Default On Visible In Reflection Captures

If true, this component will be visible in reflection captures.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:bVisibleInReflectionCaptures Default On Visible In Real Time Sky Captures

If true, this component will be visible in real-time sky light reflection captures.

USD attribute unreal:heightFog:bVisibleInRealTimeSkyCaptures Default On

items.title: hdUE Local Fog Volume 1.0
items.text:
ContextLOP nodeTypehdue::hduelocalfogvolume::1.0

Creates a UE Local Fog Volume: a sphere of fog that fades out radially, rendered by hdUE.

Like Karma Fog Box for Karma, it creates a fog prim hdUE renders: an UnrealLocalFogVolume, UE's Local Fog Volume (realtime only; UE's Path Tracer does not render local fog volumes). It authors every property, at UE's defaults too. UE draws no local fog nearer than 10 m to the camera unless r.LocalFogVolume.GlobalStartDistance is lowered (Engine Quality console variables). Height Fog Density 0 hides the whole volume: UE multiplies its radial and height coverage.

items.title: Parameters
items.text:
Primitive Path

Path of the UnrealLocalFogVolume prim.

Parameter primpath Default /fog/localfogvolume

items.title: Transform
items.text:
Translate

Centre of the volume, in scene units.

Parameter t Default 0, 0, 0 Rotate

Rotation (XYZ, degrees); the height fog falls off along the rotated up axis.

Parameter r Default 0, 0, 0 Radius

Radius of the fog sphere in scene units (UE's Local Fog Volume is a sphere of radius 500 cm, scaled uniformly).

Parameter radius Default 5

items.title: Local Fog Volume
items.text:
Radial Fog Density

The density of the radial fog representing its extinction coefficient at the center of the sphere. The final look of the volume is determined by combining the "Coverage=1-Transmittance" of both radial and height fog in order to achieve both soft edges and height fog.

Parameter RadialFogExtinction Default 1 Height Fog Density

The density of the radial fog representing its extinction coefficient at height 0 in the unit sphere. The final look of the volume is determined by combining the "Coverage=1-Transmittance" of both radial and height fog in order to achieve both soft edges and height fog.

Parameter HeightFogExtinction Default 1 Height Fog Falloff

Controls how the density decreases as height increases. Smaller values make the visible transition larger. 1.0 is the lowest value before visual artifact are visible at the horizon.

Parameter HeightFogFalloff Default 1000 Height Fog Offset

Height offset, relative to the actor Z position.

Parameter HeightFogOffset Default 0 Scattering Distribution

Controls the phase G parameter, describing the directionality of the scattering within this fog volume.

Parameter FogPhaseG Default 0.2 Fog Albedo

Controls the albedo of this fog volume.

Parameter FogAlbedo Default 1, 1, 1 Fog Emissive

Controls the emissive color of this fog volume. (Unit = Luminance)

Parameter FogEmissive Default 0, 0, 0 Start Distance

Controls the distance after which this volume starts to appear. (Unit = Centimeter) This distance is clamped to be greater than r.LocalFogVolume.GlobalStartDistance.

Parameter FogStartDistance Default 0 Fog Sort Priority

The priority can be used as a way to override the sorting by distance. A lower value means the volume will be considered further away, i.e. it will draw behind the one with a higher priority value.

Parameter FogSortPriority Default 0

items.title: hdUE Local Fog Volume
items.text:
ContextLOP nodeTypehdue::hduelocalfogvolume::2.0

Creates or edits a UE Local Fog Volume: a sphere of fog that fades out radially, rendered by hdUE.

Like Karma Sky Atmosphere for Karma, it creates or edits a prim hdUE renders: an UnrealLocalFogVolume, UE's Local Fog Volume (realtime only; UE's Path Tracer does not render local fog volumes). Uniform Scale is the radius in scene units (UE's volume is a sphere of radius 500 cm). In Create mode it authors every property, at UE's defaults too, and a guide sphere. In Edit mode every control starts at Set or Create, as on Houdini's prim LOPs: Initialize Parameters sets them to Do Nothing and reads the prim's property values (not its transform). UE draws no local fog nearer than 10 m to the camera unless r.LocalFogVolume.GlobalStartDistance is lowered (Engine Quality console variables). Height Fog Density 0 hides the whole volume: UE multiplies its radial and height coverage.

items.title: Local Fog Volume
items.text:
Radial Fog Density

The density of the radial fog representing its extinction coefficient at the center of the sphere. The final look of the volume is determined by combining the "Coverage=1-Transmittance" of both radial and height fog in order to achieve both soft edges and height fog.

USD attribute unreal:localFogVolume:RadialFogExtinction Default 1 Height Fog Density

The density of the radial fog representing its extinction coefficient at height 0 in the unit sphere. The final look of the volume is determined by combining the "Coverage=1-Transmittance" of both radial and height fog in order to achieve both soft edges and height fog.

USD attribute unreal:localFogVolume:HeightFogExtinction Default 1 Height Fog Falloff

Controls how the density decreases as height increases. Smaller values make the visible transition larger. 1.0 is the lowest value before visual artifact are visible at the horizon.

USD attribute unreal:localFogVolume:HeightFogFalloff Default 1000 Height Fog Offset

Height offset, relative to the actor Z position.

USD attribute unreal:localFogVolume:HeightFogOffset Default 0 Scattering Distribution

Controls the phase G parameter, describing the directionality of the scattering within this fog volume.

USD attribute unreal:localFogVolume:FogPhaseG Default 0.2 Fog Albedo

Controls the albedo of this fog volume.

USD attribute unreal:localFogVolume:FogAlbedo Default 1, 1, 1 Fog Emissive

Controls the emissive color of this fog volume. (Unit = Luminance)

USD attribute unreal:localFogVolume:FogEmissive Default 0, 0, 0 Start Distance

Controls the distance after which this volume starts to appear. (Unit = Centimeter) This distance is clamped to be greater than r.LocalFogVolume.GlobalStartDistance.

USD attribute unreal:localFogVolume:FogStartDistance Default 0 Fog Sort Priority

The priority can be used as a way to override the sorting by distance. A lower value means the volume will be considered further away, i.e. it will draw behind the one with a higher priority value.

USD attribute unreal:localFogVolume:FogSortPriority Default 0

items.title: hdUE Post Process Volume
items.text:
ContextLOP nodeTypehdue::hduepostprocessvolume::1.0

Creates or edits a UE Post Process Volume: a box whose post-process settings blend in while the camera is inside or near it.

Like a Post Process Volume placed in a UE level, it creates or edits an UnrealPostProcessVolume prim: a box filling the cube from -1 to 1 of its local space (Uniform Scale 1 is a 2-unit box), with UE's Priority, Blend Radius (UE centimetres), Blend Weight, Enabled and Infinite Extent (Unbound). Its other tabs are the render settings' post-process settings: turn a setting's control to Set or Create to override it, as UE's override checkboxes. UE blends the volumes the camera is in or near, by priority, before the render settings' own post-process settings (which act as the camera's). Textures take cooked paths here, not image files.

items.title: Post Process Volume
items.text:
Priority

Priority of this volume. In the case of overlapping volumes the one with the highest priority overrides the lower priority ones. The order is undefined if two or more overlapping volumes have the same priority.

USD attribute unreal:postProcessVolume:Priority Default 0 Blend Radius

World space radius around the volume that is used for blending (only if not unbound).

USD attribute unreal:postProcessVolume:BlendRadius Default 100 Blend Weight

0:no effect, 1:full effect

USD attribute unreal:postProcessVolume:BlendWeight Default 1 Enabled

Whether this volume is enabled or not.

USD attribute unreal:postProcessVolume:bEnabled Default On Infinite Extent (Unbound)

Whether this volume covers the whole world, or just the area inside its bounds.

USD attribute unreal:postProcessVolume:bUnbound Default Off

items.title: Main
items.text:
Exposure Compensation

Logarithmic adjustment for the exposure. Only used if a tonemapper is specified. 0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ... hdUE adds the USD camera exposure to it.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AutoExposureBias Default 0

items.title: Path Tracing
items.text:
Max. Bounces

Sets the path tracing maximum bounces. Counts scattering events along a path: 0 shows only emission seen directly, 1 is direct light alone, N matches Karma's Diffuse Limit N - 1. One limit covers diffuse, specular, refraction and volume bounces.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:PathTracingMaxBounces Default 32 Max Path Intensity

Sets the maximum intensity of indirect samples to reduce fireflies. Lowering this value reduces noise at the expense of accuracy. Increasing it is more accurate but may lead to more noise.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:PathTracingMaxPathIntensity Default 24 Emissive Materials

Should emissive materials contribute to scene lighting?

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:PathTracingEnableEmissiveMaterials Default On Reference Depth Of Field

Enables a reference quality depth-of-field which replaces the post-process effect. hdUE turns it on when the USD camera has depth of field.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:PathTracingEnableReferenceDOF Default On Reference Atmosphere

Enables path tracing in the atmosphere instead of baking the sky atmosphere contribution into a skylight. Any skylight present in the scene will be automatically ignored when this is enabled.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:PathTracingEnableReferenceAtmosphere Default Off Denoiser

Run the currently loaded denoiser plugin on the last sample to remove noise from the output. Has no effect if a plug-in is not loaded.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:PathTracingEnableDenoiser Default On

items.title: Lighting Components
items.text:
Emissive

Should the render include directly visible emissive elements?

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:PathTracingIncludeEmissive Default On Diffuse

Should the render include diffuse lighting contributions?

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:PathTracingIncludeDiffuse Default On Indirect Diffuse

Should the render include indirect diffuse lighting contributions?

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:PathTracingIncludeIndirectDiffuse Default On Specular

Should the render include specular lighting contributions?

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:PathTracingIncludeSpecular Default On Indirect Specular

Should the render include indirect specular lighting contributions?

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:PathTracingIncludeIndirectSpecular Default On Volume

Should the render include volume lighting contributions?

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:PathTracingIncludeVolume Default On Indirect Volume

Should the render include volume lighting contributions?

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:PathTracingIncludeIndirectVolume Default On

items.title: Bloom
items.text:
Preferred Method

Preferred bloom algorithm. A different method may be used if the preferred method is not available on the target platform, e.g. due to performance limits.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomMethod Default BM_SOG Menu Standard, Convolution Intensity

Multiplier for all bloom contributions >=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomIntensity Default 0.675

items.title: Gaussian
items.text:
Intensity

Multiplier for Gaussian bloom contributions >=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomGaussianIntensity Default 1 Threshold

minimum brightness the bloom starts having effect -1:all pixels affect bloom equally (physically correct, faster as a threshold pass is omitted), 0:all pixels affect bloom brights more, 1(default), >1 brighter

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomThreshold Default -1 Size scale

Scale for all bloom sizes

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomSizeScale Default 4 #1 Size

Diameter size for the Bloom1 in percent of the screen width (is done in ½ resolution, larger values cost more performance, good for high frequency details) >=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:Bloom1Size Default 0.3 #2 Size

Diameter size for Bloom2 in percent of the screen width (is done in ¼ resolution, larger values cost more performance) >=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:Bloom2Size Default 1 #3 Size

Diameter size for Bloom3 in percent of the screen width (is done in ⅛ resolution, larger values cost more performance) >=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:Bloom3Size Default 2 #4 Size

Diameter size for Bloom4 in percent of the screen width (is done in 1/16 resolution, larger values cost more performance, best for wide contributions) >=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:Bloom4Size Default 10 #5 Size

Diameter size for Bloom5 in percent of the screen width (is done in 1/32 resolution, larger values cost more performance, best for wide contributions) >=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:Bloom5Size Default 30 #6 Size

Diameter size for Bloom6 in percent of the screen width (is done in 1/64 resolution, larger values cost more performance, best for wide contributions) >=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:Bloom6Size Default 64 #1 Tint

Bloom1 tint color

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:Bloom1Tint Default 0.3465, 0.3465, 0.3465 #2 Tint

Bloom2 tint color

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:Bloom2Tint Default 0.138, 0.138, 0.138 #3 Tint

Bloom3 tint color

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:Bloom3Tint Default 0.1176, 0.1176, 0.1176 #4 Tint

Bloom4 tint color

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:Bloom4Tint Default 0.066, 0.066, 0.066 #5 Tint

Bloom5 tint color

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:Bloom5Tint Default 0.066, 0.066, 0.066 #6 Tint

Bloom6 tint color

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:Bloom6Tint Default 0.061, 0.061, 0.061

items.title: Convolution
items.text:
Intensity

Multiplier for Convolution bloom contributions >=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomConvolutionIntensity Default 1 Scatter Dispersion

Intensity multiplier on the scatter dispersion energy of the kernel. 1.0 means exactly use the same energy as the kernel scatter dispersion.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomConvolutionScatterDispersion Default 1 Scale

Relative size of the convolution kernel image compared to the minor axis of the viewport

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomConvolutionSize Default 1 Center

The UV location of the center of the kernel. Should be very close to (.5,.5)

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomConvolutionCenterUV Default 0.5, 0.5 Boost Min

Boost intensity of select pixels prior to computing bloom convolution (Min, Max, Multiplier). Max < Min disables

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomConvolutionPreFilterMin Default 7 Boost Max

Boost intensity of select pixels prior to computing bloom convolution (Min, Max, Multiplier). Max < Min disables

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomConvolutionPreFilterMax Default 15000 Boost Mult

Boost intensity of select pixels prior to computing bloom convolution (Min, Max, Multiplier). Max < Min disables

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomConvolutionPreFilterMult Default 15 Buffer

Implicit buffer region as a fraction of the screen size to insure the bloom does not wrap across the screen. Larger sizes have perf impact.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomConvolutionBufferScale Default 0.133

items.title: Exposure
items.text:
Metering Mode

Luminance computation method. hdUE renders with manual exposure, so the tone curve keeps the linear image's middle grey; Histogram or Basic turn on UE's auto exposure.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AutoExposureMethod Default AEM_Manual Menu Auto Exposure Histogram, Auto Exposure Basic, Manual Apply Physical Camera Exposure

Enables physical camera exposure using ShutterSpeed/ISO/Aperture.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AutoExposureApplyPhysicalCameraExposure Default Off Exposure Compensation Curve

Exposure compensation based on the scene EV100. Used to calibrate the final exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance. 0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ... Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AutoExposureBiasCurve Min Brightness

Auto-Exposure minimum adaptation. Eye Adaptation is disabled if Min = Max. Auto-exposure is implemented by choosing an exposure value for which the average luminance generates a pixel brightness equal to the Constant Calibration value. The Min/Max are expressed in pixel luminance (cd/m2) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings).

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AutoExposureMinBrightness Default 0.03 Max Brightness

Auto-Exposure maximum adaptation. Eye Adaptation is disabled if Min = Max. Auto-exposure is implemented by choosing an exposure value for which the average luminance generates a pixel brightness equal to the Constant Calibration value. The Min/Max are expressed in pixel luminance (cd/m2) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings).

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AutoExposureMaxBrightness Default 8 Speed Up
  1. Unless a speed is set, auto exposure reaches its target in every frame; set, the realtime viewport adapts at this speed (husk and Path Tracer renders always use the target).
USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AutoExposureSpeedUp Default 3 Speed Down
  1. Unless a speed is set, auto exposure reaches its target in every frame; set, the realtime viewport adapts at this speed (husk and Path Tracer renders always use the target).
USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AutoExposureSpeedDown Default 1 Low Percent

The eye adaptation will adapt to a value extracted from the luminance histogram of the scene color. The value is defined as having x percent below this brightness. Higher values give bright spots on the screen more priority but can lead to less stable results. Lower values give the medium and darker values more priority but might cause burn out of bright spots. >0, <100, good values are in the range 70 .. 80

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AutoExposureLowPercent Default 10 High Percent

The eye adaptation will adapt to a value extracted from the luminance histogram of the scene color. The value is defined as having x percent below this brightness. Higher values give bright spots on the screen more priority but can lead to less stable results. Lower values give the medium and darker values more priority but might cause burn out of bright spots. >0, <100, good values are in the range 80 .. 95

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AutoExposureHighPercent Default 90 Histogram Log Min

Histogram Min value. Expressed in Log2(Luminance) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings)

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:HistogramLogMin Default -8 Histogram Log Max

Histogram Max value. Expressed in Log2(Luminance) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings)

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:HistogramLogMax Default 4

items.title: Chromatic Aberration
items.text:
Intensity

in percent, Scene chromatic aberration / color fringe (camera imperfection) to simulate an artifact that happens in real-world lens, mostly visible in the image corners.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:SceneFringeIntensity Default 0 Start Offset

A normalized distance to the center of the framebuffer where the effect takes place.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ChromaticAberrationStartOffset Default 0

items.title: Dirt Mask
items.text:
Dirt Mask Intensity

BloomDirtMask intensity

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomDirtMaskIntensity Default 0 Dirt Mask Tint

BloomDirtMask tint color

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BloomDirtMaskTint Default 0.5, 0.5, 0.5

items.title: Camera
items.text:
Shutter Speed (1/s)

The camera shutter in 1/seconds.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:CameraShutterSpeed Default 60 ISO

The camera sensor sensitivity in ISO.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:CameraISO Default 100 Aperture (F-stop)

Defines the opening of the camera lens, Aperture is 1/fstop, typical lens go down to f/1.2 (large opening), larger numbers reduce the DOF effect. Set from the USD camera (fStop, focusDistance, focalLength); this overrides it.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldFstop Default 4 Maximum Aperture (min F-stop)

Defines the maximum opening of the camera lens to control the curvature of blades of the diaphragm. Set it to 0 to get straight blades.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldMinFstop Default 1.2 Number of diaphragm blades

Defines the number of blades of the diaphragm within the lens (between 4 and 16).

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldBladeCount Default 5

items.title: Local Exposure
items.text:
Method

Local Exposure algorithm

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LocalExposureMethod Default ELocalExposureMethod::Bilateral Menu Bilateral, Fusion (Experimental) Highlight Contrast

Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer. Contrast of the base layer is reduced based on this value. Value less than 1 will enable local exposure. Good values are usually in the range 0.6 .. 1.0.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LocalExposureHighlightContrastScale Default 1 Shadow Contrast

Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer. Contrast of the base layer is reduced based on this value. Value less than 1 will enable local exposure. Good values are usually in the range 0.6 .. 1.0.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LocalExposureShadowContrastScale Default 1 Highlight Contrast Curve

Local Exposure Highlight Contrast based on the scene EV100. Used to calibrate Local Exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance. Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LocalExposureHighlightContrastCurve Shadow Contrast Curve

Local Exposure Shadow Contrast based on the scene EV100. Used to calibrate Local Exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance. Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LocalExposureShadowContrastCurve Highlight Threshold

Threshold used to determine which regions of the screen are considered highlights.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LocalExposureHighlightThreshold Default 0 Shadow Threshold

Threshold used to determine which regions of the screen are considered shadows.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LocalExposureShadowThreshold Default 0 Detail Strength

Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer. Value different than 1 will enable local exposure. This value should be set to 1 in most cases.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LocalExposureDetailStrength Default 1 Blurred Luminance Blend

Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer. Blend between bilateral filtered and blurred luminance as the base layer. Blurred luminance helps preserve image appearance and specular highlights, and reduce ringing. Good values are usually in the range 0.4 .. 0.6

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LocalExposureBlurredLuminanceBlend Default 0.6 Blurred Luminance Kernel Size Percent

Kernel size (percentage of screen) used to blur frame luminance.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LocalExposureBlurredLuminanceKernelSizePercent Default 50 Highlight Threshold Strength

Strength of the highlight threshold.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LocalExposureHighlightThresholdStrength Default 1 Shadow Threshold Strength

Strength of the shadow threshold.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LocalExposureShadowThresholdStrength Default 1 Middle Grey Bias

Logarithmic adjustment for the local exposure middle grey. 0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ...

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LocalExposureMiddleGreyBias Default 0

items.title: Lens Flares
items.text:
Intensity

Brightness scale of the image cased lens flares (linear)

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LensFlareIntensity Default 1 Tint

Tint color for the image based lens flares.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LensFlareTint Default 1, 1, 1 BokehSize

Size of the Lens Blur (in percent of the view width) that is done with the Bokeh texture (note: performance cost is radius*radius)

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LensFlareBokehSize Default 3 Threshold

Minimum brightness the lens flare starts having effect (this should be as high as possible to avoid the performance cost of blurring content that is too dark too see)

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LensFlareThreshold Default 8

items.title: Image Effects
items.text:
Vignette Intensity

0..1 0=off/no vignette .. 1=strong vignette

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:VignetteIntensity Default 0.4 Sharpen

Controls the strength of image sharpening applied during tonemapping.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:Sharpen Default 0 Vignette Type

The shape type of the vignette

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:VignetteType Default EVignetteType::CosineFourthLaw Menu Cosine Fourth Law (Default), Texture, Oval Vignette Center

Position of the vignette center in UV space.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:VignetteCenter Default 0.5, 0.5 Vignette Color

Color multiplied with areas that are masked by the vignette. Default is black.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:VignetteColor Default 0, 0, 0 Vignette Size

Scale of the vignette shape in screenspace. Can be used to scale vignette anamorphically. Default is 1.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:VignetteSize Default 1, 1 Vignette Softness

The softness of the transition from opaque to transparant on the edge of the vignette shape.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:VignetteSoftness Default 5

items.title: Depth of Field
items.text:
Enabled

When false, post-process depth of field will not be used. When true, DoF may be used depending on lens and scalability settings.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldEnabled Default On Sensor Width (mm)

Width of the camera sensor to assume, in mm. Set from the USD camera (fStop, focusDistance, focalLength); this overrides it.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldSensorWidth Default 24.576 Squeeze Factor

This is the squeeze factor for the DOF, which emulates the properties of anamorphic lenses. Set from the USD camera (fStop, focusDistance, focalLength); this overrides it.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldSqueezeFactor Default 1 Focal Distance

Distance in which the Depth of Field effect should be sharp, in unreal units (cm). Set from the USD camera (fStop, focusDistance, focalLength); this overrides it.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldFocalDistance Default 0 Depth Blur km for 50%

CircleDOF only: Depth blur km for 50%

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldDepthBlurAmount Default 1 Depth Blur Radius

CircleDOF only: Depth blur radius in pixels at 1920x

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldDepthBlurRadius Default 0 Petzval Bokeh

Simulate stretching in blur and bokeh. Positive values for sagittal (swirly bokeh), negative values for tangential.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldPetzvalBokeh Default 0 Petzval Bokeh Falloff

How quickly does the Petzval bokeh effect increase towards the edge of the image

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldPetzvalBokehFalloff Default 1 Petzval Bokeh Exclusion Box

Box, centered on screen, around which the Petzval effect is applied.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldPetzvalExclusionBoxExtents Default 0, 0 Petzval Bokeh Exclusion Box Radius

Corner radius

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldPetzvalExclusionBoxRadius Default 0 Aspect Ratio Scalar

Amount to scale the output viewport's aspect ratio by when computing depth of field properties.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldAspectRatioScalar Default 1 Barrel Radius

The lens barrel creates vignetting and occludes bokeh, i.e. cat's eye bokeh

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldBarrelRadius Default 5 Barrel Length

The lens barrel creates vignetting and occludes bokeh, i.e. cat's eye bokeh

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldBarrelLength Default 0 Use Hair Depth

For depth of field to use the hair depth for computing circle of confusion size. Otherwise use an interpolated distance between the hair depth and the scene depth based on the hair coverage (default).

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DepthOfFieldUseHairDepth Default Off

items.title: Temperature
items.text:
Temperature Type

Selects the type of temperature calculation. White Balance uses the Temperature value to control the virtual camera's White Balance. This is the default selection. Color Temperature uses the Temperature value to adjust the color temperature of the scene, which is the inverse of the White Balance operation.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:TemperatureType Default TEMP_WhiteBalance Menu White Balance, Color Temperature Temp

Controls the color temperature or white balance in degrees Kelvin which the scene considers as white light.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:WhiteTemp Default 6500 Tint

Controls the color of the scene along the magenta - green axis (orthogonal to the color temperature). This feature is equivalent to color tint in digital cameras.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:WhiteTint Default 0

items.title: Global
items.text:
Saturation

Control the intensity of the color(hue) for the entire image.Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorSaturation Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Contrast

Control the range of light and dark values in your scene. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorContrast Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Gamma

Control the luminance curve of the scene. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the entire image.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorGamma Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Gain

This value multiplies the colors of the image. Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the entire scene.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorGain Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Offset

This value is added to the colors of the scene. Raising or lowering this value will result in the image being more or less washed-out.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorOffset Default 0, 0, 0, 0

items.title: Shadows
items.text:
Saturation

Control the intensity of the colors (hue) in the shadow region of the image. Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorSaturationShadows Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Contrast

Control the range of light and dark values in your scene. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorContrastShadows Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Gamma

Control the luminance curve of the shadow region. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the shadow region.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorGammaShadows Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Gain

This value multiplies the colors in the shadow region. Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the affected region.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorGainShadows Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Offset

This value is added to the colors in the shadow region. Raising or lowering this value will result in the shadows being more or less washed-out.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorOffsetShadows Default 0, 0, 0, 0 ShadowsMax

This value sets the threshold for what is considered to be the shadow region of the image.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorCorrectionShadowsMax Default 0.09

items.title: Midtones
items.text:
Saturation

Control the intensity of the colors (hue) in the mid-tone region of the image. Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorSaturationMidtones Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Contrast

Control the range of light and dark values in the mid-tone region. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorContrastMidtones Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Gamma

Control the luminance curve of the mid-tone region of the image. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the image.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorGammaMidtones Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Gain

This value multiplies the colors in the mid-tone region of the image. Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the affected region.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorGainMidtones Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Offset

This value is added to the colors in the mid-tone region of the image. Raising or lowering this value will result in the mid-tones being more or less washed-out.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorOffsetMidtones Default 0, 0, 0, 0

items.title: Highlights
items.text:
Saturation

Control the intensity of the color (hue) for the highlights region of the image. Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorSaturationHighlights Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Contrast

Control the range of light and dark values in the highlights region. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorContrastHighlights Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Gamma

Control the luminance curve of the highlight region. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the highlight region.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorGammaHighlights Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Gain

This value multiplies the colors in the highlight region. Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the affected region.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorGainHighlights Default 1, 1, 1, 1 Offset

This value is added to the colors in the highlight region. Raising or lowering this value will result in the highlights being more or less washed-out.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorOffsetHighlights Default 0, 0, 0, 0 HighlightsMin

This value sets the lower threshold for what is considered to be the highlight region of the image.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorCorrectionHighlightsMin Default 0.5 HighlightsMax

This value sets the upper threshold for what is considered to be the highlight region of the image. This value should be larger than HighlightsMin. Default is 1.0, for backwards compatibility

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorCorrectionHighlightsMax Default 1

items.title: Misc
items.text:
Blue Correction

Correct for artifacts with "electric" blues due to the ACEScg color space. Bright blue desaturates instead of going to violet.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:BlueCorrection Default 0.6 Expand Gamut

Expand bright saturated colors outside the sRGB gamut to fake wide gamut rendering.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ExpandGamut Default 1 Tone Curve Amount

Allow effect of Tone Curve to be reduced (Set ToneCurveAmount and ExpandGamut to 0.0 to fully disable tone curve)

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ToneCurveAmount Default 1 Scene Color Tint

Scene tint color

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:SceneColorTint Default 1, 1, 1 Color Grading LUT Intensity

Color grading lookup table intensity. 0 = no intensity, 1=full intensity

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ColorGradingIntensity Default 1

items.title: Film
items.text:
Method

Controls the method of tonemapping.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:TonemappingMethod Default ETonemappingMethod::Filmic Menu Filmic, Standard ACES Slope

Controls the overall steepness of the tonemapper curve. Larger values increase scene contrast and smaller values reduce contrast.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:FilmSlope Default 0.88 Toe

Controls the contrast of the dark end of the tonemapper curve. Larger values increase contrast and smaller values decrease contrast.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:FilmToe Default 0.55 Shoulder

Sometimes referred to as highlight rolloff. Controls the contrast of the bright end of the tonemapper curve. Larger values increase contrast and smaller values decrease contrast.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:FilmShoulder Default 0.26 Black clip

Lowers the toe of the tonemapper curve by this amount. Increasing this value causes more of the scene to clip to black. For most purposes, this property should remain 0

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:FilmBlackClip Default 0 White clip

Controls the height of the tonemapper curve. Raising this value can cause bright values to more quickly approach fully-saturated white.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:FilmWhiteClip Default 0.04

items.title: Film Grain
items.text:
Film Grain Intensity

0..1 Film grain intensity to apply. LinearSceneColor *= lerp(1.0, DecodedFilmGrainTexture, FilmGrainIntensity)

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:FilmGrainIntensity Default 0 Film Grain Intensity Shadows

Control over the grain intensity in the regions of the image considered shadow areas.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:FilmGrainIntensityShadows Default 1 Film Grain Intensity Midtones

Control over the grain intensity in the mid-tone region of the image.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:FilmGrainIntensityMidtones Default 1 Film Grain Intensity Highlights

Control over the grain intensity in the regions of the image considered highlight areas.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:FilmGrainIntensityHighlights Default 1 Film Grain Shadows Max

Sets the upper bound used for Film Grain Shadow Intensity.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:FilmGrainShadowsMax Default 0.09 Film Grain Highlights Min

Sets the lower bound used for Film Grain Highlight Intensity.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:FilmGrainHighlightsMin Default 0.5 Film Grain Highlights Max

Sets the upper bound used for Film Grain Highlight Intensity. This value should be larger than HighlightsMin.. Default is 1.0, for backwards compatibility

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:FilmGrainHighlightsMax Default 1 Film Grain Scale

Controls the size of the film grain. Size of texel of FilmGrainTexture on screen.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:FilmGrainScale Default 1, 1

items.title: Global Illumination
items.text:
Method

Chooses the Dynamic Global Illumination method. Not compatible with Forward Shading. Overrides unreal:lumenEnabled.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:DynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod Default EDynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod::Lumen Menu None, Lumen, Screen Space (Deprecated), Plugin Indirect Lighting Color

Adjusts indirect lighting color. (1,1,1) is default. (0,0,0) to disable GI. The show flag 'Global Illumination' must be enabled to use this property.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:IndirectLightingColor Default 1, 1, 1 Indirect Lighting Intensity

Scales the indirect lighting contribution. A value of 0 disables GI. Default is 1. The show flag 'Global Illumination' must be enabled to use this property.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:IndirectLightingIntensity Default 1

items.title: Lumen Global Illumination
items.text:
Ray Lighting Mode

Controls how Lumen rays are lit when Lumen is using Hardware Ray Tracing. By default, Lumen uses the Surface Cache for best performance, but can be set to 'Hit Lighting' for higher quality.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenRayLightingMode Default ELumenRayLightingModeOverride::Default Menu Project Default, Surface Cache, Hit Lighting for Reflections, Hit Lighting Lumen Scene Lighting Quality

Scales Lumen Scene's quality. Larger scales cause Lumen Scene to be calculated with a higher fidelity, which can be visible in reflections, but increase GPU cost.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenSceneLightingQuality Default 1 Lumen Scene Detail

Controls the size of instances that can be represented in Lumen Scene. Larger values will ensure small objects are represented, but increase GPU cost.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenSceneDetail Default 1 Lumen Scene View Distance

Sets the maximum view distance of the scene that Lumen maintains for ray tracing against. Larger values will increase the effective range of sky shadowing and Global Illumination, but increase GPU cost.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenSceneViewDistance Default 20000 Final Gather Quality

Scales Lumen's Final Gather quality. Larger scales reduce noise, but greatly increase GPU cost.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenFinalGatherQuality Default 1 Screen Traces

Whether to use screen space traces for Lumen Global Illumination. Screen space traces bypass Lumen Scene and instead sample Scene Depth and Scene Color. This improves quality, as it bypasses Lumen Scene, but causes view dependent lighting.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenFinalGatherScreenTraces Default On Max Trace Distance

Controls the maximum distance that Lumen should trace while solving lighting. Values that are too small will cause lighting to leak into large caves, while values that are large will increase GPU cost.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenMaxTraceDistance Default 20000 Lumen Surface Cache Resolution

Scale factor for Lumen Surface Cache resolution. Smaller values save GPU memory, at a cost in quality. Defaults to 0.5 for Scene Captures if not overridden.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenSurfaceCacheResolution Default 1 Lumen Scene Lighting Update Speed

Controls how much Lumen Scene is allowed to cache lighting results to improve performance. Larger scales cause lighting changes to propagate faster, but increase GPU cost.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenSceneLightingUpdateSpeed Default 1 Final Gather Lighting Update Speed

Controls how much Lumen Final Gather is allowed to cache lighting results to improve performance. Larger scales cause lighting changes to propagate faster, but increase GPU cost and noise.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenFinalGatherLightingUpdateSpeed Default 1 Diffuse Color Boost

Allows brightening indirect lighting by calculating material diffuse color for indirect lighting. Values above 1 (original diffuse color) aren't physically correct, but they can be useful as an art direction knob to increase the amount of bounced light in the scene. Best to keep below 2 as it also causes reflections to be brighter than the scene.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenDiffuseColorBoost Default 1 Ambient Occlusion Intensity

Allows control over the strength of Lumen's Short Range Ambient Occlusion.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenAmbientOcclusionIntensity Default 1 Skylight Leaking

Controls what fraction of the skylight intensity should be allowed to leak. This can be useful as an art direction knob (non-physically based) to keep indoor areas from going fully black.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenSkylightLeaking Default 0 Skylight Leaking Tint

Color tint for Lumen Skylight Leaking.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenSkylightLeakingTint Default 1, 1, 1 Full Skylight Leaking Distance

Controls the distance from a receiving surface where skylight leaking reaches its full intensity. Smaller values make the skylight leaking flatter, while larger values create an Ambient Occlusion effect.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenFullSkylightLeakingDistance Default 1000

items.title: Reflections
items.text:
Method

Chooses the Reflection method. Not compatible with Forward Shading. Overrides unreal:lumenEnabled.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ReflectionMethod Default EReflectionMethod::Lumen Menu None, Lumen, Screen Space

items.title: Lumen Reflections
items.text:
Quality

Scales the Reflection quality. Larger scales reduce noise in reflections, but increase GPU cost.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenReflectionQuality Default 1 Screen Traces

Whether to use screen space traces for Lumen Reflections. Screen space traces bypass Lumen Scene and instead sample Scene Depth and Scene Color. This improves quality, as it bypasses Lumen Scene, but causes view dependent lighting.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenReflectionsScreenTraces Default On High Quality Translucency Reflections

Whether to use high quality mirror reflections on the front layer of translucent surfaces. Other layers will use the lower quality Radiance Cache method that can only produce glossy reflections. Increases GPU cost when enabled.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenFrontLayerTranslucencyReflections Default Off Max Roughness To Trace

Sets the maximum roughness value for which Lumen still traces dedicated reflection rays. Higher values improve reflection quality, but greatly increase GPU cost.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenMaxRoughnessToTraceReflections Default 0.4 Max Reflection Bounces

Sets the maximum number of recursive reflection bounces. 1 means a single reflection ray (no secondary reflections in mirrors). Currently only supported by Hardware Ray Tracing with Hit Lighting.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenMaxReflectionBounces Default 1 Max Refraction Bounces

The maximum count of refraction event to trace. When hit lighting is used, Translucent meshes will be traced when LumenMaxRefractionBounces > 0, making the reflection tracing more expenssive.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:LumenMaxRefractionBounces Default 0

items.title: Screen Space Reflections
items.text:
Intensity

Enable/Fade/disable the Screen Space Reflection feature, in percent, avoid numbers between 0 and 1 fo consistency

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ScreenSpaceReflectionIntensity Default 100 Quality

0=lowest quality..100=maximum quality, only a few quality levels are implemented, no soft transition, 50 is the default for better performance.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ScreenSpaceReflectionQuality Default 50 Max Roughness

Until what roughness we fade the screen space reflections, 0.8 works well, smaller can run faster

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:ScreenSpaceReflectionMaxRoughness Default 0.6

items.title: Rendering Features
items.text:
User Flags

Per-view user flags accessible in materials via TestPostVolumeUserFlag node, allowing per-view overrides of material behavior.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:UserFlags Default 0 Post-Process Materials

Cooked post-process material paths, separated by spaces, added as blendables to the beauty. Before Tonemapping materials work with the Unreal tonemapper off.

USD attribute unreal:postProcessMaterials

items.title: Motion Blur
items.text:
Amount

Strength of motion blur, 0:off

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:MotionBlurAmount Default 0.5 Max

max distortion caused by motion blur, in percent of the screen width, 0:off

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:MotionBlurMax Default 5 Target FPS

Defines the target FPS for motion blur. Makes motion blur independent of actual frame rate and relative to the specified target FPS instead. Higher target FPS results in shorter frames, which means shorter shutter times and less motion blur. Lower FPS means more motion blur. A value of zero makes the motion blur dependent on the actual frame rate.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:MotionBlurTargetFPS Default 30 Per Object Size

The minimum projected screen radius for a primitive to be drawn in the velocity pass, percentage of screen width. smaller numbers cause more draw calls, default: 4%

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:MotionBlurPerObjectSize Default 0

items.title: MegaLights
items.text:
MegaLights

Allows forcing MegaLights on or off for this volume, regardless of the project setting for MegaLights. MegaLights will stochastically sample lights, which allows many shadow casting lights to be rendered efficiently, with a consistent and low GPU cost. When MegaLights is enabled, other direct lighting algorithms like Deferred Shading will no longer be used, and other shadowing methods like Ray Traced Shadows, Distance Field Shadows and Shadow Maps will no longer be used. MegaLights requires Hardware Ray Tracing and Shader Model 6.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:bMegaLights Default On MegaLights - High Quality Translucency

Whether to use high quality direct lighting on the front layer of translucent surfaces. Other layers will use the lower quality Translucency Lighting Volume. Increases GPU cost when enabled.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:MegaLightsFrontLayerTranslucency Default Off

items.title: Ambient Cubemap
items.text:
Tint

AmbientCubemap tint color

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientCubemapTint Default 1, 1, 1 Intensity

To scale the Ambient cubemap brightness >=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientCubemapIntensity Default 1

items.title: Ambient Occlusion
items.text:
Intensity

0..1 0=off/no ambient occlusion .. 1=strong ambient occlusion, defines how much it affects the non direct lighting after base pass

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionIntensity Default 0.5 Radius

0, in unreal units, bigger values means even distant surfaces affect the ambient occlusion

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionRadius Default 200 Static Fraction

0..1 0=no effect on static lighting .. 1=AO affects the stat lighting, 0 is free meaning no extra rendering pass

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionStaticFraction Default 1 Radius in WorldSpace

true: AO radius is in world space units, false: AO radius is locked the view space in 400 units

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionRadiusInWS Default Off Fade Out Distance

0, in unreal units, at what distance the AO effect disppears in the distance (avoding artifacts and AO effects on huge object)

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionFadeDistance Default 8000 Fade Out Radius

0, in unreal units, how many units before AmbientOcclusionFadeOutDistance it starts fading out

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionFadeRadius Default 5000 Power

0, in unreal units, bigger values means even distant surfaces affect the ambient occlusion

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionPower Default 2 Bias

0, in unreal units, default (3.0) works well for flat surfaces but can reduce details

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionBias Default 3 Quality

0=lowest quality..100=maximum quality, only a few quality levels are implemented, no soft transition

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionQuality Default 50 Mip Blend

Affects the blend over the multiple mips (lower resolution versions) , 0:fully use full resolution, 1::fully use low resolution, around 0.6 seems to be a good value

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionMipBlend Default 0.6 Mip Scale

Affects the radius AO radius scale over the multiple mips (lower resolution versions)

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionMipScale Default 1.7 Mip Threshold

to tweak the bilateral upsampling when using multiple mips (lower resolution versions)

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionMipThreshold Default 0.01 Temporal Blend Weight

How much to blend the current frame with previous frames when using GTAO with temporal accumulation

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionTemporalBlendWeight Default 0.1

items.title: Ray Tracing Ambient Occlusion
items.text:
Enabled

Enables ray tracing ambient occlusion.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingAO Default Off Samples Per Pixel

Sets the samples per pixel for ray tracing ambient occlusion.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingAOSamplesPerPixel Default 1 Intensity

Scalar factor on the ray-tracing ambient occlusion score.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingAOIntensity Default 1 Radius

Defines the world-space search radius for occlusion rays.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingAORadius Default 200

items.title: Translucency
items.text:
Translucency Method

Sets the translucency type

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:TranslucencyType Default ETranslucencyType::Raster Menu Raster, Ray Traced Max Roughness
