USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveRayleighScatteringFadeDistance Default 0 Aerial Pespective Mie Scattering Start Distance

Specify the aerial perspective start distance on cloud for Mie scattering only. (kilometers)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveMieScatteringStartDistance Default 0 Aerial Pespective Mie Scattering Fade Distance

Specify the distance over which the Rayleigh scattering will linearly ramp up to full effect. (kilometers)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveMieScatteringFadeDistance Default 0

items.title: Rendering
items.text:
Holdout

If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:bHoldout Default Off Render In Main Pass

If true, this component will be rendered in the main pass (basepass, transparency)

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:bRenderInMainPass Default On Holdout

If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:bHoldout Default Off Render In Main Pass

If true, this component will be rendered in the main pass (basepass, transparency)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:bRenderInMainPass Default On Visible In Real Time Sky Captures

If true, this component will be visible in real-time sky light reflection captures.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:bVisibleInRealTimeSkyCaptures Default On

items.title: Layer
items.text:
Layer Bottom Altitude

The altitude at which the cloud layer starts. (kilometers above the ground)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:LayerBottomAltitude Default 5 Layer Height

The height of the the cloud layer. (kilometers above the layer bottom altitude)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:LayerHeight Default 10 Tracing Start Max Distance

The maximum distance of the volumetric surface, i.e. cloud layer upper and lower bound, before which we will accept to start tracing. (kilometers)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:TracingStartMaxDistance Default 350 Tracing Start Distance From Camera

The distance from which the tracing will start. This is useful when the camera for instance is inside the layer of cloud. (kilometers)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:TracingStartDistanceFromCamera Default 0 Tracing Max Distance

The maximum distance that will be traced inside the cloud layer. (kilometers)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:TracingMaxDistance Default 50

items.title: Cloud Material
items.text:
Material

The material describing the cloud volume. It must be a Volume domain material. Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:Material

items.title: Cloud Tracing
items.text:
Use Per Sample Atmospheric Light Transmittance

Whether to apply atmosphere transmittance per sample, instead of using the light global transmittance.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:bUsePerSampleAtmosphericLightTransmittance Default Off Sky Light Cloud Bottom Occlusion

Occlude the sky light contribution at the bottom of the cloud layer. This is a fast approximation to sky lighting being occluded by cloud without having to trace rays or sample AO texture. Ignored if the cloud material explicitely sets the ambient occlusion value.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:SkyLightCloudBottomOcclusion Default 0.5 View Sample Count Scale

Scale the tracing sample count in primary views. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.ViewRaySampleCountMax'.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:ViewSampleCountScale Default 1 Reflection View Sample Count Scale Value

Scale the tracing sample count in reflection views. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.ReflectionRaySampleMaxCount'.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:ReflectionViewSampleCountScaleValue Default 1 Shadow View Sample Count Scale

Scale the shadow tracing sample count in primary views, only used with Advanced Output ray marched shadows. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.Shadow.ViewRaySampleMaxCount'.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:ShadowViewSampleCountScale Default 1 Shadow Reflection View Sample Count Scale Value

Scale the shadow tracing sample count in reflection views, only used with Advanced Output ray marched shadows. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.Shadow.ReflectionRaySampleMaxCount'.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:ShadowReflectionViewSampleCountScaleValue Default 1 Shadow Tracing Distance

The shadow tracing distance in kilometers, only used with Advanced Output ray marched shadows.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:ShadowTracingDistance Default 15 Stop Tracing Transmittance Threshold

When the mean transmittance is below this threshold, we stop tracing. This is a good way to reduce the ray marched sample count, and thus to increase performance.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:StopTracingTransmittanceThreshold Default 0.005

items.title: Rendering Features
items.text:
User Flags

Per-view user flags accessible in materials via TestPostVolumeUserFlag node, allowing per-view overrides of material behavior.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:UserFlags Default 0 Post-Process Materials

Cooked post-process material paths, separated by spaces, added as blendables to the beauty. Before Tonemapping materials work with the Unreal tonemapper off.

USD attribute unreal:postProcessMaterials

items.title: Motion Blur
items.text:
Motion Blur

Average sub-frames over the camera shutter (shutter:open/close) when something moves. Depth of field comes from the camera's fStop and focusDistance.

USD attribute unreal:motionBlur Default On Motion Samples

Sub-frames per frame. Path Tracer samples and realtime warmup frames are divided between them; too few show discrete copies of fast objects.

USD attribute unreal:motionSamples Default 16 Amount

Strength of motion blur, 0:off

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:MotionBlurAmount Default 0.5 Max

max distortion caused by motion blur, in percent of the screen width, 0:off

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:MotionBlurMax Default 5 Target FPS

Defines the target FPS for motion blur. Makes motion blur independent of actual frame rate and relative to the specified target FPS instead. Higher target FPS results in shorter frames, which means shorter shutter times and less motion blur. Lower FPS means more motion blur. A value of zero makes the motion blur dependent on the actual frame rate.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:MotionBlurTargetFPS Default 30 Per Object Size

The minimum projected screen radius for a primitive to be drawn in the velocity pass, percentage of screen width. smaller numbers cause more draw calls, default: 4%

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:MotionBlurPerObjectSize Default 0

items.title: MegaLights
items.text:
MegaLights

Allows forcing MegaLights on or off for this volume, regardless of the project setting for MegaLights. MegaLights will stochastically sample lights, which allows many shadow casting lights to be rendered efficiently, with a consistent and low GPU cost. When MegaLights is enabled, other direct lighting algorithms like Deferred Shading will no longer be used, and other shadowing methods like Ray Traced Shadows, Distance Field Shadows and Shadow Maps will no longer be used. MegaLights requires Hardware Ray Tracing and Shader Model 6.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:bMegaLights Default On MegaLights - High Quality Translucency

Whether to use high quality direct lighting on the front layer of translucent surfaces. Other layers will use the lower quality Translucency Lighting Volume. Increases GPU cost when enabled.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:MegaLightsFrontLayerTranslucency Default Off Samples per Pixel

Number of samples per downsampled pixel for the opaque lighting pass. Final number of samples depends also on the downsampling mode. Supported values: 1, 2 and 4. Console variable r.MegaLights.NumSamplesPerPixel (process-wide).

USD attribute unreal:cvar:r:MegaLights:NumSamplesPerPixel Default 4 Default Shadow Method

The default shadowing method for MegaLights, unless over-ridden on the light component. 0 - Ray Tracing. Preferred method, which guarantees fixed MegaLights cost and correct area shadows, but is dependent on the BVH representation quality. 1 - Virtual Shadow Maps. Has a significant per light cost, but can cast shadows directly from the Nanite geometry using rasterization. Console variable r.MegaLights.DefaultShadowMethod (process-wide).

USD attribute unreal:cvar:r:MegaLights:DefaultShadowMethod Default 0

items.title: Ambient Cubemap
items.text:
Tint

AmbientCubemap tint color

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientCubemapTint Default 1, 1, 1 Intensity

To scale the Ambient cubemap brightness >=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientCubemapIntensity Default 1 Cubemap Texture

The Ambient cubemap (Affects diffuse and specular shading), blends additively which if different from all other settings here. An image file, imported at render time (a lat-long panorama, made a cubemap as UE imports one), or the path of a cooked texture in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientCubemap

items.title: Ambient Occlusion
items.text:
Intensity

0..1 0=off/no ambient occlusion .. 1=strong ambient occlusion, defines how much it affects the non direct lighting after base pass

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionIntensity Default 0.5 Radius

0, in unreal units, bigger values means even distant surfaces affect the ambient occlusion

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionRadius Default 200 Static Fraction

0..1 0=no effect on static lighting .. 1=AO affects the stat lighting, 0 is free meaning no extra rendering pass

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionStaticFraction Default 1 Radius in WorldSpace

true: AO radius is in world space units, false: AO radius is locked the view space in 400 units

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionRadiusInWS Default Off Fade Out Distance

0, in unreal units, at what distance the AO effect disppears in the distance (avoding artifacts and AO effects on huge object)

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionFadeDistance Default 8000 Fade Out Radius

0, in unreal units, how many units before AmbientOcclusionFadeOutDistance it starts fading out

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionFadeRadius Default 5000 Power

0, in unreal units, bigger values means even distant surfaces affect the ambient occlusion

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionPower Default 2 Bias

0, in unreal units, default (3.0) works well for flat surfaces but can reduce details

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionBias Default 3 Quality

0=lowest quality..100=maximum quality, only a few quality levels are implemented, no soft transition

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionQuality Default 50 Mip Blend

Affects the blend over the multiple mips (lower resolution versions) , 0:fully use full resolution, 1::fully use low resolution, around 0.6 seems to be a good value

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionMipBlend Default 0.6 Mip Scale

Affects the radius AO radius scale over the multiple mips (lower resolution versions)

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionMipScale Default 1.7 Mip Threshold

to tweak the bilateral upsampling when using multiple mips (lower resolution versions)

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionMipThreshold Default 0.01 Temporal Blend Weight

How much to blend the current frame with previous frames when using GTAO with temporal accumulation

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:AmbientOcclusionTemporalBlendWeight Default 0.1

items.title: Ray Tracing Ambient Occlusion
items.text:
Enabled

Enables ray tracing ambient occlusion.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingAO Default Off Samples Per Pixel

Sets the samples per pixel for ray tracing ambient occlusion.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingAOSamplesPerPixel Default 1 Intensity

Scalar factor on the ray-tracing ambient occlusion score.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingAOIntensity Default 1 Radius

Defines the world-space search radius for occlusion rays.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingAORadius Default 200

items.title: Translucency
items.text:
Translucency Method

Sets the translucency type

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:TranslucencyType Default ETranslucencyType::Raster Menu Raster, Ray Traced Max Roughness

Sets the maximum roughness until which ray tracing translucency will be visible (lower value is faster). Translucency contribution is smoothly faded when close to roughness threshold. This parameter behaves similarly to ScreenSpaceReflectionMaxRoughness.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingTranslucencyMaxRoughness Default 0.6 Max. Refraction Rays

Sets the maximum number of ray tracing refraction rays.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingTranslucencyRefractionRays Default 3 Samples Per Pixel

Sets the samples per pixel for ray traced translucency.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingTranslucencySamplesPerPixel Default 1 Max. Primary Hit Events

Maximum number of hit events allowed on primary ray paths

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingTranslucencyMaxPrimaryHitEvents Default 4 Max. Secondary Hit Events

Maximum number of hit events allowed on secondary ray paths

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingTranslucencyMaxSecondaryHitEvents Default 2 Shadows

Sets the translucency shadows type.

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingTranslucencyShadows Default EReflectedAndRefractedRayTracedShadows::Hard_shadows Menu Disabled, Hard Shadows, Area Shadows Refraction

Sets whether refraction should be enabled or not (if not rays will not scatter and only travel in the same direction as before the intersection event).

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingTranslucencyRefraction Default On Use Ray Traced Refraction

Whether to use ray traced refraction which currently doesn't work well with rough refraction or simulate it using a screen space effect

USD attribute unreal:postProcess:RayTracingTranslucencyUseRayTracedRefraction Default Off

items.title: Image Output
items.text:
Render Products

Which render products the render settings render: this node's own product (Output Picture above, AOVs below), the render products authored upstream (hdUE Render Products, Render Product LOPs), or both.

Parameter outputproducts Default builtin Menu Built-in Product, Upstream Products, Built-in and Upstream Products Upstream Products

items.title: hdUE Sky Atmosphere
items.text:
ContextLOP nodeTypehdue::hdueskyatmosphere::1.0

Creates or edits a UE Sky Atmosphere: UE's physical sky, lit by the distant lights.

Like a Sky Atmosphere placed in a UE level, it creates or edits an UnrealSkyAtmosphere prim with UE's properties (kilometres, as in UE). Distant lights light it as atmosphere suns. A prim takes the place of hdUE Render Settings' Sky Atmosphere; UE draws one, the first prim by path. Its position counts only when Transform Mode places the planet at the component.

items.title: Planet
items.text:
Transform Mode

The ground albedo that will tint the atmosphere when the sun light will bounce on it. Only taken into account when MultiScattering>0.0.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:TransformMode Default ESkyAtmosphereTransformMode::PlanetTopAtAbsoluteWorldOrigin Menu PlanetTopAtAbsoluteWorldOrigin, PlanetTopAtComponentTransform, PlanetCenterAtComponentTransform Ground Radius

The radius in kilometers from the center of the planet to the ground level.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:BottomRadius Default 6360 Ground Albedo

The ground albedo that will tint the atmosphere when the sun light will bounce on it. Only taken into account when MultiScattering>0.0.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:GroundAlbedo Default 0.401978, 0.401978, 0.401978

items.title: Atmosphere
items.text:
Atmosphere Height

The height of the atmosphere layer above the ground in kilometers.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:AtmosphereHeight Default 60 MultiScattering

Factor applied to multiple scattering only (after the sun light has bounced around in the atmosphere at least once). Multiple scattering is evaluated using a dual scattering approach. A value of 2 is recommended to better represent default atmosphere when r.SkyAtmosphere.MultiScatteringLUT.HighQuality=0.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:MultiScatteringFactor Default 1 Trace Sample Count Scale

Scale the atmosphere tracing sample count. Quality level scalability The sample count is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.SkyAtmosphere.SampleCountMax' when 'r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT' is 0. The sample count is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT.SampleCountMax' when 'r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT' is 1. The sample count is still clamped for aerial perspective according to 'r.SkyAtmosphere.AerialPerspectiveLUT.SampleCountMaxPerSlice'.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:TraceSampleCountScale Default 1

items.title: Atmosphere - Rayleigh
items.text:
Rayleigh Scattering Scale

Rayleigh scattering coefficient scale.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:RayleighScatteringScale Default 0.0331 Rayleigh Scattering

The Rayleigh scattering coefficients resulting from molecules in the air at an altitude of 0 kilometer.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:RayleighScattering Default 0.175287, 0.409607, 1 Rayleigh Exponential Distribution

The altitude in kilometer at which Rayleigh scattering effect is reduced to 40%.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:RayleighExponentialDistribution Default 8

items.title: Atmosphere - Mie
items.text:
Mie Scattering Scale

Mie scattering coefficient scale.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:MieScatteringScale Default 0.003996 Mie Scattering

The Mie scattering coefficients resulting from particles in the air at an altitude of 0 kilometer. As it becomes higher, light will be scattered more.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:MieScattering Default 1, 1, 1 Mie Absorption Scale

Mie absorption coefficient scale.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:MieAbsorptionScale Default 0.000444 Mie Absorption

The Mie absorption coefficients resulting from particles in the air at an altitude of 0 kilometer. As it becomes higher, light will be absorbed more.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:MieAbsorption Default 1, 1, 1 Mie Anisotropy

A value of 0 mean light is uniformly scattered. A value closer to 1 means lights will scatter more forward, resulting in halos around light sources.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:MieAnisotropy Default 0.8 Mie Exponential Distribution

The altitude in kilometer at which Mie effects are reduced to 40%.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:MieExponentialDistribution Default 1.2

items.title: Atmosphere - Absorption
items.text:
Absorption Scale

Absorption coefficients for another atmosphere layer. Density increase from 0 to 1 between 10 to 25km and decreases from 1 to 0 between 25 to 40km. This approximates ozone molecules distribution in the Earth atmosphere.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:OtherAbsorptionScale Default 0.001881 Absorption

Absorption coefficients for another atmosphere layer. Density increase from 0 to 1 between 10 to 25km and decreases from 1 to 0 between 25 to 40km. The default values represents ozone molecules absorption in the Earth atmosphere.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:OtherAbsorption Default 0.345561, 1, 0.0451887

items.title: Art Direction
items.text:
Sky Luminance Factor

Scales the luminance of pixels representing the sky. This will impact the captured sky light.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:SkyLuminanceFactor Default 1, 1, 1 Sky And Aerial Perspective Luminance Factor

Scales the luminance of pixels representing the sky and the aerial perspective. This will impact the captured sky light.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:SkyAndAerialPerspectiveLuminanceFactor Default 1, 1, 1 Aerial Perspective View Distance Scale

Makes the aerial perspective look thicker by scaling distances from view to surfaces (opaque and translucent).

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:AerialPespectiveViewDistanceScale Default 1 Height Fog Contribution

Scale the sky and atmosphere lights contribution to the height fog when SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog project setting is true.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:HeightFogContribution Default 1 Transmittance Min Light Elevation Angle

The minimum elevation angle in degree that should be used to evaluate the sun transmittance to the ground. Useful to maintain a visible sun light and shadow on meshes even when the sun has started going below the horizon. This does not affect the aerial perspective.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:TransmittanceMinLightElevationAngle Default -90 Aerial Perspective Start Depth

The distance (kilometers) at which we start evaluating the aerial perspective. Having the aerial perspective starts away from the camera can help with performance: pixels not affected by the aerial perspective will have their computation skipped using early depth test.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:AerialPerspectiveStartDepth Default 0.1

items.title: Rendering
items.text:
Holdout

If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:bHoldout Default Off Render In Main Pass

If true, this component will be rendered in the main pass (basepass, transparency)

USD attribute unreal:skyAtmosphere:bRenderInMainPass Default On

items.title: hdUE Standard Render Vars
items.text:
ContextLOP nodeTypehdue::hduestandardrendervars::1.0

Creates the render vars (AOVs) hdUE renders.

Like Karma Standard Render Vars, it creates a render var prim per enabled output under the parent primitive path, for hdUE Render Products or hdUE Render Settings (Image Output > Import Upstream Render Vars) to write. The beauty is rendered as converged; the other AOVs are read from the GBuffer of the nearest opaque surface (path traced: albedo and normal from the Path Tracer), Cryptomatte from sub-pixel ID passes (see docs/output/aovs.md in the hdUE repository).

items.title: Parameters
items.text:
Parent Primitive Path

Path of the prim under which this node creates its render vars.

Parameter parentprimpath Default /Render/Products/Vars

items.title: Beauty
items.text:

Adds the render var C. The beauty: the rendered image with alpha (color4f, sourceName color).

Parameter aov_C Default On Precision

Parameter aov_C_format Default color4h Menu 16 Bit, 32 Bit

items.title: Cryptomatte
items.text:
Crypto Object

Adds the Cryptomatte layer CryptoObject of prim paths: the render vars CryptoObject00 to CryptoObject02 (float4, ranks 0 to 5), with coverage from 16 sub-pixel ID passes after the beauty converges. husk writes the layer's metadata and manifest into each image.

Parameter aov_CryptoObject Default Off Crypto Material

Adds the Cryptomatte layer CryptoMaterial of bound material paths: the render vars CryptoMaterial00 to CryptoMaterial02 (float4, ranks 0 to 5), with coverage from 16 sub-pixel ID passes after the beauty converges. husk writes the layer's metadata and manifest into each image.

Parameter aov_CryptoMaterial Default Off

items.title: hdUE Unreal Asset
items.text:
ContextLOP nodeTypehdue::hdueunrealasset::1.0

Places an asset from a UE project (a Niagara effect, a mesh, a Blueprint, a level) and imports it into hdUE.

Choose a UE project and one of its assets, then press Import: UE's editor cooks the asset in the background and adds it to the running hdUE runtime, without a restart. The prim is a small box hdUE renders the asset in place of (primvars:unreal:asset). A Niagara System is simulated to the frame rendered from Effect Start Frame. Needs UE's editor (editor_root in .local/paths.json), as hdUE's Substrate materials do.

items.title: Parameters
items.text:
UE Project

The UE project (.uproject) the asset comes from. It is not changed: its content is copied into hdUE's UE project to cook.

Parameter project Asset

The asset to place, as a cooked object path (/Game/Folder/NS_Fire.NS_Fire): the menu lists the project's levels and the assets named with UE's prefixes (SM_, SK_, BP_, SVT_, NS_).

Parameter asset Import

Cooks the asset and what it uses with UE's editor in the background, about a minute for one effect, and adds them to the running hdUE runtime: no restart. An asset the runtime already has needs none.

Parameter import Imported

On once the runtime has the asset (Import turns it on): the prim names the asset only then.

Parameter imported Default Off Primitive Path

The prim the asset renders on: a small box, which hdUE replaces with the asset.

Parameter primpath Default /assets/$OS Translate

Translate of the prim; the asset keeps UE's size (centimetres) in any stage unit.

Parameter t Default 0, 0, 0 Rotate

Rotate of the prim; the asset keeps UE's size (centimetres) in any stage unit.

Parameter r Default 0, 0, 0 Scale

Scale of the prim; the asset keeps UE's size (centimetres) in any stage unit.

Parameter s Default 1, 1, 1 Effect Start Frame

For a Niagara System: the frame it starts at. hdUE simulates it to the frame rendered, in steps of one frame, as Sequencer plays a Niagara track.

Parameter startframe Default 1

items.title: hdUE Volumetric Cloud
items.text:
ContextLOP nodeTypehdue::hduevolumetriccloud::1.0

Creates or edits a UE Volumetric Cloud layer, drawn with a Sky Atmosphere.

Like a Volumetric Cloud placed in a UE level, it creates or edits an UnrealVolumetricCloud prim with UE's properties; with no Material it uses UE's default cloud material. It needs a Sky Atmosphere (prim or render setting). A prim takes the place of hdUE Render Settings' Volumetric Cloud; UE draws one, the first prim by path.

items.title: Planet
items.text:
Planet Radius

The planet radius used when there is not SkyAtmosphere component present in the scene.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:PlanetRadius Default 6360 Ground Albedo

The ground albedo used to light the cloud from below with respect to the sun light and sky atmosphere. This is only used by the cloud material when the 'Volumetric Advanced' node have GroundContribution enabled.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:GroundAlbedo Default 0.401978, 0.401978, 0.401978

items.title: Art Direction
items.text:
Aerial Pespective Rayleigh Scattering Start Distance

Specify the aerial perspective start distance on cloud for Rayleigh scattering only. (kilometers)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveRayleighScatteringStartDistance Default 0 Aerial Pespective Rayleigh Scattering Fade Distance

Specify the distance over which the Rayleigh scattering will linearly ramp up to full effect. (kilometers)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveRayleighScatteringFadeDistance Default 0 Aerial Pespective Mie Scattering Start Distance

Specify the aerial perspective start distance on cloud for Mie scattering only. (kilometers)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveMieScatteringStartDistance Default 0 Aerial Pespective Mie Scattering Fade Distance

Specify the distance over which the Rayleigh scattering will linearly ramp up to full effect. (kilometers)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveMieScatteringFadeDistance Default 0

items.title: Rendering
items.text:
Holdout

If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:bHoldout Default Off Render In Main Pass

If true, this component will be rendered in the main pass (basepass, transparency)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:bRenderInMainPass Default On Visible In Real Time Sky Captures

If true, this component will be visible in real-time sky light reflection captures.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:bVisibleInRealTimeSkyCaptures Default On

items.title: Layer
items.text:
Layer Bottom Altitude

The altitude at which the cloud layer starts. (kilometers above the ground)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:LayerBottomAltitude Default 5 Layer Height

The height of the the cloud layer. (kilometers above the layer bottom altitude)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:LayerHeight Default 10 Tracing Start Max Distance

The maximum distance of the volumetric surface, i.e. cloud layer upper and lower bound, before which we will accept to start tracing. (kilometers)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:TracingStartMaxDistance Default 350 Tracing Start Distance From Camera

The distance from which the tracing will start. This is useful when the camera for instance is inside the layer of cloud. (kilometers)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:TracingStartDistanceFromCamera Default 0 Tracing Max Distance

The maximum distance that will be traced inside the cloud layer. (kilometers)

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:TracingMaxDistance Default 50

items.title: Cloud Material
items.text:
Material

The material describing the cloud volume. It must be a Volume domain material. Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:Material

items.title: Cloud Tracing
items.text:
Use Per Sample Atmospheric Light Transmittance

Whether to apply atmosphere transmittance per sample, instead of using the light global transmittance.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:bUsePerSampleAtmosphericLightTransmittance Default Off Sky Light Cloud Bottom Occlusion

Occlude the sky light contribution at the bottom of the cloud layer. This is a fast approximation to sky lighting being occluded by cloud without having to trace rays or sample AO texture. Ignored if the cloud material explicitely sets the ambient occlusion value.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:SkyLightCloudBottomOcclusion Default 0.5 View Sample Count Scale

Scale the tracing sample count in primary views. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.ViewRaySampleCountMax'.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:ViewSampleCountScale Default 1 Reflection View Sample Count Scale Value

Scale the tracing sample count in reflection views. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.ReflectionRaySampleMaxCount'.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:ReflectionViewSampleCountScaleValue Default 1 Shadow View Sample Count Scale

Scale the shadow tracing sample count in primary views, only used with Advanced Output ray marched shadows. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.Shadow.ViewRaySampleMaxCount'.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:ShadowViewSampleCountScale Default 1 Shadow Reflection View Sample Count Scale Value

Scale the shadow tracing sample count in reflection views, only used with Advanced Output ray marched shadows. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.Shadow.ReflectionRaySampleMaxCount'.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:ShadowReflectionViewSampleCountScaleValue Default 1 Shadow Tracing Distance

The shadow tracing distance in kilometers, only used with Advanced Output ray marched shadows.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:ShadowTracingDistance Default 15 Stop Tracing Transmittance Threshold

When the mean transmittance is below this threshold, we stop tracing. This is a good way to reduce the ray marched sample count, and thus to increase performance.

USD attribute unreal:volumetricCloud:StopTracingTransmittanceThreshold Default 0.005

items.title: Render settings reference
items.text: Every one of the 372 render settings, in the order the Unreal Engine tab of a Render Settings LOP shows them. Each is a unreal:* attribute on the UsdRenderSettings prim; the Houdini parameter name is the attribute's encoded form. Unreal's settings keep UE's names, tooltips, ranges and defaults, read from the engine source. See Render settings for how they reach UE.

items.title: Render Mode
items.text:
DefaultRealtime (Lumen)USD attributeunreal:renderModeHoudini parameterxn__unrealrenderMode_41a

Realtime renders with UE's deferred renderer, Lumen and MegaLights, and is meant for final frames too. Path Tracer accumulates UE's reference path tracer.

Value Label realtime Realtime (Lumen) pathtraced Path Tracer

items.title: Path Tracer Samples
items.text:
Default2048Range1 to 65536USD attributeunreal:samplesPerPixelHoudini parameterxn__unrealsamplesPerPixel_99aPath Tracer only

Samples per pixel. Divided between motion-blur sub-frames.

items.title: Warmup Frames
items.text:
Default64Range1 to 256USD attributeunreal:warmupFramesHoudini parameterxn__unrealwarmupFrames_e5aRealtime only

Realtime frames rendered before a frame counts as converged, so Lumen and temporal effects settle. In husk, only a sequence's first frame warms up: each later frame continues its history with one draw, as Movie Render Queue does.

items.title: Unreal Tonemapper
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:tonemapperHoudini parameterxn__unrealtonemapper_41a

Run UE's tonemapper, bloom, colour grading, vignette and grain. With the tone curve, the beauty becomes UE's tone-mapped image (display-linear): view it with an sRGB view that only encodes (Houdini's Un-tone-mapped), not Raw.

items.title: Disable Tone Curve
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:disableToneCurveHoudini parameterxn__unrealdisableToneCurve_wcb

Movie Render Queue's Disable Tone Curve: the Unreal Tonemapper still grades, blooms, vignettes and adds grain, without UE's film curve, so the beauty stays scene-linear for the OCIO view. Forced on, as UE forces it when OpenColorIO does the display, when the OCIO config's default view is a display transform of its own (ACES, AgX).

items.text:
Default0Range-15 to 15USD attributeunreal:postProcess:AutoExposureBiasHoudini parameterxn__unrealpostProcessAutoExposureBias_tubl

Logarithmic adjustment for the exposure. Only used if a tonemapper is specified. 0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ... hdUE adds the USD camera exposure to it.

items.title: Sky Light Capture In-Scattering Roughness
items.text:

This is the roughness at which the sky light capture cubemap will be sample to simulate scattering dispersion due to a phase function.

items.title: Inscattering Color Cubemap Angle
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 360USD attributeunreal:heightFog:InscatteringColorCubemapAngleHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogInscatteringColorCubemapAngle_qdcjRealtime only

Angle to rotate the InscatteringColorCubemap around the Z axis.

items.title: Inscattering Texture Tint
items.text:

Tint color used when InscatteringColorCubemap is specified, for quick edits without having to reimport InscatteringColorCubemap.

items.title: Fully Directional Inscattering Color Distance
items.text:

items.title: Non Directional Inscattering Color Distance

Distance at which only the average color of InscatteringColorCubemap should be used as Inscattering Color.

items.title: Directional Inscattering Exponent
items.text:
Default4Range2 to 64USD attributeunreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringExponentHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogDirectionalInscatteringExponent_zgcjRealtime only

Controls the size of the directional inscattering cone, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - there must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored and the volumetric fog Scattering Distribution is used instead.

items.title: Directional Inscattering Start Distance
items.text:
Default10000USD attributeunreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringStartDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogDirectionalInscatteringStartDistance_4ocjRealtime only

Controls the start distance from the viewer of the directional inscattering, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - There must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored.

items.title: Directional Inscattering Color
items.text:
Default0, 0, 0USD attributeunreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringLuminanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogDirectionalInscatteringLuminance_micjRealtime only

Controls the color of the directional inscattering, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - there must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored.

items.title: Volumetric Fog
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:heightFog:bEnableVolumetricFogHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogbEnableVolumetricFog_2xbj

Whether to enable Volumetric fog. Scalability settings control the resolution of the fog simulation. Note that Volumetric fog currently does not support StartDistance, FogMaxOpacity and FogCutoffDistance. Volumetric fog also can't match exponential height fog in general as exponential height fog has non-physical behavior.

items.title: Scattering Distribution
items.text:
Default0.2Range-0.9 to 0.9USD attributeunreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogScatteringDistributionHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogScatteringDistribution_incj

Controls the scattering phase function - how much incoming light scatters in various directions. A distribution value of 0 scatters equally in all directions, while .9 scatters predominantly in the light direction. In order to have visible volumetric fog light shafts from the side, the distribution will need to be closer to 0.

items.title: Albedo
items.text:
Default1, 1, 1USD attributeunreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogAlbedoHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogAlbedo_gwbj

The height fog particle reflectiveness used by volumetric fog. Water particles in air have an albedo near white, while dust has slightly darker value.

items.title: Emissive
items.text:
Default0, 0, 0USD attributeunreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogEmissiveHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogEmissive_pzbjRealtime only

Light emitted by height fog. This is a density so more light is emitted the further you are looking through the fog. In most cases skylight is a better choice, however right now volumetric fog does not support precomputed lighting, So stationary skylights are unshadowed and static skylights don't affect volumetric fog at all.

items.title: Extinction Scale
items.text:
Default1Range0.1 to 10USD attributeunreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogExtinctionScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogExtinctionScale_3bcj

Scales the height fog particle extinction amount used by volumetric fog. Values larger than 1 cause fog particles everywhere absorb more light.

items.title: View Distance
items.text:
Default6000Range1000 to 10000USD attributeunreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogDistance_pzbj

Distance over which volumetric fog should be computed, after the start distance. Larger values extend the effect into the distance but expose under-sampling artifacts in details.

items.title: Start Distance
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 5000USD attributeunreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogStartDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogStartDistance_u7bjRealtime only

Distance from the camera that the volumetric fog will start, in world units.

items.title: Near Fade In Distance
items.text:

Distance over which volumetric fog will fade in from the start distance.

items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:heightFog:bOverrideLightColorsWithFogInscatteringColorsHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogbOverrideLightColorsWithFogInscatteringColors_s3cjRealtime onlyAdvanced

Whether to use FogInscatteringColor for the Sky Light volumetric scattering color and DirectionalInscatteringColor for the Directional Light scattering color. Make sure your directional light has 'Atmosphere Sun Light' enabled! Enabling this allows Volumetric fog to better match Height fog in the distance, but produces non-physical volumetric lighting that may not match surface lighting.

items.title: Enable Fog Screen Space Scattering
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:heightFog:bEnableFSSSHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogbEnableFSSS_fjbjRealtime onlyAdvanced

Enable FSSS (Fog Screen Space Scattering) to approximate multiple scattering.

items.title: Scene Color Scattering Amount Scale
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:heightFog:FSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogFSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountScale_incjRealtime onlyAdvanced

The amount of scene color injected into the fog screen space scattering technique. When 0, only the fog luminance will be scattered. When 1, fog and scene luminance will be scattered. When above 1, more scene color can be injected to increase the brightness of the multiple scattering effect, even when the fog is not too intense. We cannot scatter more than the scene color however.

items.title: Scene Color Scattering Amount Power
items.text:
Default1Range0 to 2USD attributeunreal:heightFog:FSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountPowerHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogFSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountPower_incjRealtime onlyAdvanced

Apply a power over the amount of scattered scene luminance after it is evaluated using Scene Color Scattering Amount Scale. A value smaller than 1 can show more scattering where the fog is less intense.

items.title: Spread Scale
items.text:
Default0.1Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:heightFog:FSSSSpreadScaleHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogFSSSSpreadScale_xpbjRealtime onlyAdvanced

The scale of the spread for the fog multiple scattering. This basically scales mip level sampled from the blurred screen space FSSS texture. Increasing will make scene and thicker fog look fuzzier. But too high values can cause artifacts such as halos around depth discontinuities.

items.title: Blur Control
items.text:
Default0.5Range0 to 1USD attributeunreal:heightFog:FSSSBlurControlHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogFSSSBlurControl_xpbjRealtime onlyAdvanced

When generating the the blurred screen space FSSS texture, this controls how much of the blurred lower mip levels is injected back into the sharper higher mip levels. A higher value will result in a blurrier result. But when = 1, multiple scattering will be a single average color of the FSSS texture.

items.title: Holdout
items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:heightFog:bHoldoutHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogbHoldout_jebjAdvanced

If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

items.title: Render In Main Pass
items.text:
DefaultOnUSD attributeunreal:heightFog:bRenderInMainPassHoudini parameterxn__unrealheightFogbRenderInMainPass_6sbjAdvanced

If true, this component will be rendered in the main pass (basepass, transparency)

The Min/Max are expressed in pixel luminance (cd/m2) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings).

items.text:

items.text:
Default1Range0.25 to 4USD attributeunreal:postProcess:LumenSceneDetailHoudini parameterxn__unrealpostProcessLumenSceneDetail_tublRealtime only

items.text:

items.text:

items.text:

items.title: Max Trace Distance
items.text:
Default20000Range1 to 2097152USD attributeunreal:postProcess:LumenMaxTraceDistanceHoudini parameterxn__unrealpostProcessLumenMaxTraceDistance_y2blRealtime only

Controls the maximum distance that Lumen should trace while solving lighting. Values that are too small will cause lighting to leak into large caves, while values that are large will increase GPU cost.

items.text:

items.text:
Default1Range0.5 to 4USD attributeunreal:postProcess:LumenSceneLightingUpdateSpeedHoudini parameterxn__unrealpostProcessLumenSceneLightingUpdateSpeed_zgclRealtime onlyAdvanced

items.title: Final Gather Lighting Update Speed
items.text:

Best to keep below 2 as it also causes reflections to be brighter than the scene.

A value of zero makes the motion blur dependent on the actual frame rate.

items.title: Per Object Size
items.text:
Default0Range0 to 100USD attributeunreal:postProcess:MotionBlurPerObjectSizeHoudini parameterxn__unrealpostProcessMotionBlurPerObjectSize_75blRealtime only

items.title: MegaLights
items.text:
DefaultOnUSD attributeunreal:postProcess:bMegaLightsHoudini parameterxn__unrealpostProcessbMegaLights_omblRealtime only

Allows forcing MegaLights on or off for this volume, regardless of the project setting for MegaLights. MegaLights will stochastically sample lights, which allows many shadow casting lights to be rendered efficiently, with a consistent and low GPU cost. When MegaLights is enabled, other direct lighting algorithms like Deferred Shading will no longer be used, and other shadowing methods like Ray Traced Shadows, Distance Field Shadows and Shadow Maps will no longer be used. MegaLights requires Hardware Ray Tracing and Shader Model 6.

The default shadowing method for MegaLights, unless over-ridden on the light component. 0 - Ray Tracing. Preferred method, which guarantees fixed MegaLights cost and correct area shadows, but is dependent on the BVH representation quality. 1 - Virtual Shadow Maps. Has a significant per light cost, but can cast shadows directly from the Nanite geometry using rasterization. Console variable r.MegaLights.DefaultShadowMethod (process-wide).

Value Label 0 Ray Tracing 1 Virtual Shadow Maps

items.text:
DefaultOnUSD attributeunreal:substrateAutoPrepareHoudini parameterxn__unrealsubstrateAutoPrepare_fjbAdvanced

Substrate Builder materials missing from the Prepared Substrate Library, and MaterialX materials hdUE cannot translate at render time, are prepared in the background (UE's editor compiles or imports them, seconds per job) and render once ready: in Houdini's viewport as you edit, and in husk before the frame renders. Off, such a Substrate Builder material shows the library's message and fails a husk frame; such a MaterialX material renders with the inputs hdUE cannot translate at their constants.

items.text:
DefaultOffUSD attributeunreal:skyAtmosphereHoudini parameterxn__unrealskyAtmosphere_06a

Without a DomeLight, hdUE adds a Sky Light with Real Time Capture so the sky lights the scene, as UE needs for Lumen and its Path Tracer; a DomeLight's environment takes its place.

items.title: Colour management (OCIO, ACES)
items.text:
hdUE hands Houdini a scene-linear image in the colour space of your OpenColorIO config, as Karma does. Houdini's OCIO view then turns it into a picture for your monitor.

The same frame as a scene-linear beauty (Unreal Tonemapper off, the default) and as UE's tone-mapped image (on), both through an sRGB view.

items.title: How the image flows
items.text:
flowchart LR
    A("fal:fa-palette USD colours and textures<br/>(scene_linear, file colour spaces)") -->|OCIO| B("fal:fa-sun UE renders<br/>linear Rec.709")
    B -->|"Unreal Tonemapper off (default)"| C("fal:fa-image Beauty: scene-linear")
    B -->|"Tonemapper on, film curve on"| D("fal:fa-contrast Beauty: UE's tone-mapped image<br/>(display-linear)")
    B -->|"Tonemapper on, Disable Tone Curve"| C
    C -->|OCIO| E("fal:fa-monitor Houdini view / EXR<br/>in scene_linear")
    D -->|OCIO primaries only| E

    classDef host stroke-width:1px
    classDef hdue stroke-width:1px
    classDef unreal stroke-width:1px
    classDef output stroke-width:1px

    class A host
    class B unreal
    class C,D output
    class E host
  • Colours you author (Preview Surface diffuse and emissive colours, displayColor, light colours) are read as values in the config's scene_linear role.
  • UE renders in linear Rec.709.
  • The beauty comes back in the scene_linear role. With Houdini's default config that is linear Rec.709, so nothing is converted. With an ACES config whose scene_linear is ACEScg, the beauty is ACEScg.

hdUE uses the config Houdini uses ($OCIO). usdview and other hosts without OCIO get linear Rec.709.

Unreal Engine departs here on purpose

UE's editor shows a display-ready image: tonemapper, auto exposure, bloom, vignette and grain on. hdUE keeps the Unreal Tonemapper off by default, so Houdini receives scene-linear values and applies its own OCIO view. Turn it on to get UE's look; see Post-processing.

items.title: Viewing the beauty in Houdini
items.text:
Unreal Tonemapper Config's default view What the beauty holds View it with Off (default) any Scene-linear radiance Any view: Un-tone-mapped, ACES, AgX On Un-tone-mapped (Houdini's default) UE's tone-mapped image, display-linear Rec.709 Un-tone-mapped (an sRGB encode). Not Raw: Raw shows it too dark On An ACES or AgX view Scene-linear, graded: hdUE turns UE's film curve off The ACES or AgX view

With the tonemapper on and an ACES or AgX default view, hdUE does what UE does when OpenColorIO handles the display: it turns UE's film curve off and keeps the rest of the tonemapper. Grading, bloom, vignette and grain still apply. Without this, the image would be tone-mapped twice.

hdUE reads the config's default view only. Switching the viewport to another view does not change what hdUE renders.

items.title: Disable Tone Curve
items.text:
Disable Tone Curve (unreal:disableToneCurve) · Default Off · reference

Movie Render Queue's Disable Tone Curve. The Unreal Tonemapper still grades, blooms, vignettes and adds grain, but skips UE's film curve, so the beauty stays scene-linear for your OCIO view. It has no effect while the Unreal Tonemapper is off. hdUE forces it on when the config's default view is an ACES or AgX display transform.

Unreal Tonemapper on, Disable Tone Curve off and on, through an sRGB view.

items.title: Unreal Tonemapper
items.text:
Unreal Tonemapper (unreal:tonemapper) · Default Off · reference

Runs UE's tonemapper and every effect inside it. See Post-processing.

items.title: Texture colour spaces
items.text:
hdUE converts colour textures (base colour, emissive, specular colour) to linear Rec.709 for UE, from the colour space you author. Data textures (roughness, normal, ...) are never converted.

Authored colour space 8-bit image (PNG, JPG, TIF) Float image (EXR, HDR) sRGB, srgb_texture UE decodes sRGB itself UE decodes sRGB itself raw, data Used as is Used as is lin_rec709 (linear Rec.709) Used as is Used as is Another linear space (acescg, ...) Converted through OCIO to a half-float copy Converted through OCIO None, or auto sRGB for colour inputs, linear for data inputs Read as scene_linear, converted if needed

Where the colour space comes from, first match wins:

  1. UsdUVTexture Source Color Space (inputs:sourceColorSpace: raw, sRGB, auto).
  2. The file's colorSpace metadata, or MaterialX colorspace on an image node (srgb_texture, lin_rec709, acescg, ...).

Names are resolved through your OCIO config. A name the config does not know is used as is, with one warning.

Converted copies are cached in your temp folder (%TEMP%/hdue_ocio), keyed by file, file time and colour space. Entries unused for a week are deleted.

items.title: How to match UE's editor look
items.text:
Use Houdini's default OCIO config (default view Un-tone-mapped).

  1. On hdUE Render Settings, turn on Unreal Tonemapper.
  2. Set Lens > Exposure > Metering Mode to Auto Exposure Histogram.
  3. Set Exposure Compensation to 1 (UE's project default, r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure.Bias).
  4. Keep the viewport and image viewer on Un-tone-mapped.

Bloom (0.675) and vignette (0.4) are already at UE's defaults once the tonemapper is on. See Post-processing for the exposure caveats.

items.title: How to deliver ACEScg EXRs for comp
items.text:
1. Point OCIO at a config whose scene_linear role is ACEScg before you start Houdini. Houdini 22 ships one: $HFS/packages/ocio/cg-config-v3.0.0_aces-v2.0_ocio-v2.5.ocio.
  2. Leave Unreal Tonemapper off. The beauty and the lighting AOVs are then scene-linear ACEScg radiance.
  3. Tag your textures: srgb_texture for 8-bit colour maps, acescg for ACEScg EXRs, raw for data.
  4. Write 16-bit half or 32-bit float EXRs (hdUE Standard Render Vars Precision).

If you need UE's grade baked in, turn on Unreal Tonemapper and Disable Tone Curve: the EXR stays scene-linear ACEScg, with grading, bloom and vignette applied.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Cause Fix Tonemapper on, image too dark and contrasty Viewed with Raw Use the Un-tone-mapped view. Tonemapper on, highlights look flat and twice compressed The film curve and an ACES view both applied: you switched the viewport to ACES, but the config's default view is Un-tone-mapped Turn on Disable Tone Curve, or make ACES the config's default view. Textures look washed out or too dark Wrong colour space on the texture Set sourceColorSpace or MaterialX colorspace: srgb_texture for 8-bit colour, raw for data. Warning "the OCIO config has no colour space ..." The texture's colour space name is not in your config Use a colour space name from the config file. The texture is used as is. Viewport shadows black, husk EXR shows detail Houdini 22.0.368's viewport OCIO display shows linear values below about 0.004 as black Judge dark images in the EXR, or turn the viewport's OCIO off to check. Need UE's raw linear Rec.709 output You want no conversion at all Set HDUE_COLOR_MANAGEMENT=0 before starting Houdini.

items.title: Unreal Engine and Karma
items.text:
• UE renders in linear Rec.709; its working colour space is a project setting baked into cooked shaders. UsdRenderSettings renderingColorSpace is therefore not applied: hdUE warns.
  • Disable Tone Curve is the same switch Movie Render Queue's Color Output turns on when OCIO handles the display.
  • Karma ignores colorSpace metadata on a UsdUVTexture file; hdUE converts by it. An ACEScg EXR on a MaterialX image renders at 1.03 times Karma's brightness.
  • With the tonemapper off, hdUE's beauty is scene-linear like Karma's. With it on, the beauty is UE's look, which Karma does not reproduce.

items.title: Debug views
items.text:
A debug view replaces the lit image with one of the view modes of UE's viewport View Mode menu: lighting only, a GBuffer channel, Lumen's scene, shadow map pages. Use them to find out why an image looks the way it does.

The Bistro in UE's lighting view modes.

items.title: Using it in Solaris
items.text:
1. Set Render Mode to Realtime: debug views apply to the Realtime beauty only.
  2. In the viewport's Display Options > Unreal Engine tab, or on your Render Settings LOP (Rendering > View Mode, Advanced), set Debug View.
  3. Set it back to Lit when you are done. A debug view set on a Render Settings LOP renders in husk too.

Debug View (unreal:debugView), default Lit (off). Realtime only, Advanced.

AOVs and Path Tracer renders are unchanged by a debug view.

items.title: Lighting views
items.text:
Value Label Shows Use it to off Lit the final lit image unlit Unlit base colour and emission, no lighting check textures and material assignments lightingOnly Lighting Only lighting on a neutral grey surface judge light placement and bounce light without textures detailLighting Detail Lighting lighting with the materials' normal maps check normal maps reflections Reflections reflections on smooth chrome-like surfaces find what each surface reflects, and missing reflections lightComplexity Light Complexity how many lights reach each pixel, cool to hot find areas where many overlapping lights cost time

These views, and the Lumen, shadow and Nanite views below, are display images drawn through UE's tonemapper, as in UE's viewport; the lighting views take the camera exposure first. To see them as UE shows them, set the Houdini viewer's colour correction to Raw.

items.title: Buffer views
items.text:
A buffer view shows one channel of UE's GBuffer, the per-pixel material data the lighting reads.

Value Shows buffer:BaseColor base colour buffer:Metallic metallic buffer:Roughness roughness buffer:Specular specular buffer:WorldNormal world-space normal buffer:SceneDepth distance from the camera buffer:ShadingModel UE's shading model, one colour per model

Buffer views are linear data, like AOVs. Use them to check that a USD or MaterialX input reaches UE with the value you authored, for example a roughness texture.

items.title: Lumen, shadow and Nanite views
items.text:
Value Shows Use it to lumen:Overview Lumen's scene, surface cache and geometry side by side a first look at what Lumen sees lumen:LumenScene the simplified scene Lumen traces against find objects missing from Lumen's bounce light lumen:SurfaceCache Lumen's surface cache; pink areas have no coverage find surfaces that bounce no light lumen:GeometryNormals the normals of Lumen's scene check Lumen's geometry against the real one lumen:ReflectionView the scene Lumen reflections trace against debug wrong or missing reflections vsm:mip, vsm:vpage, vsm:cache Virtual Shadow Map mip levels, virtual pages and cached pages find blurry or flickering shadows; needs Virtual Shadow Maps on nanite:Mask, nanite:Triangles, nanite:Clusters, nanite:Primitives, nanite:Instances, nanite:Overdraw Nanite's rendering data check Nanite triangle density and coverage

Nanite views show only Nanite meshes: the meshes Houdini's viewport converts to Nanite, and native Nanite assets. In husk, meshes from the stage are not Nanite, so these views show nothing for them. See Nanite.

items.title: Not available
items.text:
hdUE runs a cooked UE runtime, not the editor, so some editor view modes are missing:

  • Wireframe: UE draws it in an editor-only pass.
  • Shader Complexity, Quad Overdraw, LOD Coloration and the other material debug modes: their shaders are not cooked.
  • Lightmap modes: hdUE has no static lighting.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Cause Fix The debug view does not change the image Render Mode is Path Tracer Switch to Realtime. A Nanite view is black or empty no Nanite meshes in view (husk, or meshes not converted) Use it in Houdini's viewport, or on native Nanite assets. A virtual shadow map view is empty Virtual Shadow Maps are off Turn Virtual Shadow Maps on (Lighting > Shadows). A final husk render shows a debug view Debug View left set on the render settings Set it to Lit.

items.title: Unreal Engine and Karma
items.text: The values are UE's view modes and visualization names, as UE's r.*.Visualize console variables take them. To write material data to files instead, render AOVs, as you would with Karma.

items.title: Denoising
items.text:
The denoiser removes the noise left in a Path Tracer image after its last sample. hdUE runs UE's own denoiser plugins, as UE's Path Tracer does: NNE Denoiser by default, or NVIDIA OptiX.

The Cornell box at 16 samples per pixel, without a denoiser and with each plugin.

items.title: Using it in Solaris
items.text:
The denoiser settings are on the Unreal Engine tab of your Render Settings LOP, under Rendering > Path Tracing. They show when Render Mode is Path Tracer.

  1. Leave Denoiser on (the default).
  2. Pick a Denoiser Plugin: NNE Denoiser (the default) or NVIDIA OptiX.
  3. Set Path Tracer Samples high enough that the denoiser keeps your detail (see Samples and the denoiser).

The denoiser only touches the Path Tracer's beauty. Realtime renders have no Path Tracer noise and are unchanged.

items.title: Denoiser
items.text:
Denoiser (unreal:postProcess:PathTracingEnableDenoiser), default on. Path Tracer only.

Runs the selected denoiser plugin on the last sample. It reads the Path Tracer's albedo and normal as well as its colour, so edges and textures stay sharp.

On the glossy Cornell box at 1920 x 1080 and 32 samples, NNE Denoiser cut the noise 20 times, with the mean brightness unchanged (0.0291 before, 0.0290 after).

items.title: Denoiser Plugin
items.text:
Denoiser Plugin (unreal:cvar:r:PathTracing:Denoiser:Name), default NNE Denoiser. Path Tracer only.

Value Plugin Runs on Notes NNEDenoiser UE's NNE Denoiser: Intel Open Image Denoise 2.3 networks any D3D12 GPU, through DirectML UE's default OptiX UE's OptiX Denoise plugin (experimental in UE) NVIDIA GPUs, through CUDA

On the same Cornell frame, OptiX left a little less noise than NNE Denoiser (0.00009 against 0.00015, mean absolute Laplacian), with the same brightness.

items.title: NNE Denoiser Model
items.text:
NNE Denoiser Model (unreal:cvar:NNEDenoiser:Asset), default Project Default (Balanced, Alpha). Path Tracer only, Advanced.

The Open Image Denoise network NNE Denoiser runs: Fast, Balanced or High Quality, each with or without the alpha channel. In Open Image Denoise, High Quality keeps the most detail and Fast takes the least time. The Alpha models also denoise the alpha channel.

The Cornell box at 4 samples per pixel, where the models differ most.

items.title: NNE Denoiser Runtime
items.text:
NNE Denoiser Runtime (unreal:cvar:NNEDenoiser:Runtime:Type), default RDG. Path Tracer only, Advanced.

Where NNE Denoiser runs its network: RDG (ONNX Runtime on DirectML inside UE's render graph), GPU or CPU.

items.title: OptiX Tile Width and Tile Height
items.text:
OptiX Tile Width (unreal:cvar:r:OptixDenoise:TileWidth) and OptiX Tile Height (unreal:cvar:r:OptixDenoise:TileHeight), default 0. Path Tracer only, Advanced.

The tile size OptiX denoises in, in pixels; 0 denoises the whole image at once. Leave them at 0: UE's default of 256 fails in UE 5.8.4's OptiX library and leaves a garbled strip in the image.

items.title: Samples and the denoiser
items.text: The denoiser cannot recover detail the samples never reached. Check the denoised image at the sample count you render with.

items.title: When to turn it off
items.text:
• You denoise in compositing. AOVs are never denoised, so a denoised beauty no longer matches its AOVs. Turn Denoiser off and denoise all layers together.
  • You are judging the sample count. Compare noise with the denoiser off.
  • You render many converged samples. At thousands of samples there is little noise to remove.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Cause Fix The viewport stays noisy while the Path Tracer accumulates the denoiser runs only on the last sample Wait for the last sample, or lower Path Tracer Samples while you work. Fine texture or contact shadows look smeared too few samples for the denoiser Raise Path Tracer Samples, or pick the High Quality model. AOVs are noisy but the beauty is clean AOVs are not denoised Expected. Turn the denoiser off and denoise in compositing to keep them matched. A garbled strip across an OptiX image OptiX Tile Width or Height set to a non-zero value Set both to 0. A Realtime image is noisy the denoiser is for the Path Tracer only Raise Warmup Frames; see Render settings.

items.title: Unreal Engine and Karma
items.text: hdUE follows UE: the denoiser is on by default, and NNE Denoiser is UE's default plugin. Karma's denoiser settings do not affect hdUE.

items.title: Engine quality
items.text: Engine quality settings trade render time for quality in UE's realtime renderer: UE's scalability levels, Nanite's triangle density, ray tracing and the render resolution. They are UE's console variables, set from the Engine Quality and Rendering tabs of your Render Settings LOP.

items.title: Using it in Solaris
items.text:
1. On your Render Settings LOP's Unreal Engine tab, open Engine Quality.
  2. Set a Scalability group, or a Nanite or ray tracing setting.
  3. For the viewport only, use Display Options > Unreal Engine > Engine Quality, which offers the main scalability groups.

Each setting is a unreal:cvar:<console variable> attribute, with : in place of .: Shadows is unreal:cvar:sg:ShadowQuality, UE's sg.ShadowQuality. Console variables apply to the whole Houdini or husk process, not to one viewport. Remove the attribute to restore the value UE had before.

Any UE console variable works as an attribute, not only the ones the LOP shows: int unreal:cvar:r:Shadow:Virtual:Enable = 0. Booleans are written as 1 and 0. Variables UE marks read-only, such as r.RayTracing, cannot change while UE runs; hdUE skips them with a warning.

items.title: Scalability
items.text:
UE's scalability groups, as in UE's Engine Scalability Settings menu. Each level (Low, Medium, High, Epic, Cinematic) applies a set of console variables from UE's BaseScalability.ini; a console variable you set yourself wins over its group.

Group Attribute What the levels change View Distance unreal:cvar:sg:ViewDistanceQuality how far objects and details are drawn Anti-Aliasing unreal:cvar:sg:AntiAliasingQuality the anti-aliasing pass's quality Shadows unreal:cvar:sg:ShadowQuality shadow resolution and soft shadow rays: Low has no soft shadow rays, Epic 8 rays per pixel Global Illumination unreal:cvar:sg:GlobalIlluminationQuality Lumen's bounce light: off at Low; Epic and Cinematic add mesh distance field tracing and allow hit lighting Reflections unreal:cvar:sg:ReflectionQuality Lumen reflections: off at Low and Medium, half resolution at High, full resolution at Epic and Cinematic Post-Processing unreal:cvar:sg:PostProcessQuality bloom, depth of field and other post-process quality Textures unreal:cvar:sg:TextureQuality texture streaming and filtering Effects unreal:cvar:sg:EffectsQuality translucency and effect quality Foliage unreal:cvar:sg:FoliageQuality foliage density Shading unreal:cvar:sg:ShadingQuality material shading quality

The default is Epic in Houdini's viewport and Cinematic in husk and the USD Render ROP, as Movie Render Queue renders with Cinematic. The Path Tracer ignores the Anti-Aliasing, Shadows, Global Illumination and Reflections groups.

Global Illumination in the Bistro, lit by its lamps. Low turns Lumen's bounce light off.

items.title: Nanite
items.text:
Nanite (unreal:cvar:r:Nanite), default on, Advanced.

Renders Nanite meshes with Nanite. Off, they render with their fallback meshes. See Nanite for which meshes are Nanite.

Max Pixels per Edge (unreal:cvar:r:Nanite:MaxPixelsPerEdge), default 1, range 0.25 to 8. Realtime only, Advanced.

The triangle edge length Nanite aims for on screen, in pixels. Lower values draw more, smaller triangles and take more time.

items.title: Ray tracing
items.text:
Ray Tracing (unreal:cvar:r:RayTracing:Enable), default on, Advanced.

UE's hardware ray tracing, which the Path Tracer, Lumen's hardware ray tracing, ray traced shadows and ray traced translucency need.

Nanite Ray Tracing (unreal:cvar:r:RayTracing:Nanite:Mode), default Fallback Mesh, Advanced.

What rays hit on Nanite meshes. Fallback Mesh, UE's default, traces each mesh's simplified fallback: foliage simplified into its fallback looks thinner in the Path Tracer and in Lumen's reflections. Streamed Out Mesh traces the full Nanite geometry streamed in for the view. On Intel Sponza's tree, a 256-sample husk frame took 65 s with Streamed Out Mesh against 25 s with Fallback Mesh, both including scene load.

Other ray tracing settings are on the Lighting and Rendering Features tabs:

Setting Attribute Default What it does Hardware Ray Tracing unreal:cvar:r:Lumen:HardwareRayTracing on Lumen traces triangles instead of distance fields Ray Traced Shadows unreal:cvar:r:RayTracing:Shadows off ray traced shadows instead of shadow maps Translucency Method unreal:postProcess:TranslucencyType Raster Ray Traced traces every layer of glass

Tip

Glass seen through other glass is lit from Lumen's approximate radiance cache with Raster translucency, and can come out far too bright. In a dome-lit room, a bottle was 18 times the Path Tracer's brightness with Raster and within 2 times with unreal:postProcess:TranslucencyType = "ETranslucencyType::RayTraced".

items.title: Resolution and anti-aliasing
items.text:
These settings are on the Rendering tab, under Anti-Aliasing. They apply to Realtime renders.

Setting Attribute Default What it does Anti-Aliasing Method unreal:cvar:r:AntiAliasingMethod TSR None, FXAA, TAA or TSR Screen Percentage unreal:cvar:r:ScreenPercentage 100 render resolution in percent of the output, upscaled by the anti-aliasing method; 50 renders a quarter of the pixels Lower Resolution While Moving unreal:cvar:r:HdUE:InteractiveResolution on Houdini's viewport renders at Moving Screen Percentage (50) while the view changes NVIDIA DLSS unreal:cvar:r:NGX:DLSS:Enable off DLSS Super Resolution replaces TAA or TSR

With NVIDIA DLSS on, Screen Percentage picks the DLSS mode: 50 is Performance, about 67 Quality, 100 DLAA. DLSS needs an NVIDIA RTX GPU and an hdUE build with NVIDIA's DLSS plugin; otherwise the anti-aliasing method renders. DLSS Ray Reconstruction (unreal:cvar:r:HdUE:DLSS:RayReconstruction, off) makes DLSS denoise Lumen reflections and ray traced shadows too, in place of UE's denoisers; it needs DLSS on. The Path Tracer does not use DLSS.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Cause Fix No bounce light in Realtime Global Illumination at Low Set it to Epic or Cinematic. No reflections of other objects Reflections at Low or Medium Set it to High or above. Hard shadows from area lights Shadows at Low Set it to Medium or above. Viewport and husk renders differ the viewport defaults to Epic, husk to Cinematic Author the scalability groups you want on the Render Settings LOP. Thin foliage in the Path Tracer rays hit Nanite fallback meshes Set Nanite Ray Tracing to Streamed Out Mesh. Glass behind glass is too bright Raster translucency Set Translucency Method to Ray Traced. A console variable attribute has no effect, with a warning UE marks it read-only None at render time: read-only variables cannot change while UE runs.

items.title: Unreal Engine and Karma
items.text: Every setting here is UE's own console variable with UE's default, and husk renders with Movie Render Queue's offline levels. Karma has no equivalent of scalability; its quality comes from sample counts.

items.title: Motion blur
items.text:
Motion blur smears what moves while the camera's shutter is open. hdUE renders it by averaging sub-frames spread over the shutter, as Movie Render Queue's temporal sampling does, in both render modes.

A ball crossing the Cornell box during a half-frame shutter, Realtime.

items.title: Using it in Solaris
items.text:
Motion blur needs three things:

  1. An open shutter. On your Camera LOP, set the shutter so that shutter:open is before shutter:close, in frames relative to the rendered frame. -0.25 and 0.25 is a half-frame shutter centred on the frame.
  2. Something that moves within the shutter (see What moves).
  3. Motion Blur on in the render settings (the default).

items.title: What moves
items.text:
Motion From Object transforms transform time samples on meshes, curves, points and their parent prims Deformation time-sampled mesh points with a constant point count; otherwise per-point velocities (Houdini's v) Points per-point velocities Instances PointInstancer transform samples; per-instance velocities, accelerations and angularVelocities; otherwise time-sampled positions, orientations, scales or instance matrices Camera camera transform time samples
  • velocities are in scene units per second. hdUE converts them to frames with the frame rate Houdini passes; without one, with unreal:framesPerSecond (default 24).
  • motion:blurScale on a prim scales its motion: 0.5 halves its blur, 0 removes it.
  • Transforms are interpolated linearly between time samples. A fast rotation within one frame blurs along a slightly shorter arc.
  • Time-sampled instance placements blur along one straight segment through the shutter, and animated instance scales do not blur. Author velocities and angularVelocities for curved instance paths.

items.title: Motion Blur
items.text:
Motion Blur (unreal:motionBlur), default on.

Averages sub-frames over the camera shutter when something moves. Off, each frame renders at the frame's time. A render settings prim's disableMotionBlur (or the deprecated instantaneousShutter) turns it off too.

items.title: Motion Samples
items.text:
Motion Samples (unreal:motionSamples), default 16, range 1 to 64.

Sub-frames per frame. The Path Tracer's samples and Realtime's warmup frames are divided between the sub-frames, so a frame with motion blur takes about the same time as one without. Too few sub-frames show separate copies of fast objects.

Path Tracer, 512 samples per pixel in total.

Note

A deforming mesh is uploaded again for each sub-frame. On dense meshes this adds time per sub-frame; lower Motion Samples if a deforming frame is slow.

items.title: Shutter length
items.text: The shutter interval sets the length of the blur: a 1-frame shutter blurs twice as far as a half-frame shutter. Set it on the camera, not in the render settings.

items.title: Realtime and Path Tracer
items.text: Both modes average the same sub-frames. In Realtime, UE's post-process motion blur also smears each sub-frame over its share of the shutter, which fills the gaps between sub-frames. Its strength is the shutter interval in frames (UE's shutter fraction, as Movie Render Queue reads it), divided by the motion samples, unless you author Amount (unreal:postProcess:MotionBlurAmount). The other Realtime motion blur settings are in Rendering Features > Motion Blur.

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
Film-style blur, 180-degree shutter: camera shutter:open -0.25, shutter:close 0.25; Motion Samples 16.

Fast spinning objects, Path Tracer: Motion Samples 32 and Path Tracer Samples 1024, so each sub-frame keeps 32 samples.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Cause Fix No blur at all the shutter is closed: shutter:open equals shutter:close (USD's fallback is 0 and 0) Set the camera's shutter, for example -0.25 and 0.25. No blur at all Motion Blur off, or disableMotionBlur on the render settings prim Turn Motion Blur on and remove disableMotionBlur. No blur on a simulation its points have a changing point count and no velocities Export v from the simulation as velocities. Fast objects show separate copies too few motion samples Raise Motion Samples. Instances blur in straight lines time-sampled positions blur as one segment Author velocities and angularVelocities. Path Tracer blur is noisy the samples are split between sub-frames Raise Path Tracer Samples.

items.title: Unreal Engine and Karma
items.text: Averaging sub-frames is how Movie Render Queue renders motion blur with temporal samples. Karma reads the same USD camera shutter, so a scene blurs over the same interval in both.

items.title: Post-processing
items.text:
UE's post-processing turns the rendered light into a finished picture: exposure, tone curve, bloom, lens effects, vignette, grain and colour grading. In hdUE it is off by default, so Houdini gets a scene-linear beauty. Turn on Unreal Tonemapper to get UE's look.

Unreal Tonemapper off (default) and on.

items.title: Using it in Solaris
items.text:
HoudiniUSD
  1. Add hdUE Render Settings (TAB menu > hdUE > Rendering), or select the one in your scene.
  2. Turn on Unreal Tonemapper at the top of the parameters.
  3. Set the effects on the Lens and Color Grading tabs. Their parameters are greyed out while the tonemapper is off, and hidden in Essential mode.
  4. View the result with Houdini's default Un-tone-mapped view, not Raw. See Colour management.

On a plain Render Settings LOP or in a USD file, author unreal:postProcess:<Property> on the render settings prim:

bool unreal:tonemapper = 1
float unreal:postProcess:BloomIntensity = 2
float4 unreal:postProcess:ColorSaturation = (1, 1, 1, 0.8)

Every parameter is UE's own Post Process Settings property, with UE's name, range and default. The render settings reference lists all of them.

Post-processing applies to the beauty only. AOVs stay unprocessed. Changing a post-process setting restarts Path Tracer accumulation.

What works with the tonemapper off

Depth of field, motion blur and post-process materials set to Before Tonemapping work with the tonemapper off. Everything else on this page needs it on.

items.title: Unreal Tonemapper
items.text:
Unreal Tonemapper (unreal:tonemapper) · Default Off · reference

Runs UE's tonemapper pass, which holds bloom, colour grading, the film curve, vignette, grain, chromatic aberration and lens flares. The beauty becomes UE's tone-mapped image: middle grey (0.18) stays 0.18, 1.0 becomes 0.72, 4.0 becomes 0.94, and 0.03 drops to 0.011. Dark scenes therefore look darker than without it; raise Exposure Compensation.

items.title: Disable Tone Curve
items.text:
Disable Tone Curve (unreal:disableToneCurve) · Default Off · reference

Keeps the tonemapper's grading, bloom, vignette and grain, without the film curve: the beauty stays scene-linear for an ACES or AgX view. See Colour management.

items.title: Exposure Compensation
items.text:
Exposure Compensation (unreal:postProcess:AutoExposureBias) · Default 0 · Range -15 to 15 · reference

Exposure in stops: +1 doubles the image, -1 halves it. The USD camera's Exposure adds to it. Only used with the tonemapper on.

items.title: Metering Mode
items.text:
Metering Mode (unreal:postProcess:AutoExposureMethod) · Default Manual · reference

Manual keeps exposure fixed, so every frame is exposed the same. Auto Exposure Histogram or Auto Exposure Basic turn on UE's eye adaptation, between Min Brightness (0.03) and Max Brightness (8).

Manual (default) and Auto Exposure Histogram.

Auto exposure in sequences

Auto exposure is measured per frame. Two identical Sponza renders differed by about 7%, and each frame of a sequence is exposed on its own. Use Manual for final sequences.

In husk and in Path Tracer mode, auto exposure reaches its target on every frame. In the realtime viewport it does too, unless you set Speed Up or Speed Down: then the viewport adapts gradually, as in UE.

UE's physical camera exposure (ISO, shutter speed, aperture) stays off unless you turn on Apply Physical Camera Exposure.

items.title: Bloom
items.text:
